factors.trading_idea: The child treats broad-fear capitulation as a state variable that makes prior selling less informative, but only trades it when a fresh positive earnings surprise remains unincorporated by stale consensus and the report-day price response is still below the fundamental implication. It then requires the announcement to reignite a pre-existing positive return-volume execution cascade, identifying constrained investors beginning a delayed re-risking process rather than a mechanical panic bounce. The interaction carries edge because capitulation alone mixes genuine deterioration with forced selling, while stale-surprise drift alone does not distinguish a quietly underreacted report from one backed by persistent institutional demand.
factors.name: Fear-State Stale Surprise Diffusion

factors.trading_idea: Negative price shocks can become self-exciting when prior down moves have repeatedly induced further selling, particularly when a new decline occurs with unusually poor dollar-volume support. This is a daily-bar proxy for asymmetric downward order-flow excitation: stressed holders and volatility-targeting participants continue selling into thin liquidity, while natural arbitrage capital is reluctant to absorb inventory during a developing cascade. The signal should be short high-excitation names and long names with weak or symmetric downside excitation; it is falsified if conditional post-shock returns are not more negative following high estimated downside branching intensity.
factors.name: Downside Excitation Under Volume Drought

factors.trading_idea: A negative earnings surprise alone mixes genuine information with oversold, already-absorbed liquidation, which explains why Parent A's unconditional cascade direction was unstable. This child only activates when the surprise-driven downside cascade is expressed through repeated closes near the low of unusually wide, low-turnover bars: a thin-book auction state indicating that sell demand remains unexecuted rather than fully incorporated into price. The interaction has edge because Parent B's endpoint state becomes informative when anchored to a fresh fundamental catalyst, while Parent A's bad-news cascade becomes a continuation signal only when liquidity withdrawal prevents immediate price discovery.
factors.name: Bad-News Thin-Book Persistence

factors.trading_idea: A fresh earnings surprise accompanied by unusually high turnover but an abnormally small same-day price displacement represents a disagreement auction: informed investors trade against liquidity suppliers and slower discretionary investors without immediately moving the daily midpoint. The direction of the reported surprise should subsequently dominate as the temporary opposing inventory is unwound and investors who require time to interpret the report update positions. This is falsified if high-impedance surprise events do not deliver stronger six-day returns in the direction of the surprise than equally sized surprise events with immediate price displacement; the edge can persist because this conditional state is infrequent and cannot be identified from the surprise or volume alone.
factors.name: Earnings Turnover-Impedance Resolution

factors.trading_idea: Renewed volume-tail flow is informative at six days only when the range-shock state identifies whether the order flow is an orderly execution program or a destabilizing liquidation. Under-impacted buy renewal after downside-range shocks rapidly relax identifies replenished liquidity and a recoverable demand program, whereas under-impacted sell renewal during persistent downside-range shocks identifies ongoing volatility-targeting deleveraging. Neither parent alone separates directional execution from the asymmetric liquidity regime that determines whether the same signed flow continues or is merely a completed forced-sale episode.
factors.name: Asymmetric Range-Relaxation Flow Completion (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: Investors extrapolate favorable revenue-consensus revisions most aggressively when the stock has already outperformed its industry, treating the price move and analyst optimism as mutually confirming information. A newly disclosed rise in receivables intensity contradicts that narrative because reported sales may be increasingly dependent on slow collections; the combination should predict a relative correction over the following six sessions. The edge persists because collections quality is quarterly, heterogeneous across firms, and less salient than price and consensus changes; it is falsified if fresh receivables deterioration does not add negative predictive power conditional on prior relative performance and estimate revisions.
factors.name: Revision Extrapolation Collection Break

factors.trading_idea: The child treats surprise novelty as a processing-regime variable rather than a continuation multiplier: extremely rare earnings ruptures are rapidly attention-grabbing and can reverse by day six, whereas statistically unusual but non-extreme coherent reports remain costly for investors to fully assimilate. It trades the signed analyst-revision/price-response gap only when the report lies in this moderate-novelty regime and is supported by internally funded cash generation. This interaction carries edge neither parent has alone because Parent A cannot distinguish gradual-assimilation events from rupture-driven reversals, while Parent B incorrectly extrapolates the most extreme rupture regime to the six-bar horizon.
factors.name: Moderate-Rupture Cash Revision Assimilation

factors.trading_idea: Analyst consensus revisions contain gradually disseminated fundamental information, but the six-bar drift should be strongest when the stock's sector-relative price response has lagged the revision rather than already incorporating it. The child therefore buys positive estimate revisions with weak relative price acknowledgement and shorts negative revisions whose prices remain unusually resilient. The hypothesis is falsifiable: conditional on a recent revision, forward returns should increase monotonically with the gap between revision direction and contemporaneous sector-relative return; the edge can persist because revisions arrive discretely across analysts and institutional investors face staggered mandate, research, and trading constraints.
factors.name: Unassimilated Consensus Revision Gap

factors.trading_idea: Downside volatility is not simply a symmetric risk estimate: an extreme negative-range innovation can either reveal a persistent crisis state or a transient liquidity overshoot. When downside range variance is far above its causally estimated nonlinear relaxation level but the bar closes near its high, the path indicates that selling pressure was absorbed rather than accepted at lower prices. Such episodes should subsequently mean-revert upward as volatility-control and forced-sale flow dissipate; the hypothesis is rejected if these recovery-shaped variance shocks continue to produce materially negative six-day returns.
factors.name: Asymmetric Volatility Relaxation Gap

factors.trading_idea: A one-sided sequence of large, high-volume daily moves is treated as a proxy for self-exciting metaorder activity rather than independent news. When this excitation remains elevated but begins to decay and price range compresses, the execution program is likely nearing completion; transient impact then unwinds over the next week, so the child trades against the prior excited direction. The edge can persist because external investors cannot observe the metaorder's terminal size or completion time from daily bars, while liquidity providers initially accommodate rather than immediately arbitrage the flow. This is falsified if cooling positive-excitation episodes continue to outperform, or cooling negative-excitation episodes continue to underperform, at six bars.
factors.name: Hawkes Cooling Metaorder Reversal

factors.trading_idea: Common sector shocks transmit asymmetrically through firms because leveraged, illiquid balance sheets make equity a residual claim with greater effective market and industry beta. Following a negative sector shock, financially fragile firms with historically high downside shock sensitivity may experience continued selling from risk-limit reductions, lender concerns, and mandate-driven de-risking; the positive-shock counterpart is weaker and can be down-weighted. This mechanism is falsified if leverage and liquidity ratios do not increase the persistence of shock-direction returns after controlling for the stock's ordinary trailing volatility.
factors.name: Balance-Sheet Common-Shock Amplification

factors.trading_idea: Fresh deterioration in receivables intensity identifies firms whose reported growth is becoming less cash-backed, a latent fragility state that is usually too slow-moving to time on its own. A left-tail return/range event that closes near the low on abnormal volume is instead evidence of unabsorbed execution demand and liquidity depletion; conditioning that event on the fresh collection break isolates repricings where marginal buyers are least willing to provide support. The interaction has edge because collection weakness alone lacks a catalyst and a generic downside shock can rebound, whereas a cash-quality break accompanied by persistent sell-side execution is more likely to continue over the next week.
factors.name: Fresh Collection Tail-Execution Unwind

factors.trading_idea: Orderly, low-entropy selling identifies an active and persistent liquidation program, but it does not reveal whether the flow is informed or merely mechanical. The child only trusts a fall in marginal downside impact when that selling remains coherent and the latest cash-quality revision is positive, indicating a liquidity supplier is absorbing a transient seller; it shorts the mirror state of coherent selling, rising impact, and deteriorating cash quality. This three-way interaction has edge beyond Parent A because impact release is filtered to genuine metaorder-like flow, and beyond Parent B because directional flow is classified by whether its price impact is relaxing or accelerating.
factors.name: Cash-Anchored Orderly Sell Absorption

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s slow dilution-and-valuation fragility appears to accrue beyond six bars, so this child concentrates on the short-lived disclosure-processing window instead. Investors initially reward a positive price/volume reaction to a newly available report, but may underweight newly disclosed share-count dilution and stock-based compensation because adjusted earnings and headline growth are more salient; the signal shorts names where this attention-heavy reaction accompanies fresh dilution information. The edge should persist briefly because institutional estimate updates, mandate rebalancing, and recognition of per-share dilution occur with delay; it is falsified if fresh dilution disclosures do not predict weaker six-bar returns specifically after positive, high-attention reactions.
factors.name: Dilution Disclosure Attention Lag (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: A lower-wick recovery is not necessarily absorbed forced selling: after a cluster of high-participation downside-accepted bars, a close near the high can instead reflect temporary liquidity replenishment while an informed sell program remains active. The parent’s negative standalone IC is consistent with this interpretation, so the child explicitly identifies recovery-shaped downside shocks occurring inside a self-exciting sell-flow cluster and predicts subsequent negative returns. This edge can persist because the latent parent-order schedule and dealer inventory pressure are not directly observable from daily bars, while arbitrageurs face execution risk before the remaining sell flow has completed.
factors.name: Scheduled Sell Recovery Trap

factors.trading_idea: Fresh quality disclosures are most informative when the market is actively rewarding or penalizing the corresponding fundamental style, rather than in every price regime. The leading return mode across quality, conservative-investment, leverage, and value sleeves acts as a short-run state variable for changing tail-risk and consumption-growth beliefs: investors price newly disclosed operating resilience more aggressively when that common defensive style mode is persistent. The interaction carries edge because Parent A identifies an information event but not whether investors currently value that type of resilience, while Parent B identifies the priced style state but not which firms have received new firm-specific information.
factors.name: Tail-State Quality Update Alignment

factors.trading_idea: Downward order flow is often self-exciting during liquidity stress: negative returns close to the day low create further risk-limit selling and temporarily elevate downside range intensity. A rebound should occur only after that marked downside intensity and realized range begin to decay while the prior stress state remains unusually elevated, indicating that an endogenous liquidation cascade is extinguishing rather than that new bad information is still arriving. This is falsifiable: conditional on the same recent cumulative return, stocks with high prior downside excitation but a larger subsequent intensity-and-range relaxation should earn higher six-day returns; the edge persists because forced deleveraging, inventory rebuilding, and liquidity-provider risk constraints unwind more slowly than the daily shock.
factors.name: Downside Excitation Relaxation Rebound

factors.trading_idea: Investors often treat a quiet realized-price path as evidence that a levered company is safe, even when interest coverage, net-debt capacity, and operating-cash-flow momentum imply that its equity has become highly state contingent. The factor shorts financially fragile stocks whose downside range is abnormally compressed relative to their sector and longs robust firms with similarly subdued realized risk, especially after a broad negative market bar reveals a demand for balance-sheet safety. The hypothesis fails if leverage and coverage add no incremental predictive value beyond sector-relative realized volatility, or if the spread does not strengthen following market downside states.
factors.name: Coverage-Compression Tail Premium

factors.trading_idea: Analyst revisions are more likely to represent an industry-level information shock when their sign agrees with a contemporaneous peer-industry return shock, especially for stocks historically tightly linked to that peer basket. If the stock's own price has not yet incorporated its revision while the industry shock is already being accepted elsewhere, common-shock propagation predicts a near-term catch-up. The edge can persist because dispersed analyst coverage, heterogeneous investor attention, and gradual portfolio rebalancing delay the mapping from sector information to each constituent; falsifiably, the effect should be strongest for sign-confirmed, high-linkage names and should disappear or reverse when revision and peer-shock signs disagree.
factors.name: Common-Shock Revision Confirmation Lag

factors.trading_idea: Concordant EPS and revenue-consensus revisions identify a broader change in analysts' operating outlook than an EPS-only revision, while a quiet contemporaneous volume response indicates that the information has not yet received broad investor attention. The signal emphasizes fresh revisions and lets their effect decay over subsequent sessions, matching gradual institutional assimilation rather than treating a quarterly estimate level as continuously new information. The edge can persist because discretionary investors and benchmarked funds react slowly to low-salience estimate updates, whereas arbitrageurs face uncertainty over whether an isolated forecast change is durable. The hypothesis is falsified if fresh, same-direction EPS and revenue revisions with low event-day volume do not show stronger six-bar drift than equally sized high-attention revisions.
factors.name: Quiet Dual-Estimate Assimilation

factors.trading_idea: A jointly positive earnings and revenue surprise that is supported by cash conversion is more likely to represent durable information than an accrual-driven headline beat. When the initial one-day price response is muted relative to the stock's pre-event volatility, investors have not fully incorporated that information, so analyst and institutional reassessment should continue over the following week. The edge persists because interpreting the agreement among revenue, earnings, and cash flow is attention-intensive, while portfolio constraints and delayed analyst-note dissemination slow the repricing; it is falsified if cash-confirmed surprises with muted initial reactions do not outperform over six subsequent bars.
factors.name: Cash-Confirmed Surprise Absorption Drift (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: When daily returns become unusually synchronized across the market, a common risk shock dominates firm-specific price discovery and capital reallocates toward balance-sheet quality. In that state, profitable cash-rich firms with conservative leverage should outperform fragile firms over the following week because passive de-risking and mandate-constrained investors cannot immediately rebalance every exposure. This is a cross-sectional implementation of factor timing: it should fail if high return synchrony does not raise the subsequent quality-minus-fragility spread, despite the signal being active only during common-shock regimes.
factors.name: Common-Shock Quality Defense (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: Sector shocks propagate first through liquid bellwethers, leaving low-turnover firms with temporary beta-adjusted response gaps. The child trades that delayed assimilation only when a fresh cash-conversion-versus-consensus wedge supports the shock direction and peer estimate revisions confirm that the sector move reflects information rather than indiscriminate risk transfer. This interaction has edge because sector shocks identify the immediate propagation impulse, while the cash/headline contradiction identifies which apparent laggards are fundamentally capable of catching up rather than correctly discounted for hidden funding or operating stress.
factors.name: Sector Shock Cash-Wedge Diffusion

factors.trading_idea: Investors and narrative-driven models tend to extrapolate visually clean price trends, especially when the path has high linearity and therefore appears easier to explain. The factor buys firms where improving estimate and cash-flow evidence has not yet produced a correspondingly clear upward trend, and shorts firms with a highly linear positive trend unsupported by improving consensus or cash-generation fundamentals. The inefficiency should persist because slow-moving discretionary investors often update from salient price paths before reconciling those paths with quarterly fundamental confirmation. It is falsified if trend/fundamental disagreement has no subsequent directional correction after controlling for industry and valuation.
factors.name: Trend Linearity Fundamental Validation Gap (jitter) (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: Quarterly disclosures that jointly show revenue-growth acceleration, gross-margin expansion, and faster inventory turnover reveal genuine demand and operating leverage rather than a transitory accounting surprise. Investors and analysts often parse these linked income-statement and balance-sheet implications gradually, so the information should diffuse over the following trading week rather than be fully incorporated on the filing date; the edge persists because assembling and interpreting the cross-statement confirmation is costly and sparse. Falsifiably, high-score disclosure updates should outperform low-score updates over six days even after conditioning on contemporaneous earnings-surprise magnitude and release-day return, while isolated or internally contradictory operating updates should not.
factors.name: Operating-Leverage Efficiency Disclosure Drift

factors.trading_idea: Downside returns accompanied by unusual participation can form self-exciting liquidation clusters: prior selling raises volatility, triggers risk limits, and attracts further mechanically motivated sales. The child goes long only as the exponentially decayed sell-pressure intensity begins to fall from an elevated level relative to its slower background, indicating that the endogenous cascade is exhausting rather than that negative information is still arriving. This is falsified if the post-extinction signal has no positive six-day return after controlling for recent idiosyncratic return, realized volatility, and relative volume; the edge can persist because latent liquidation completion is difficult to distinguish from informed selling in daily data and liquidity providers require time to replenish inventory.
factors.name: Endogenous Sell-Cluster Relaxation

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth states are proxied by market downside-semivariance bursts, when marginal investors become unusually sensitive to assets whose returns have recently acquired greater downside exposure. A rising conditional downside beta should trigger short-horizon de-risking most strongly for firms with weak cash-liquidity buffers, because their equity is more exposed to financing and consumption-tail states. The edge should persist because tail-risk sensitivity is estimated noisily and portfolio-risk reallocations occur gradually; it is falsified if downside-beta innovations do not predict relatively negative six-day returns specifically during elevated market downside-semivariance regimes after conditioning on cash liquidity.
factors.name: Consumption-Tail Semibeta De-Risking

factors.trading_idea: Forced deleveraging and stop-loss activity create clustered negative-return events whose intensity decays only gradually after the marginal seller has exhausted inventory. The signal estimates fast and slow exponential kernels of volume-confirmed downside shocks: a slow kernel above the fast kernel identifies a recently intense sell cascade that is now decelerating, while the reverse identifies fresh downside ignition. The falsifiable hypothesis is that names with the largest sector-relative kernel-decay state outperform names with fresh downside acceleration over the next six sessions; the edge can persist because constrained sellers and liquidity providers unwind inventory over multiple days rather than instantaneously.
factors.name: Downside Kernel Release

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s positive realized IC implies that its apparent sell-impact deficit is not unfinished downside, but evidence that abnormal sell arrivals are being absorbed with unexpectedly little price concession. This child treats that state explicitly as resilient absorption: after a coherent negative earnings rupture, name-specific sell activity that is high relative to its sector but produces less downside than the name’s own trailing sell-impact relationship predicts should precede a rebound over the next six sessions. The edge can persist because liquidity suppliers and fundamental buyers absorb event-driven institutional liquidation gradually, while risk limits and uncertainty prevent immediate arbitrage; the hypothesis is falsified if these observations do not exhibit both low contemporaneous impact conditional on sell arrivals and positive subsequent returns.
factors.name: Isolated Sell-Arrival Absorption Reversal

factors.trading_idea: A directional metaorder is most likely to reverse when its self-exciting arrival rate has begun to cool, but the preceding flow has already produced abnormally large displacement per unit activity. Cooling alone can reflect a pause in informed trading, while impact acceleration alone can be an ongoing liquidity-buffer failure; their interaction identifies the terminal overshoot state in which demand is fading while transient inventory and liquidity-premium effects remain priced in. The signal therefore trades against the earlier directional burst only when compression confirms that new price discovery has stopped.
factors.name: Cooling Impact Overshoot Reversal

factors.trading_idea: Broad peer-mode moves are normally assimilated gradually, so a stock that has not yet matched its leave-one-out peer move tends to catch up. The economically important asymmetry occurs after a negative sector shock: firms with fragile balance sheets and historically elevated downside sector beta face risk-limit selling, lender concerns, and constrained arbitrage, making a lagging negative peer move more likely to continue rather than merely normalize. Neither parent isolates this state-specific channel: the spectral factor does not distinguish financially vulnerable delayed downside assimilation, while the balance-sheet factor lacks a stock-specific peer-implied completion deficit.
factors.name: Fragility-Gated Spectral Downside Lag

factors.trading_idea: Sparse pre-release estimate maintenance proxies for analyst attention gaps and information avoidance: a reported surprise is harder for investors to classify when consensus has been quiet. The child only amplifies such neglected surprises when contemporaneous operating-cash conversion, adjusted for receivables growth, confirms the surprise's direction. Staleness alone has no directional fundamental content, while cash quality alone is likely incorporated rapidly for well-covered names; their interaction identifies uncertainty that is resolved gradually after an economically credible earnings release.
factors.name: Consensus Silence Cash Resolution Drift

factors.trading_idea: Large return-volume events that arrive during an already self-exciting sequence are more likely to reflect an unfinished institutional execution cascade than isolated public-news incorporation. The child goes with the latest signed event only when prior same-direction abnormal events imply high endogenous Hawkes-style excitation and directional coherence. The edge should persist because trading against an active cascade is costly when the underlying order splitting and liquidity replenishment process is not directly observable from daily bars; it is falsified if event-day continuation is equally strong for isolated events or for events opposing the prior cascade direction.
factors.name: Endogenous Cascade Reignition

factors.trading_idea: Rather than assuming that quality, conservative investment, and balance-sheet safety always earn the same premium, this signal estimates the currently dominant fundamental-style return mode and its short-run persistence. It follows the factor-timing object in the source paper, but applies it cross-sectionally: a stock receives exposure to the fundamental sleeves whose recent aggregate premium is forecast to persist. The edge should disappear if lagged style-premium dynamics have no out-of-sample predictive power after volatility scaling, or if the inferred dominant mode is unstable from one rebalance to the next.
factors.name: Fundamental Style Eigenmode Premium Cast

factors.trading_idea: Analyst estimate changes in one firm convey read-through information about common industry demand, costs, and competitive conditions before every peer has received an explicit consensus update. The factor buys firms whose own estimates remain quiet while their industry peers have recently received positive EPS and revenue revisions, and shorts the converse. The edge should persist for several days because earnings releases, analyst coverage, and portfolio-manager research are staggered; it is falsified if peer revisions do not predict laggard returns after excluding names with their own contemporaneous estimate changes.
factors.name: Industry Revision Laggard Relay

factors.trading_idea: Downward price moves tend to generate self-exciting liquidity withdrawal: an initial sell shock raises the probability of further selling as dealers widen risk limits and forced traders respond to losses. The child identifies names with elevated inherited downside excitation but a sharply reduced current sell impulse and an upper-range close, indicating that sell-side pressure has exhausted while liquidity is beginning to refill. The edge should persist because inventory replenishment and the return of constrained liquidity providers occur over several daily bars rather than instantaneously; it is falsified if these exhaustion states do not deliver higher six-bar returns than equally volatile states with continuing downside excitation.
factors.name: Downside Excitation Exhaustion Repair

factors.trading_idea: Analyst EPS-consensus revisions contain new fundamental information, but the information is incorporated slowly when the contemporaneous price response is small relative to the revision. The factor therefore buys stocks with unusually positive recent estimate revisions whose prices have not kept pace, and shorts the converse after removing sector-level revision and return effects. The edge should persist because interpreting estimate changes requires attention and confidence in a noisy, discrete information source; it is falsifiable if revision magnitude has no incremental 6-bar predictive power when the initial price response is muted versus when it is already aligned with the revision.
factors.name: Estimate-Price Assimilation Gap

factors.trading_idea: Negative-return volatility innovations can become self-exciting during forced deleveraging, but a declining short-horizon downside-semivariance estimate while total downside risk remains elevated identifies the transition from cascade propagation to inventory digestion. The child requires this cooling state to occur with unusually high turnover but compressed intraday impact, indicating that liquidity providers are absorbing residual supply rather than withdrawing. The edge should persist because the distinction between an active sell cascade and a cooling inventory overhang is difficult to arbitrage using daily bars: it requires observing both the asymmetric volatility-memory path and contemporaneous execution capacity.
factors.name: Asymmetric Semivariance Cooling Repair

factors.trading_idea: Peer-mode lag is most actionable when the lagging stock is simultaneously receiving quiet, abnormal directional volume that historically converts into subsequent price impulses. The spectral peer residual identifies the information already incorporated by economically connected names, while the attention-to-price conversion state distinguishes latent institutional accumulation or distribution from benign liquidity noise. Their interaction carries edge because a peer catch-up gap alone can persist for slow-moving or noise-dominated names, whereas attention conversion alone lacks an external information anchor; aligned peer pressure and proven local conversion jointly identify imminent assimilation.
factors.name: Conversion-Gated Peer Lag

factors.trading_idea: The parent indicates that financing resilience is useful during stress, but its strongest decay occurs beyond the mandated six-bar horizon, consistent with a persistent fear-level gate that remains active after the initial reallocating impulse. This child instead activates only when broad downside, range, and participation stress are accelerating: risk-controlled allocators first rotate toward firms with liquidity, cash generation, debt capacity, and interest-service resilience when a new fear episode begins. The hypothesis is falsified if the resilience spread is equally strong after fear has already persisted for several sessions, or if it remains after removing the fear-onset interaction; the edge can persist because balance-sheet resilience is quarterly disclosed while forced de-risking and mandate-driven reallocation occur rapidly at stress onset.
factors.name: Fear-Onset Financing Resilience Rotation

factors.trading_idea: Fresh analyst EPS-consensus revisions contain information that is incorporated gradually because investors must assess whether revised forecasts reflect durable operating improvement or merely transitory accounting effects. Upward revisions should drift most reliably for firms with high cash-flow income quality, where reported earnings are more likely to be realizable; low-quality firms receive little weight rather than being mechanically shorted. The hypothesis is falsified if quality-conditioned estimate innovations do not predict six-day returns after industry demeaning, or if their predictive relation is no stronger than unconditioned revisions.
factors.name: Quality-Gated Consensus Innovation Drift

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s positive realized IC suggests that high-volume downside wicks closing near the high more often represent successful absorption than unfinished sell programs. This child isolates that interpretation by requiring unusually low range-per-participation (liquidity replenishment) and persistent, regular elevated participation after the recovery, consistent with a latent buy program being executed against temporarily supplied liquidity. The hypothesis is falsified if these compressed, regular recovery events do not outperform otherwise similar high-volume recovery events over the next six days; the edge can persist because latent execution schedules and effective depth are not directly observable from daily bars, while arbitraging them requires absorbing inventory and impact risk.
factors.name: Compressed Recovery Execution Resilience

factors.trading_idea: The child treats the pre-announcement rollover cascade as a state variable rather than a standalone short signal: financially fragile firms with negative estimate revisions and clustered downside flow are candidates for forced-sale exhaustion. Within that state, a high-turnover intraday recovery during broad market fear is interpreted as genuine inventory transfer and short-covering confirmation, so the rebound continues over the next six bars rather than fading. Neither parent alone distinguishes a generic fear rebound from a rebound that occurs precisely after a vulnerable issuer's forced-selling inventory has likely been absorbed.
factors.name: Fear-Conditioned Rollover Relief Continuation

factors.trading_idea: A positive EPS beat with weak revenue confirmation creates an information-avoidance state: investors can observe the headline but cannot quickly determine whether the implied margin improvement is durable. In that state, a cooling one-sided price-volume excitation is more likely to represent temporary headline-driven execution and positioning than a fully informed repricing, so its terminal impact should reverse. Margin ambiguity alone does not identify whether price pressure is transient, while Hawkes cooling alone cannot distinguish informed flow from mechanically amplified headline flow; their interaction isolates completion reversals specifically where fundamental interpretation is costly.
factors.name: Ambiguity-Gated Hawkes Completion Reversal

factors.trading_idea: Gradually executed institutional demand generates clustered, same-direction high-volume bars: a daily-bar proxy for self-exciting order flow is the acceleration of exponentially decayed signed-volume-event intensity. The child trades only the portion of this acceleration whose contemporaneous price response is below the stock's own trailing flow-to-return impact estimate, interpreting it as temporarily absorbed demand that should transmit into price within six days. This is falsifiable: conditional on signed flow acceleration, the impact-deficit residual should predict forward returns, while fully priced or over-priced flow episodes should not; the edge can persist because execution participation limits and liquidity-provider inventory management defer impact.
factors.name: Excitation Impact-Deficit Acceleration

factors.trading_idea: Positive revenue-consensus revisions are most vulnerable when they coincide with deteriorating collection quality, weak cash conversion, and financing dependence, because investors initially extrapolate the headline revision while underweighting the balance-sheet evidence. The parent-B sign contradiction is interpreted as rapid repricing rather than a compensated premium: high downside-tail exposure makes financing-sensitive collection problems especially painful when aggregate bad-state innovations arrive. The interaction carries edge because an optimistic revision alone may be credible, while collection fragility alone may be stale; their conjunction identifies precisely the over-extrapolated claims whose downside-state sensitivity is not yet fully reflected in price.
factors.name: Revision-Collection Tail Repricing

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s positive realized IC despite its intended short-cascade interpretation suggests that daily downside excitation more often identifies a liquidity-driven overshoot than persistent fundamental deterioration. This child retains the asymmetric Hawkes-style downside-clustering signal, but only treats it as a positive repair opportunity when the selloff occurs on abnormally weak participation and the company has industry-relative balance-sheet resilience. The edge should persist because liquidity-constrained sellers and risk-averse arbitrageurs can temporarily push fundamentally solvent names below clearing prices; it is falsified if resilient firms with high cascade-and-drought scores do not outperform fragile firms with comparable downside cascades over the following six bars.
factors.name: Resilient Downside Cascade Repair

factors.trading_idea: A large idiosyncratic downside opening gap can reflect thin opening-auction liquidity, overnight inventory transfer, or a temporary imbalance rather than permanent information. When that gap is materially recovered during the same session on unusually high participation, it reveals that resting liquidity replenished and absorbed the sell imbalance; the remaining price concession should unwind over the following week. The edge persists because opening-liquidity providers and arbitrageurs face adverse-selection risk before observing whether intraday recovery is genuine, while a high-volume recovery is a delayed confirmation of absorption. This is falsified if recovered high-participation downside gaps do not outperform equally large downside gaps that remain weak into the close.
factors.name: Opening Dislocation Recovery Participation

factors.trading_idea: During broad, high-participation market selloffs, investors often extrapolate index-level fear into individual names and temporarily punish the largest sector-relative losers. The effect should reverse within roughly six sessions when the selloff is not corroborated by a contemporaneous negative analyst-consensus update; the absence of new fundamental deterioration distinguishes temporary flow pressure from genuine repricing. The edge can persist because identifying whether a sharp relative loss is macro-flow-driven rather than information-driven requires combining market state, sector-relative returns, and point-in-time estimate revisions, while constrained investors may still be forced to sell during the stress episode.
factors.name: Macro-Flow Information-Silence Repair

factors.trading_idea: A discrete consensus revision is informative only when the market has not yet acknowledged it in sector-relative price, but that apparent underreaction is more likely to correct for firms with internally credible funding. The signal therefore treats Parent B's genuine revision-event state as an activation condition and Parent A's free-cash-flow/debt-financing state as a reliability weight. This interaction distinguishes delayed information diffusion in self-funded firms from rational skepticism toward debt-dependent issuers, where an unpriced revision may not be durable.
factors.name: Cash-Credible Revision Event Gap

factors.trading_idea: Earnings surprises that are difficult to translate from revenue into sustainable margin implications are incorporated more slowly when analyst consensus has been relatively stale and the initial price response is muted. The child isolates this margin-translation problem rather than relying on a potentially noisy endogenous execution-cascade gate, then holds the signal only until a visible consensus estimate revision resolves the uncertainty. The hypothesis is falsifiable: conditional on fresh dual EPS/revenue disclosures, future six-bar returns should be increasing in signed EPS surprise times revenue-versus-EPS disagreement, prior estimate staleness, and same-day underreaction; the edge should disappear after an estimate update because analyst-model roll-forward removes the information-processing bottleneck.
factors.name: Consensus Margin Translation Latency

factors.trading_idea: Analyst estimate revisions predict returns most cleanly when the market has not yet incorporated them, but investors are more willing to defer price discovery when the issuer has a credible capital-allocation buffer: strong free-cash-flow yield, limited debt issuance, and no apparent need to fund repurchases beyond internally generated cash. This conditions Parent A's fast revision-versus-price mismatch on Parent B's slow balance-sheet credibility state, rather than relying on Parent B's sparse and overfit earnings-surprise branches. The interaction carries edge because a muted reaction to a revision is more likely to be temporary underattention for financially self-funded firms, whereas the same apparent gap in debt-dependent firms can rationally reflect skepticism about the durability of per-share earnings.
factors.name: Cash-Backed Revision Assimilation

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s positive realized sign suggests that high-participation rebounds were more often evidence of demand absorption than temporary seller exits. This child tests a slower and more directly falsifiable version of that interpretation: a newly reported, jointly positive EPS and revenue surprise that receives a muted industry-relative price response should continue upward as analysts, fundamental investors, and benchmarked allocators assimilate the information over the following week; the reverse should hold for jointly negative surprises. The edge persists because updating estimates, mandates, and portfolio weights is staggered, while immediately arbitraging the signal requires trading around sparse quarterly disclosures and bearing event-specific gap risk. The hypothesis is falsified if six-bar returns do not increase monotonically with surprise direction times the residual-response gap, or if the effect remains after the announcement-day residual response is already fully aligned with the surprise.
factors.name: Dual-Surprise Residual Assimilation

factors.trading_idea: Information often arrives through economically connected peer groups, while individual names adjust with heterogeneous speed because of liquidity, analyst coverage, and investor attention. Build a rolling return-correlation graph and isolate coherent peer-mode moves rather than treating a sector average as the relevant benchmark; buy stocks lagging a broad positive mode and short stocks lagging a broad negative mode. The hypothesis is falsified when coherent graph-mode moves do not predict catch-up returns after excluding the stock's own contribution, while the opposite side is supplied by traders treating the move as idiosyncratic noise or by constrained relative-value capital.
factors.name: Spectral Peer-Mode Lag Assimilation

factors.trading_idea: Negative sector moves become more informative when they arrive in an accelerating cluster rather than as an isolated shock: repeated peer losses trigger correlated risk-limit reductions, ETF/redemption flow, and dealer inventory constraints. Firms with weak cash buffers and high leverage have greater equity convexity to this common-flow state, while high historical downside loading identifies the names most exposed to the sector cascade. The edge should persist because synchronized institutional deleveraging is costly to reverse immediately and is not fully arbitraged while liquidity providers are managing inventory. This is falsified if accelerated leave-one-out sector sell intensity does not predict more-negative six-day returns specifically among fragile, high-downside-loading firms.
factors.name: Leave-One-Out Sector Sell-Cluster Fragility

factors.trading_idea: The child identifies a two-stage forced-sale process: Parent A's slow-minus-fast marked Hawkes intensity indicates that a sell cascade has aged and marginal selling is subsiding, while Parent B's panic morphology confirms that the residual pressure was absorbed through a close away from the intraday low. The balance-sheet buffer is used as an interaction term rather than a standalone score: a terminal-looking price reversal is more credible when cash, operating cash flow, and low leverage make the selloff unlikely to reflect imminent financing distress. Neither parent alone distinguishes an exhausted cascade that has actually found demand from a merely fading but still unabsorbed decline.
factors.name: Hawkes Absorption Buffer Repair

factors.trading_idea: Analyst information avoidance is most consequential when a fresh earnings disclosure is materially inconsistent with the same-day price response, but consensus had already been stale before the report. The price move is an immediate, low-processing-cost reaction, whereas reconciling EPS and revenue news with a stale forecast requires analyst work; the resulting implementation gap should persist until the next visible consensus revision, rather than disappearing after one bar. The edge persists against arbitrage because the relevant uncertainty is issuer-specific and quarterly, while the factor explicitly measures the temporary interval in which public accounting information has arrived but the analyst forecast bridge remains unresolved.
factors.name: Unresolved Earnings Implementation Clock

factors.trading_idea: Earnings information diffuses gradually when both earnings and revenue surprises point in the same direction but the contemporaneous price response is small relative to the fundamental news. The child goes long positive coherent surprises that received too little immediate price confirmation and short negative coherent surprises that were insufficiently discounted, expressing the gap over the following six sessions. The edge should persist because interpreting cross-channel earnings releases and reallocating institutional portfolios takes longer than reacting to a headline; it is falsified if response-gap portfolios have no positive 6-bar return spread after controlling for the signed surprise itself.
factors.name: Coherent Surprise Response Gap

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth states make aggregate downside shocks disproportionately important to marginal investors, so equities that reliably load on those shocks should earn compensation. The child measures each stock's trailing downside-tail beta to the cross-sectional market return, but only rewards that exposure when the company is both cash-generative and cheaply valued on free-cash-flow yield; this separates compensated systematic tail exposure from likely permanent distress. The edge should persist because tail-risk-bearing capital is scarce and arbitrageurs cannot cheaply eliminate compensation for crash-state exposure, while the cash-flow screen reduces bankruptcy and accounting-noise contamination. Falsifiably, the long leg should have higher realized returns than the short leg primarily in periods with elevated aggregate left-tail frequency, and it should exhibit more negative realized returns conditional on future market-tail days.
factors.name: Cashflow Tail-Exposure Compensation

factors.trading_idea: Analyst revisions are more credible when earnings and revenue consensus move in the same direction, because the revision then reflects a broad reassessment of demand and operating outlook rather than a mechanical margin or accounting adjustment. The signal retains revision information briefly after it arrives, allowing asynchronous updates across the two forecast channels to confirm one another while excluding the immediate report-day surprise mechanism that was sparse in the parent. The hypothesis is falsifiable: positive six-day IC should concentrate in names with coherent EPS-and-revenue revision memory, while single-channel or conflicting revisions should have weak or negative IC. The edge can persist because consensus updates are fragmented across analysts and are incorporated into institutional valuation systems with heterogeneous monitoring and portfolio-rebalancing delays.
factors.name: Forecast Channel Coherence Decay

factors.trading_idea: Sector-synchronous, high-volume sell-arrival clusters are usually mechanical deleveraging shocks and tend to repair when a name is unusually weak relative to its sector. However, Parent B's realized negative IC indicates that peer-concordant tail moves from a fresh earnings anchor are informational continuation events rather than reversals: peer agreement validates gradual incorporation of a heavy-tailed belief shock. The child therefore buys forced-selling residuals only after discounting names whose downside is earnings-anchored and industry-confirmed, while allowing peer-confirmed positive and negative earnings tails to retain their directional continuation component.
factors.name: Earnings-Disambiguated Liquidity Repair (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: An adverse earnings-and-revenue rupture in a financially fragile company can create forced institutional selling, but negative close-location flow is only a rebound signal when that supply is demonstrably being absorbed in a compressed individual range. The complementary state variable is leave-one-out sector-wide range-volume stress: it identifies correlated dealer-capacity withdrawal while avoiding mechanically treating the stock's own compressed bar as sector stress. In this regime, a fragile firm's persistent sell imbalance is temporary inventory transferred to constrained liquidity providers rather than fresh price discovery, so delayed dealer replenishment and seller exhaustion produce a six-session rebound that neither fundamental rupture nor sector synchrony isolates alone.
factors.name: Sector-Stress Rupture Absorption Rebound

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth risk makes co-crash exposure especially costly: firms whose returns load more strongly on market downside-tail days than on ordinary days should require a higher expected return premium. The premium should be largest for financially fragile firms, because leverage and weak liquidity make aggregate consumption shocks more likely to impair their financing capacity. The signal is only expressed outside an ongoing aggregate selloff, when this disaster compensation is priced rather than overwhelmed by contemporaneous deleveraging; it persists because arbitrageurs must bear rare, correlated crash losses and funding constraints. This is falsifiable: high-score names should outperform over the next six bars primarily in calm market states, and their realized losses should be disproportionately severe during future market-tail observations.
factors.name: Calm-State Disaster Beta Carry

factors.trading_idea: A sudden rise in a stock's correlation with its leave-one-out industry basket indicates that an industry-wide common shock has become the dominant return driver, rather than merely reflecting isolated name-level news. Stocks with larger pre-existing loading to that industry innovation should continue moving in the direction of the peer shock while covariance beliefs and hedges adjust over the following week. The edge can persist because dynamic correlation and beta are noisy, time-varying objects that cannot be costlessly arbitraged without bearing idiosyncratic hedge error; it is falsified if the conditional forward-return slope on beta times peer shock is absent after correlation acceleration, or is equally strong when correlations are declining.
factors.name: Correlation-Burst Industry Loading Relay

factors.trading_idea: A firm's receivables-and-inventory deterioration is most informative when recent peer disclosures already establish a common customer-credit or demand shock, but the firm's own price has not yet reacted materially to its filing. Funding-fragile firms cannot absorb the resulting cash-conversion pressure, so muted initial price response represents an attention-limited underreaction rather than resilience. Neither parent alone identifies this disclosure-to-price assimilation gap: peer confirmation validates that the event is systemic, while the muted-response state selects the cases where the validated shock remains unpriced.
factors.name: Peer Cash-Cycle Muted-Reaction Fragility

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed downside shocks create a nonlinear belief-update state in which investors extrapolate the visible selloff and discount slow-moving fundamental evidence. The signal activates Parent A's fundamental-versus-linear-trend disagreement only when Parent B's marked downside-excitation process indicates an acute, accepted selloff: firms with improving estimates and cash-flow support but weak prices should rebound as forced selling exhausts, while weak-fundamental firms with apparently smooth prior trends remain vulnerable. The interaction carries edge because fundamental disagreement alone is slow-moving and panic intensity alone cannot distinguish temporary liquidity liquidation from economically justified deterioration.
factors.name: Panic-State Fundamental Extrapolation Wedge

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth risk makes investors particularly sensitive to firms whose cash flows are exposed to aggregate downside states. A firm with high realized downside beta, worsening receivables intensity, and deteriorating operating-cash-flow conversion is vulnerable to a rapid repricing when its new quarterly disclosure makes the duration and fragility of its cash flows salient. The edge should persist because tail-state exposure and working-capital quality are costly to aggregate across issuers and are not fully incorporated by investors focused on headline revenue growth; it is falsified if this disclosure-timed vulnerability has no negative six-bar return association after controlling for downside beta or collection deterioration separately.
factors.name: Tail-State Collection Fragility

factors.trading_idea: The parent mixes the immediate shock with its later repair phase, which is consistent with its stronger 1-3 bar and 12-bar results but weak 6-bar result. This child explicitly enters only after an idiosyncratic range-volatility shock has begun to relax and trading capacity has replenished, identifying the gradual inventory-transfer phase in which liquidity providers can unwind positions and prices continue to normalize over roughly a week. The edge should persist because replenishment and inventory redistribution are constrained by dealer balance sheets and by investors' staggered execution rather than being instantaneously arbitraged. It is falsified if, conditional on equally large idiosyncratic shocks, names with declining range stress and recovering dollar volume do not have more signed 6-day reversal than names whose stress remains elevated.
factors.name: Idiosyncratic Shock Relaxation Phase

factors.trading_idea: A revenue-and-margin-confirmed earnings surprise is most underpriced when consensus had been stale immediately before the report: investors anchored on an unrevised forecast and have not fully incorporated the new evidence about demand and operating leverage. The durable-surprise component filters transitory EPS beats or misses, while estimate silence identifies the information-avoidance state in which the same fundamental revelation requires a larger repricing. Neither parent alone distinguishes a credible operating shock from the degree of prior forecast anchoring.
factors.name: Pre-Report Silence Durable Surprise Drift

factors.trading_idea: Repeated abnormal directional trading with unusually compressed intraday ranges indicates a latent metaorder being absorbed by replenishing liquidity rather than immediately incorporated into price. Unlike the parent’s short-lived acceleration signal, this child requires sustained directional participation across many days and uses range compression as evidence that dealer inventory capacity is being consumed, implying that subsequent price adjustment should occur as absorption capacity weakens. The hypothesis is falsifiable: conditional on equally persistent signed-volume pressure, forward returns should be substantially stronger when realized ranges are compressed than when the same pressure already produces wide-range price discovery; the edge can persist because institutional execution schedules and liquidity replenishment are not directly observable from daily bars.
factors.name: Persistent Absorption Range Compression (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: An idiosyncratic downside-range shock that closes near the bar high is not necessarily completed selling: it can be a temporary liquidity-provider rebound while a stock-specific institutional sell program remains active. The negative realized signs of both parents are consistent with this interpretation: isolated flow and intrabar resilience identify a deceptive absorption phase rather than durable recovery, with dealers and slower participants subsequently re-hedging inventory over the next week. The interaction carries edge because sector isolation distinguishes name-specific supply from broad risk-off volatility, while close-location recovery identifies the transient bounce within that otherwise persistent sell-pressure episode; neither condition alone identifies this relay state.
factors.name: Isolated Downside Absorption Relay

factors.trading_idea: Firms with a stable historical exposure to sector-wide return innovations should eventually absorb a sector impulse, but heterogeneous investor attention and benchmark-driven trading cause some constituents to lag their implied response. The factor estimates each stock's trailing exposure to leave-one-out sector returns and buys stocks whose recent return is below the beta-implied sector move, while shorting those that have overreacted. This is falsified if beta-implied sector-response gaps do not predict within-sector relative returns over the next six sessions; the edge can persist because estimating changing firm-level sector exposures and trading the residual gap requires more than a simple sector-momentum trade.
factors.name: Persistent Exposure Peer Impulse Gap

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth risk implies that the relevant priced exposure is not ordinary market beta but the additional sensitivity of a stock specifically on aggregate downside-tail days. Stocks whose returns co-crash more than their normal beta predicts should require higher expected returns as compensation for losses when marginal utility is highest; this premium can persist because arbitraging it requires bearing concentrated crash risk and financing drawdowns. The hypothesis is falsifiable: after controlling for ordinary market beta, forward six-bar returns should increase monotonically with estimated downside-tail beta amplification, and the relationship should be weakest for names without statistically sufficient tail observations.
factors.name: Consumption-Tail Amplification Premium

factors.trading_idea: Broad fear shocks create mechanical selling that is strongest in stocks with high historical exposure to market-wide de-risking. The child isolates an idiosyncratic negative return residual relative to that fear exposure, then conditions its expected reversal on sector-relative financing resilience: a defensive firm sold beyond its fear-beta-implied move is more likely to recover over six days because its balance sheet reduces genuine refinancing risk. Neither parent alone distinguishes a generic defensive rotation from a temporary, stock-specific forced-sale overshoot in a defensive firm.
factors.name: Fear-Beta Resilience Overshoot Repair

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth risk implies that equities which lose disproportionately when the rest of the market enters its left tail should command a premium, especially when debt makes their cash flows difficult to self-insure. The child estimates each stock's causal lower-tail beta to a leave-one-out market return and amplifies it only for financially fragile firms, rather than using disclosure attention or dilution. This is falsified if high conditional tail beta combined with high debt-to-assets does not predict higher six-bar returns after controlling for ordinary market beta; the premium can persist because these positions are most painful to arbitrage during aggregate downside states.
factors.name: Consumption Tail Financing Premium

factors.trading_idea: The parent report shows that downside-excitation and thin-volume shocks predict positive, rather than negative, subsequent returns, consistent with forced-selling cascades reaching an exhaustion phase instead of continuing indefinitely. This child isolates that mature-cascade state by requiring a current downside shock and abnormal price impact, but only when the bar closes well above its low, indicating that latent liquidity has begun absorbing distressed supply. The edge should persist because inventory-constrained liquidity providers and fundamental buyers cannot immediately offset a multi-day liquidation program; it is falsified if high-scoring names do not outperform over the following six bars, or if their apparent absorption does not distinguish them from equally severe unabsorbed selloffs.
factors.name: Cascade Maturity Absorption Rebound

factors.trading_idea: A close near one end of an unusually large daily range is evidence that the closing auction cleared with one-sided demand; when that displacement occurred on abnormally little turnover, the move is more likely to reflect temporarily withdrawn liquidity than fully completed price discovery. Persistent signed endpoint pressure that remains after removing contemporaneous return exposure should predict further same-direction adjustment over the next six bars as latent liquidity demand is gradually executed. This is falsified if the residualized thin-book endpoint signal has no incremental six-bar return relationship after controlling for recent return, range volatility, and relative volume; the effect can persist because publicly observable bars only imperfectly reveal latent supply, while arbitraging it requires bearing inventory and adverse-selection risk.
factors.name: Endpoint Auction Thin-Book Pressure

factors.trading_idea: Institutional metaorders are commonly split across consecutive continuous-trading sessions, producing elevated but unusually regular participation together with same-signed intraday price pressure. Unlike an overnight news jump, this footprint indicates that execution demand is likely unfinished, so the signed intraday impact should continue over the next several days. The edge persists because liquidity providers and arbitrageurs cannot observe the remaining parent-order quantity and face adverse-selection risk when leaning against a persistent execution program. It is falsified if equally strong intraday moves have identical six-day returns whether volume participation is regular and elevated or irregular and episodic.
factors.name: Cadenced Intraday Information Footprint

factors.trading_idea: The parent result implies that a cooling downside-shock cluster is not generally a liquidity-repair state: declining immediate price impact can instead reflect an informed seller spreading a remaining order across days as displayed liquidity replenishes. This child isolates that interpretation by requiring cooling downside excitation to coincide with persistently abnormal trading activity and closes near the daily low, evidence that supply is still being executed rather than that selling has exhausted. The edge should persist because execution schedules, dealer inventory constraints, and the adverse-selection risk faced by liquidity providers make the residual supply difficult to arbitrage away immediately; it is falsified if these high-participation cooling states do not have more negative six-day returns than otherwise similar cooling clusters whose volume normalizes.
factors.name: Scheduled Sell Pressure Continuation

factors.trading_idea: A peer-mode return lead is most likely to be assimilated rapidly when the lagging company has a credible, internally financed repurchase program and is cheap relative to its sector: the buyback supplies both an informed capital-allocation signal and a natural marginal buyer. Conversely, peer-implied moves in expensive firms financing distributions with debt are less credible and can reverse as investors reassess the support mechanism. The interaction creates edge because the spectral signal supplies near-term timing while the financing-and-value state distinguishes durable information diffusion from fragile peer contagion.
factors.name: Cash-Credible Peer Completion

factors.trading_idea: A fresh earnings surprise that attracts unusually high participation but produces little same-direction price displacement is interpreted as public information being temporarily absorbed by available liquidity rather than fully incorporated into price. The residual information should drift in the direction of the surprise over the next several sessions as liquidity providers rebalance and slower fundamental investors trade after the release. This is falsifiable: conditional on fresh surprises, the effect should be positive only for high-volume, narrow-range, muted-response events, and should disappear or reverse when the initial directional price response is already large. The edge can persist because interpreting surprise quality and supplying/reallocating liquidity after a discrete announcement are costly and capital-constrained, preventing instantaneous arbitrage of every muted event.
factors.name: Depth-Dampened Earnings Assimilation

factors.trading_idea: During a systemic drawdown, persistent low-impact selling in firms with weak cash buffers, high leverage, and slow inventory conversion is more likely to be forced funding-driven liquidation than informed repricing. Liquidity providers can temporarily absorb this supply, but constrained arbitrage capital prevents immediate correction; once the selling schedule eases, the absorbed inventory produces a short-horizon rebound. The interaction matters because balance-sheet fragility identifies the economic origin of the flow, while the absorbed-flow signature identifies names where that stress has actually reached the market but has not yet cleared.
factors.name: Funding-Gated Absorbed Sell Reversal

factors.trading_idea: Analysts often revise earnings and sales assumptions asynchronously as they update different parts of a valuation model; persistent agreement between the two revisions is therefore more credible than a same-day coincidence. When this coherent revision is not yet reflected in the stock's recent price response, institutional investors still need to reconcile updated revenue, margin, and valuation implications, producing a roughly one-week assimilation drift. The hypothesis is falsifiable: positive future returns should concentrate in names with jointly positive EPS/revenue revision memory and muted recent returns, while the effect should disappear or reverse when revisions disagree or the price has already moved sharply.
factors.name: Coherent Revision Muted-Response Gap

factors.trading_idea: Persistent informed trading should make the joint sequence of daily return direction, relative volume, and range less random before a larger move, consistent with the hidden-order entropy mechanism. Unlike a pure magnitude signal, this factor supplies direction from the dominant recent signed state, so low transition entropy is used only when the structured state is directionally asymmetric. The trade should fail if low entropy predicts only symmetric volatility expansion and not continuation in the dominant state direction; the other side is liquidity providers and short-horizon mean-reversion traders treating a persistent execution program as ordinary noise.
factors.name: Directional State-Entropy Breakout

factors.trading_idea: Earnings surprises supported by revenue growth and improving operating margin contain more durable information than headline-only EPS beats, but the information should only predict six-day returns when the initial price response has not already incorporated it. The signal therefore identifies a fundamental-information/price-assimilation gap rather than simply buying earnings momentum. The edge can persist because investors, analysts, and systematic revision processes update on different schedules after a filing; it is falsified if confirmed surprises with muted same-day reactions do not outperform equally confirmed surprises whose prices immediately move in the surprise direction over the following six bars.
factors.name: Confirmed Surprise Assimilation Gap

factors.trading_idea: A positive earnings surprise is especially underreacted to when it arrives after a resilient company has been sold below its normal fear-beta-implied return during a broad deleveraging episode. The forced-sale state makes the prior negative price narrative less informative, while the surprise supplies a discrete fundamental catalyst that validates a reversal and induces slower institutional estimate and benchmark-position repair. Neither announcement conflict alone nor capitulation reversal alone distinguishes temporary panic selling that is subsequently disproved by fresh earnings information.
factors.name: Capitulation-Validated Surprise Conflict Drift

factors.trading_idea: A fundamentally confirmed earnings surprise should continue to drift when the analyst consensus has not yet updated after the report: investors initially process the headline, while analysts and slower institutional workflows revise forecasts over subsequent days. The signal enters only after the report day and expires when a new EPS-consensus update arrives, converting the parent's one-day event reaction into a six-day revision-latency state. The edge should persist because forecast-revision processing is operationally delayed and is costly to arbitrage perfectly across many dispersed reports; it is falsified if confirmed surprises with stale consensus do not outperform otherwise similar confirmed surprises whose estimates update promptly.
factors.name: Post-Report Consensus Latency Drift

factors.trading_idea: Analysts and investors frequently process an EPS-consensus revision as a headline event, but the persistence of that revision depends on whether it is supported by revenue expectations and improving operating leverage. A positive EPS-estimate change accompanied by positive revenue-estimate change and rising operating or gross margins is more likely an information-rich profitability update than a transient accounting effect, yet constrained attention can delay full repricing. The hypothesis is falsified if price-adjusted, operating-confirmed revisions do not outperform unconfirmed revisions or if their effect is fully incorporated on the update date.
factors.name: Operating-Leverage Confirmed Revision Lag

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s declining-impact condition can arise during sector-wide information shocks, ETF activity, or broad liquidity changes, where reversal is less likely and overlap with the existing book is high. This child isolates stock-specific execution by requiring participation and signed flow to be unusually large relative to the stock’s sector while normalized impact is falling, indicating that liquidity providers are replenishing against a likely mechanical single-name schedule. The hypothesis is falsifiable: reversal should be concentrated in high idiosyncratic-participation, declining-impact episodes and should weaken or disappear when the same activity is sector-synchronous. The edge can persist because the distinction between a latent single-name execution program and common information flow is not directly observable from daily bars, while arbitraging it entails inventory risk if the hidden program continues.
factors.name: Idiosyncratic Refill Inventory Unwind

factors.trading_idea: A concentrated sequence of downside, high-volume bars is a daily-bar proxy for self-exciting liquidation flow. The child goes long only when the slow sell-flow intensity remains elevated but its fast intensity has decayed, while an unusually strong buy-side event arrives: this is the observable signature of sell-program extinction and cross-excited replenishment demand rather than a generic bounce. The edge should persist because fragmented liquidity provision, inventory transfer, and delayed recognition of a completed sell program prevent arbitrageurs from perfectly inferring extinction from a single bar; it is falsified if buy events following decelerating sell intensity do not outperform identical buy events following stable or accelerating sell intensity over six days.
factors.name: Sell-to-Buy Hawkes Extinction

factors.trading_idea: A sharp downside move accompanied by unusually high trading activity is more likely to persist when a firm's financial buffer is thin: low cash/current ratios and high debt reduce management's flexibility and increase the chance of mandate-driven de-risking by holders. This is a buffer-regulated intensity mechanism: the same market shock produces a larger and more persistent order-flow cascade for financially constrained firms. It should be falsified if weak-buffer firms exhibit faster rebound than well-buffered firms after matched downside volume shocks; the other side is value and contrarian capital willing to absorb forced selling but constrained by balance-sheet risk and uncertain financing outcomes.
factors.name: Liquidity-Buffer Downside Cascade

factors.trading_idea: Own downside-flow acceleration is informative for continuation only when it is isolated from a pre-existing sector-wide liquidation state. Parent B supplies the self-exciting arrival-rate signal, while Parent A supplies the leave-one-out peer-flow state: broad peer selling is more consistent with transient basket-flow and dealer inventory transfer, which Parent A's sign contradiction suggests often rebounds, whereas an accelerating shock without peer confirmation is more likely a persistent name-specific execution program. Neither signal alone distinguishes transient systemic liquidation from a concentrated metaorder whose supply can persist through the six-bar horizon.
factors.name: Isolated Sell-Program Continuation

factors.trading_idea: Peer earnings surprises create a signed external valuation impulse, while clustered return-volume events identify whether local trading is beginning to transmit that information through a self-exciting execution cascade. Unlike the standalone Hawkes signal, whose volume clusters can be liquidity noise or exhausted mechanical flow, the child only treats concordant acceleration as informative when it is anchored to a fresh peer fundamental shock and the stock's own price has still underreacted. The interaction captures an early transmission phase: peer news supplies direction, and muted-impact concordant local order-flow clustering supplies evidence that delayed assimilation is actively starting rather than already complete.
factors.name: Fundamental-Anchored Hawkes Relay

factors.trading_idea: Analysts and discretionary investors often process EPS and revenue misses using familiar templates, but jointly unusual earnings reports that are far from a firm's own historical EPS-revenue surprise pattern require slower model and narrative revision. Go long firms with recently released, coherent positive EPS-and-revenue surprises that are statistically off their historical surprise manifold, and short analogous negative ruptures. The mechanism is falsified if manifold-distance conditioning adds no incremental post-release return predictability beyond the signed EPS and revenue surprises themselves; it may persist because rare multi-dimensional outcomes are difficult to assimilate into standardized analyst models and institutional earnings workflows within several trading days.
factors.name: Joint Surprise Manifold Rupture Drift

factors.trading_idea: This factor treats a stock's recent price response to signed abnormal participation as a causal linear-response system rather than assuming every high-volume move is continuation or reversal. When signed volume shocks repeatedly lead same-signed returns at roughly a one-week delay, and participation exhibits concentrated periodic energy, a fresh signed participation shock should predict a same-signed six-day response because liquidity providers and benchmarked investors update inventory gradually across recurring liquidity cycles. The hypothesis is falsified if high transfer-response scores do not have positive six-day cross-sectional returns, or if the effect is equally strong when the estimated lagged response is unstable or volume lacks periodic concentration. The edge can persist because exploiting it requires warehousing inventory through the delayed response and absorbing execution risk, rather than observing a publicly known static characteristic.
factors.name: Spectral Flow Transfer Response

factors.trading_idea: Persistent downside-volatility regimes create demand for low-downside-semibeta stocks as portfolio hedges, while broad idiosyncratic fear makes that demand especially concentrated in names showing high-close, high-turnover defensive resilience. The realized negative sign of Parent B is economically consistent with low-semibeta names becoming the expensive recipients of risk-control reallocation rather than beneficiaries of a durable defensive premium. This child shorts only the overlap of low-semibeta exposure and Parent A-style expensive defensive crowding, isolating temporary hedge-demand overpricing that neither ordinary semibeta nor crowding alone can identify reliably at six bars.
factors.name: Fear Semibeta Defensive Crowding Unwind (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: A downside cascade is informative only after its peer-arrival intensity begins to decay: this is the point at which forced industry selling is being exhausted rather than accelerating. Firms that hold relative to their peers and close near the top of the bar on elevated volume are absorbing supply rather than merely receiving delayed bad news, so capital should rotate into them over the next six sessions as the contagion state normalizes. The edge persists because extinction of a clustered sell program and the identity of its absorbers are latent state variables that are not directly observable from a single stock's return, while attention-constrained investors continue to trade the industry basket after informed liquidity providers have distinguished resilient names. This is falsified if post-extinction relative resilience does not predict positive six-bar returns, or if the effect is equally strong while peer downside intensity is still accelerating.
factors.name: Peer Extinction Resilience Rotation

factors.trading_idea: The child distinguishes mechanically exhausted selling from fundamentally informed selling by conditioning sell-pressure impact curvature on the direction of recently disclosed cash-quality revisions.
