Improving cash realization combined with falling marginal downside impact indicates that liquidity suppliers are absorbing transient liquidation despite a strengthening fundamental anchor, creating a fast rebound opportunity. Conversely, deteriorating cash quality combined with rising marginal impact identifies adverse information being distributed into a thinning liquidity buffer, so downside continuation is more credible than either flow curvature or cash quality alone.
factors.name: Cash-Quality Gated Impact Release

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth shocks should disproportionately damage firms whose product economics depend on discretionary, design-intensive demand and whose capital is difficult to redeploy. The child measures nonlinear lower-tail co-crash dependence with the market rather than ordinary downside beta, then concentrates that exposure in R&D-intensive, high-margin, low-turnover businesses that proxy for product-design irreversibility. This is falsifiable: high-score firms should underperform over the next six days primarily following aggregate lower-tail events, and the effect should be weak or absent among low-R&D, high-turnover firms. The edge can persist because rare-state demand elasticity and irrecoverable product-development costs are difficult to hedge precisely, while constrained investors reduce exposure only after tail dependence becomes salient.
factors.name: Design Irreversibility Tail Dependence

factors.trading_idea: Prior clustered downside shocks and abnormally weak participation identify the forced-selling mechanism emphasized by Parent A, but a large opening gap followed by an intraday refill indicates that the selling schedule has finally met renewed buy-side depth. Parent B's resilience insight is retained through industry-relative cash-flow quality and free-cash-flow yield rather than leverage/liquidity ratios: a refill is more credible when the issuer can fund itself internally and is less likely to be repricing imminent distress. Neither parent alone distinguishes an ongoing low-volume cascade from the specific terminal state in which a fundamentally cash-generative name gaps down but liquidity replenishes during the same bar.
factors.name: Cashflow-Resilient Cascade Refill

factors.trading_idea: A local deceleration in downside excitation is ambiguous in normal markets: an upper-range close can be a temporary bounce within a continuing idiosyncratic decline, consistent with Parent A's reversed standalone sign. The interaction becomes informative when persistent market fear activates high-downside-semibeta names and the stock has already underperformed its semibeta-implied move on abnormal volume: this identifies a mechanical, systemic deleveraging episode rather than ordinary bad-news continuation. Within that state, a fading fresh sell impulse and intraday recovery indicate that forced supply has been consumed while liquidity provision returns, creating a short-horizon repair that neither the market-fear state nor local exhaustion signal isolates alone.
factors.name: Fear-Gated Idiosyncratic Excitation Repair

factors.trading_idea: A directional, high-participation range shock is more likely to reflect persistent informed or meta-order flow when it is idiosyncratic to the stock rather than shared by its sector. Sector-wide volatility shocks can be hedged and repriced quickly, whereas a stock-specific liquidity-demand shock forces dealers and risk managers to infer whether flow is transient, causing delayed inventory adjustment and continued drift. The hypothesis is falsified if high-volume directional bars with a positive stock-versus-sector range-synchrony gap do not outperform equivalent directional bars occurring during synchronized sector volatility.
factors.name: Idiosyncratic Liquidity Synchrony Gap Drift

factors.trading_idea: A concentrated burst of trading creates a salient recent cost-basis reference even when investor-level ownership is unobserved. Prospect-theory disposition effects imply that prices materially below this high-participation reference face reduced willingness from incumbent holders to sell, while prices above it face increased realization supply; the resulting supply-elasticity asymmetry should pull prices back toward the reference over the next six sessions. This is falsified if reference-price deviations have no conditional reversal specifically when recent volume is concentrated, and it can persist because the underlying investor cost bases and willingness to realize gains or losses are latent and costly for arbitrageurs to identify in real time.
factors.name: Salient Cost-Basis Anchor

factors.trading_idea: Concordant EPS and revenue surprises are more likely to represent a genuine change in firm fundamentals than a one-metric accounting distortion. When such a disclosure arrives with unusually low relative trading activity, the market has received the information but attention and institutional processing are incomplete, so repricing should diffuse over the following week rather than occur entirely on the event day. The edge persists because low event participation identifies issuer-specific information that is publicly available but not yet broadly incorporated by capital-constrained investors; it is falsified if low-turnover concordant surprises are fully incorporated by the next close or reverse over the subsequent six bars.
factors.name: Quiet Attention Surprise Diffusion

factors.trading_idea: Under a heavy-tailed consumption-growth process, an unusually strong reported sales outcome can reflect a transitory tail realization rather than a persistent upward shift in demand. Investors and analysts tend to classify a positive revenue surprise as uniformly good news, but a contemporaneous deterioration in operating-cash-flow conversion reveals that the sales increment is not being collected or monetized at the same rate; this should trigger a relatively fast reassessment after the filing. The edge persists because quarterly cash conversion is less salient than the headline surprise and requires combining two accounting statements at the event date. It is falsified if, conditional on a fresh positive revenue surprise, deteriorating cash conversion does not predict lower industry-relative six-day returns.
factors.name: Tail Demand Cash-Conversion Break

factors.trading_idea: During broad fear episodes, a negative stock-specific residual relative to its own fear beta is most likely temporary when the firm has strong liquidity, debt-service capacity, cash generation, and low net leverage. Conversely, a fragile firm that resists the fear selloff can be an unfinished financing-risk reallocation rather than genuine strength. The interaction creates edge because fear-beta residuals identify the immediate dislocation while financing resilience determines whether that dislocation should repair or continue.
factors.name: Fear-Beta Financing Mismatch Repair (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: Clusters of same-signed peer earnings surprises act as a cross-exciting information process: repeated reports make the industry implication more credible and prompt rapid comparable-company repricing. The child targets firms with no own release whose idiosyncratic price and volume participation remain muted relative to this freshly accelerating peer-news intensity, identifying an analyst-attention and portfolio-implementation queue rather than a slow generic peer relay. This is falsified if, conditional on no own event, low-participation laggards following coherent peer-surprise clusters do not outperform already participating peers in the signed direction over the next six days. The edge can persist because interpreting cross-firm read-throughs and reallocating diversified industry books is costly, while clustered disclosures create a short-lived coordination catalyst that is difficult to fully arbitrage immediately.
factors.name: Peer Surprise Attention Queue

factors.trading_idea: Information and institutional sector reallocations diffuse unevenly across firms: a broad positive industry impulse is incorporated first in liquid or salient peers, while temporarily lagging members catch up over subsequent sessions. The child goes long stocks whose own three-day return lags a leave-one-out industry-peer return, but only insofar as the peer move is positive relative to the market and broadly shared across the industry. This should persist because portfolio-manager attention, peer-comparison workflows, and constrained rebalancing operate with delay; it is falsifiable because the premium should disappear when the peer impulse is nonpositive or concentrated in only a small fraction of peers.
factors.name: Leave-One-Out Industry Impulse Lag

factors.trading_idea: A directional, unusually high-volume bar is treated as an observable forcing impulse, while each stock's trailing lagged response coefficient measures whether its prices historically absorb such impulses with delay rather than immediately. Stocks with positive excess-volume pressure and a strong positive one-day flow-to-return transfer coefficient should continue to adjust over the next week; the converse holds for negative pressure or negative transfer coefficients. This is falsifiable: the signal should fail when the pressure sequence is time-shuffled within stock, and its effect should be concentrated in names whose returns lag their own signed-volume impulses. The edge can persist because the lag arises from fragmented execution, delayed portfolio rebalancing, and intermittent liquidity provision, none of which can be eliminated cheaply by trading on a single daily bar.
factors.name: Lagged Flow-Response Susceptibility

factors.trading_idea: Multi-day institutional execution schedules generate repeated, same-signed intraday price pressure when participation is elevated, because large investors split orders across sessions rather than completing them immediately. The child explicitly removes gap-led moves: overnight gaps are more likely to be discrete information incorporation, while continuous-session pressure is more consistent with unfinished execution demand and should continue over the next six bars. The edge persists because dealers and liquidity providers cannot instantaneously absorb a persistent metaorder without taking inventory risk; it is falsifiable because follow-through should be concentrated in high-participation, directionally coherent, intraday-dominant episodes and disappear for otherwise similar gap-driven moves.
factors.name: Auction-Filtered Intraday Execution Pressure

factors.trading_idea: Clustered directional abnormal volume with muted price impact identifies an absorbed latent metaorder, but this signal is ambiguous when the move is an idiosyncratic liquidity shock. The child conditions that unfinished-order state on a cohesive residual-return peer network: continuation is strongest when the peer mode independently moves in the same direction, confirming that the flow is informed by a shared industry, supply-chain, or institutional-information shock. Opposite peer-mode movement suppresses the trade because the same muted-impact flow is then more likely to be a temporary relative dislocation that should repair rather than continue.
factors.name: Network-Confirmed Metaorder Absorption Drift

factors.trading_idea: Broad clustering of idiosyncratic downside realizations is a daily-market proxy for heightened concern about heavy-tailed consumption-growth states, during which investor attention and risk-bearing capacity are scarce. In those states, a newly disclosed positive earnings or revenue surprise is incorporated more slowly when it is credible but not immediately easy to finance or arbitrage; cash-rich firms provide the cleanest credibility signal because their positive surprise is less likely to be offset by refinancing risk. The hypothesis is falsifiable: the cash-backed surprise signal should have positive 6-day IC primarily following unusually broad tail-cluster days, with materially weaker IC after ordinary cross-sectional downside breadth. The edge can persist because it requires jointly identifying a latent aggregate tail state, release freshness, and balance-sheet credibility rather than trading a standalone earnings-surprise anomaly.
factors.name: Tail-Cluster Cash-Backed Surprise Diffusion

factors.trading_idea: Persistent sell pressure is not uniformly informative: when repeated downside, volume-marked bars produce progressively smaller incremental price damage, liquidity suppliers are absorbing a likely mechanical liquidation flow and a rebound becomes likely once the flow exhausts. Conversely, increasing marginal price impact for comparable sell-pressure marks indicates a thinning liquidity buffer and predicts continued downside. This is falsifiable if the estimated impact curvature does not separate subsequent returns after controlling for recent return, volatility, and volume; it can persist because liquidation programs, benchmarked managers, and short-sale constraints prevent arbitrageurs from cheaply taking the other side before the forced flow ends.
factors.name: Sell-Pressure Impact Curvature Release (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: Broad market drawdowns propagate unevenly because firms with slow inventory conversion, weak cash buffers, and high debt must finance working capital precisely when external funding becomes scarce. These firms face delayed de-risking by lenders and investors, so their relative underperformance should continue over the following week rather than be fully incorporated on the first common-shock day. This is falsifiable: conditional on a statistically large trailing market drawdown, the high-fragility portfolio should underperform the low-fragility portfolio, while the spread should be materially weaker in non-stress periods; the edge persists because systemic funding constraints make immediate arbitrage capital-intensive and correlated across investors.
factors.name: Systemic Inventory Funding Fragility

factors.trading_idea: The parent waits for slow volatility relaxation, which explains why its payoff accumulates more strongly beyond six days. This child instead identifies the terminal bar of a self-excited liquidation episode: conditional on recently elevated marked downside-event intensity, downside pressure arrives far below expectation while turnover is abnormally high and the close recovers away from the low. That combination is evidence that forced supply has been absorbed rather than merely paused, so dealer inventory replenishment and removal of marginal sellers should produce an earlier six-day rebound; the effect persists because the identity and urgency of forced sellers are not directly observable from daily bars.
factors.name: Conditional Hawkes Extinction Rebound

factors.trading_idea: A close near the daily high after a large downside excursion is not necessarily genuine absorption: when it occurs amid an already clustered sequence of downside shocks and unusually high participation, it can be a temporary dealer-facilitated bounce during an unfinished institutional sell program. Execution constraints, benchmarked liquidation schedules, and limited displayed depth prevent such flow from being immediately arbitraged away, so the residual selling pressure should depress returns over the next six sessions. This hypothesis is falsified if high-scoring recovery bounces in high-participation downside clusters subsequently outperform rather than underperform the cross-section.
factors.name: Recovery Bounce Sell-Schedule Continuation

factors.trading_idea: Sector information diffusion is fastest during the ignition phase of clustered peer shocks: a sequence of same-signed abnormal sector moves raises the near-term probability that remaining members will receive the same information or correlated order flow. The factor buys illiquid names whose three-day return has not caught up with their beta-implied peer-sector move, and shorts names that have overshot, but only when a fast exponentially decayed shock intensity is accelerating relative to its slower baseline. The edge should persist because fragmented attention, inventory constraints, and delayed risk transfer prevent immediate arbitrage across every sector constituent; it is falsified if residual gaps do not close over six bars specifically during positive excitation-acceleration states.
factors.name: Sector Excitation Ignition Gap

factors.trading_idea: A temporary impact overshoot is most likely to reverse when it occurs inside a sector-localized liquidity event: the stock has an abnormal range-and-volume shock that its sector basket does not share, so the move cannot be cleanly interpreted as a sector repricing. Parent A supplies the signed reversal leg and isolation test for a replenishable impact shock, while Parent B supplies the hedgeability state variable identifying whether the disturbance is name-specific rather than sector-wide. The interaction has edge because localized abnormal activity alone did not reliably imply continuation, but localizedness makes an otherwise ambiguous impact overshoot more likely to reflect a finite dealer-inventory imbalance that repairs over the six-bar horizon.
factors.name: Sector-Localized Impact Reversal (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: A consensus revision accompanied by muted-impact directional volume is most credible when that volume runs against a recently disclosed corporate float shock: buying despite issuance or selling despite buybacks cannot be mechanically attributed to the issuer's own supply program. The float shock is scaled by turnover-implied absorption time, so the signal emphasizes names where the countervailing corporate flow creates an inventory-reset state and delays price discovery. Parent A alone can mistake corporate rebalancing for informed flow, while Parent B alone has no reliable directional effect; their interaction isolates revision-consistent investor demand strong enough to overwhelm the disclosed mechanical flow.
factors.name: Counterflow Float-Reset Revision Drift

factors.trading_idea: A fresh issuance or buyback disclosure is not itself reliably directional: issuance can finance valuable investment and buybacks can reveal management defensiveness, explaining Parent B's failed unconditional sign. The disclosure becomes useful as a state variable when its implied corporate-flow direction agrees with a one-sided, volume-marked Hawkes burst that is elevated but cooling: this identifies a likely mechanical placement or repurchase program rather than a fundamental repricing. Once that aligned program nears completion and range compresses, transient impact reverses, so the child trades against the observed flow; neither parent alone distinguishes this terminal mechanical-flow subset.
factors.name: Disclosed Supply-Aligned Hawkes Reversal

factors.trading_idea: Volume-leading range hysteresis identifies demand arriving before liquidity providers have fully repriced inventory risk, while a positive stock-versus-sector range gap distinguishes isolated flow from common sector information. Parent B's realized negative sign is consistent with these isolated directional shocks being temporary liquidity vacuums or forced-flow episodes: because peers do not validate the repricing, dealers can replenish once the flow is diagnosed, reversing the close-location move. The interaction therefore targets the subset of hysteretic pressure that looks like a false idiosyncratic ignition, rather than treating all volume-range lead episodes as persistent demand.
factors.name: Idiosyncratic Hysteresis False-Ignition Reversal

factors.trading_idea: Peer earnings surprises act as source events, while a newly changed consensus EPS estimate for an unreleased target is the marked arrival event that reveals analysts have begun transmitting the peer information into that stock's valuation. Conditioning on a concordant target revision should pull the information-transfer clock forward relative to a raw peer-surprise relay, leaving a six-day continuation as further analysts and portfolio managers update. This is falsified if, among no-own-report stocks, newly arriving estimate revisions concordant with a recent industry peer-surprise impulse do not outperform discordant or unconfirmed peer impulses over the next six days. The edge can persist because comparable-company model updates are staggered across analysts and are costly to aggregate immediately, especially when several peer reports must be translated into firm-specific earnings implications.
factors.name: Marked Peer Revision Cross-Excitation

factors.trading_idea: The child forecasts the currently persistent common premium across quality, conservative-investment, balance-sheet-safety, and value sleeves, then conditions each stock's style exposure on whether it has already over-captured its industry's recent upside. At the fixed six-bar horizon, unusually strong peer-upside capture appears to be a crowded, short-run exhaustion state rather than pure continuation; the signal therefore prefers fundamentally mode-favoured names that have lagged peer upside participation, while fading fundamentally unfavoured names with exhausted relative participation. Neither parent alone distinguishes a broadly rewarded fundamental style from the cross-sectional timing of idiosyncratic peer-momentum exhaustion.
factors.name: Fundamental Mode Peer-Exhaustion Handoff (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: An earnings/revenue surprise is a common information shock, but its propagation through analyst revisions and investor attention should be more persistent when the firm's growth is visibly financed by operating cash flow rather than issuance or debt expansion. The child only carries underreacted surprise exposure when that self-financing state is strong: credibility makes the reported news more likely to represent durable operating information, while a muted same-day reaction identifies the portion not yet incorporated. Parent A alone is too slow and broad, and Parent B alone treats all confirmed surprises as equally trustworthy; their interaction targets delayed assimilation specifically for financially credible reports.
factors.name: Cash-Credible Surprise Propagation

factors.trading_idea: A newly reported, large share-repurchase outlay relative to the stock's normal dollar turnover reveals an active corporate demand program whose likely execution horizon is long compared with one trading day. Unlike a generic value or reversal signal, the relevant state variable is the inferred execution clock: large disclosed buyback capacity combined with limited market turnover implies persistent, price-insensitive demand over the next several sessions. This is falsifiable if fresh repurchase disclosures with high repurchase-to-ADV ratios do not outperform equally recent filings with little or no repurchase activity; the effect can persist because exact corporate execution schedules are opaque, institutions face front-running and mandate constraints, and the demand is mechanically distributed through time rather than immediately incorporated into price.
factors.name: Reported Buyback Execution Clock

factors.trading_idea: Information shocks diffuse across economically related firms when an industry move is broad and directionally coherent, but individual names with unusually low trading participation may incorporate that information only gradually. The child estimates each stock's trailing sensitivity to lagged leave-one-out industry-peer returns, then trades the current peer-versus-own return gap only where that lead-lag relation has been reliably positive. The edge should persist because attention, analyst coverage, and portfolio-rebalancing capacity are allocated unevenly across names; it is falsified if low-participation laggards do not converge toward coherent peer moves over the next six sessions after conditioning on historical lead-lag reliability.
factors.name: Industry Lead-Lag Attention Deficit

factors.trading_idea: A coherent EPS-and-revenue surprise supplies a signed fundamental anchor, while a newly accelerating high-volume flow burst in the opposite direction identifies forced rebalancing or inventory transfer rather than informed disagreement. Parent B's adverse realized sign is consistent with directional fresh absorbed flow being transient liquidity demand that subsequently reverses; conditioning that reversal on an independently signed earnings shock makes the release tradeable in the surprise direction rather than blindly following flow. The interaction isolates early, temporarily absorbed opposition before it becomes a mature cascade, allowing the information anchor to dominate over the six-day adjustment horizon.
factors.name: Coherent Surprise Fresh-Opposition Release

factors.trading_idea: A sales- and cash-flow-positive result relative to headline EPS is not reliably bullish over six days: the headline earnings miss can focus institutional attention on margin deterioration, working-capital timing, or future investment needs that are not captured by the initially reassuring cash and revenue components. When this disclosure wedge coincides with a regular, elevated sell schedule whose price impact is compressing, the low impact is interpreted as patient informed distribution being absorbed rather than completed forced selling. The interaction carries edge because the accounting conflict identifies a reason for reassessment while the execution state identifies that sophisticated investors are still implementing the negative interpretation.
factors.name: Cash-Sales Wedge Informed Sell Assimilation

factors.trading_idea: Analysts and growth-oriented investors may extrapolate revenue-estimate improvements before recognizing that reported growth is being financed by slower customer collections. Firms with favorable revenue-consensus revisions but unusually rapid receivables growth relative to revenue and weakening operating-cash-flow conversion are vulnerable to a short-horizon reassessment; the converse represents underappreciated cash-backed growth. Limits to arbitrage arise because quarterly working-capital evidence is less salient and less comparable than headline estimates, while the mechanism is falsified if the quality-adjusted revision spread has no incremental predictive power versus estimate changes alone.
factors.name: Receivable-Backed Revision Fragility

factors.trading_idea: A downside return normally raises expected volatility through the leverage and bad-news asymmetry, but an unusually large downside range relative to the stock's own pre-shock downside and range state is more likely to reflect a temporary liquidity vacuum. When the close finishes well above the intraday low, the selling shock has been absorbed rather than continuously repriced, so inventory replenishment and volatility mean reversion should support returns over the following week. This is falsified if stocks with large conditional downside-range innovations and high close-location do not outperform after controlling for contemporaneous idiosyncratic return and realized range; the edge can persist because liquidity replenishment and forced-sale completion are slower than the daily shock that creates the dislocation.
factors.name: Downside Range Innovation Absorption Release

factors.trading_idea: A coherent earnings-and-revenue surprise is more likely to propagate into a six-day repricing when market returns are highly synchronized, because common-shock regimes suppress idiosyncratic liquidity provision and make investors rapidly differentiate firms by financial resilience. Positive report impulses should transmit most strongly for cash-generative, conservatively financed firms with credibly funded repurchases, while negative impulses should transmit most strongly for financially fragile firms. Neither parent alone isolates this event-level cross-excitation channel: synchrony identifies when systemic attention is concentrated, while the resilience and surprise interaction identifies which names receive the asymmetric repricing.
factors.name: Synchrony-Conditioned Resilient Surprise Transmission

factors.trading_idea: Investors respond quickly to the headline EPS surprise but are slower to assess whether the surprise is economically credible when consensus has been stale. A positive surprise corroborated by operating cash flow and stable working-capital quality should continue to drift upward, while a negative cash-confirmed surprise should drift downward. The signal should fail if post-release returns are equally strong for fresh and stale consensus names, or if cash-flow corroboration adds no incremental explanatory power beyond EPS surprise.
factors.name: Stale-Consensus Cash-Confirmed Surprise

factors.trading_idea: A broad joint range-and-volume shock can reflect market-wide liquidity withdrawal, but the next-day normalization of trading activity identifies the subset of moves most likely caused by completed forced flow rather than continuing information arrival. The child isolates stock-specific displacement relative to its sector and only fades it when both the market-wide shock and the stock's own liquidity recovery are observed. The edge can persist because public daily bars reveal completed stress only imperfectly, while dealers' inventory replenishment and the completion of institutional basket trades remain latent; it is falsified if sector-residual moves continue rather than reverse following synchronized shock recovery.
factors.name: Systemic Liquidity Recovery Residual Reversal

factors.trading_idea: Sparse-liquidity names underreact to a liquid leave-one-out sector shock because price discovery and arbitrage capital arrive with delay. The child trades that beta-adjusted diffusion gap only when the lagging firm has a credible cash-funded repurchase state and sector-relative value support, making the catch-up more likely to be reinforced by a natural marginal buyer rather than representing fragile contagion. Parent B supplies a fast, tradable propagation clock, while Parent A distinguishes which apparent sector lags have financially credible demand behind their eventual completion.
factors.name: Credible Sparse-Liquidity Completion

factors.trading_idea: Fundamental surprises are normally informative, but their initial price response is unreliable when a sector-wide liquidity shock forces correlated trading and temporarily overwhelms name-specific information. The child buys positive-surprise names that suffer an idiosyncratic sector-relative selloff during synchronized thin-liquidity stress, and shorts negative-surprise names experiencing the symmetric forced uplift. Parent A identifies overshoots without knowing whether the displaced name has fundamental support, while Parent B identifies delayed news conversion without distinguishing a name-level thin book from a sector-wide forced-flow episode; their interaction isolates fundamentally anchored dislocations likely to repair within the fixed six-bar horizon.
factors.name: News-Synchrony Forced-Flow Conversion (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: Quarterly surprises are a common information shock, but their six-day diffusion depends jointly on whether the reported growth narrative was credibly self-financed before the release and whether the market initially absorbed the news weakly. Positive surprises from firms with cash-supported growth should continue to diffuse when the initial price reaction is muted, while negative surprises from externally financed growers should unravel as investors reassess a fragile expansion narrative. Neither financing quality alone nor surprise direction alone identifies this delayed-assimilation state: the interaction isolates credible or fragile information that has not yet been fully incorporated into price.
factors.name: Credible Surprise Muted Assimilation

factors.trading_idea: Concave sell-pressure impact is most bullish when a fresh improvement in cash realization indicates that the selling is likely mechanical rather than fundamental: orderly, low-entropy downside flow is being absorbed despite improving cash backing. Conversely, accelerating downside impact after a fresh cash-quality deterioration is more likely informed distribution and should continue. The interaction carries edge because impact curvature identifies whether the sell program is exhausting or destabilizing liquidity, while the cash revision distinguishes forced liquidation from justified repricing.
factors.name: Cash-Anchored Orderly Liquidation Release

factors.trading_idea: Persistent high-volume down-arrival intensity distinguishes a continuing supply imbalance from an isolated bad bar, while sector liquidity synchrony identifies when that imbalance is likely generated by ETF redemption, deleveraging, or common liquidity-provider withdrawal rather than firm-specific information. The child buys the names with the deepest sector-relative selloff only when their negative arrival clock is elevated and their sector is simultaneously undergoing an abnormal liquidity-stress episode. Neither parent alone separates persistent informed selling from persistent but mechanically forced sector-wide liquidation; their interaction targets the latter's short-horizon repair.
factors.name: Synchronized Sell-Arrival Repair (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: A genuine industry innovation should be incorporated into each constituent according to that stock's pre-shock sensitivity to the leave-one-out industry return, rather than according to an equal-weight peer move. A large common innovation combined with a negative beta-adjusted residual identifies a stock that has absorbed less of the shared information than its historical linkage implies, creating a six-day catch-up opportunity as portfolio hedgers and slower investors update exposures. This is falsifiable: forward returns should be monotonic in the signed residual only on unusually large peer innovations, should weaken after controlling for the stock's industry beta, and should be absent on ordinary idiosyncratic-return days; the delay persists because beta estimation, basket rebalancing, and cross-name information processing are costly for fragmented portfolios.
factors.name: Beta-Adjusted Common Innovation Gap

factors.trading_idea: The parent's positive realized IC implies that daily high-volume selling during market fear is more often a temporary liquidity-demand shock than continuing informed liquidation: investors demanding immediacy pay a price concession that subsequently reverses. This child preserves the marked sell-intensity and fear-state measurement, but concentrates it in firms with high operating returns, ample current liquidity, and low leverage, where severe fundamental deterioration is less plausible and the price concession is more likely transitory. The edge should persist because forced redemptions, deleveraging, and dealer inventory constraints create short-lived price pressure that arbitrageurs cannot absorb without capital, volatility, and gap-risk exposure. It is falsified if, conditional on broad fear, high-quality firms with unusually elevated marked sell intensity do not outperform their sector over the next six sessions relative to similarly shocked low-quality firms.
factors.name: Fundamental Panic Liquidity Rebound

factors.trading_idea: A coherent EPS-and-revenue surprise is most informative when it confirms an already active analyst-consensus revision that the sector-relative price has not yet absorbed. The event is weighted by free-cash-flow support net of debt issuance, because self-funded firms can translate validated earnings information into durable capital allocation while debt-dependent issuers face rational skepticism. This interaction differs from either parent alone: the surprise supplies a fresh public catalyst, the revision-price gap identifies delayed assimilation, and funding credibility separates persistent repricing from fragile headline reactions.
factors.name: Cash-Credible Surprise Revision Gap

factors.trading_idea: Analyst revisions before an earnings release encode gradual private-model updating, while a subsequent earnings surprise in the same direction validates that information and induces a rapid second-stage repricing. The child focuses on this confirmation pulse rather than holding an ambiguity signal until a later consensus update: it is strongest when the release-day price move is muted despite unusually high trading participation, suggesting that informed attention has arrived but institutional portfolio adjustment is incomplete. The edge should persist for roughly one trading week because model confirmation and mandate-driven rebalancing are sequential, whereas it should fail when pre-report revisions and realized surprises disagree or when the announcement is already fully priced on the release day.
factors.name: Pre-Report Revision Confirmation Pulse

factors.trading_idea: Persistent directional participation that closes repeatedly near one end of the daily range is a coarse daily-bar signature of a parent order being split across sessions. When that participation produces unusually little range per unit of relative volume, liquidity is absorbing the flow rather than immediately clearing it, leaving inventory pressure and information to be incorporated over the next week. The edge should persist because the latent metaorder and dealer inventory transfer are not directly observable from daily bars; it is falsified if coherent directional participation with compressed impact does not outperform either incoherent participation or comparable high-impact flow at six bars.
factors.name: Coherent Participation Absorption Drift

factors.trading_idea: During a broad industry sell cascade, an earnings surprise is not interpreted uniformly: a positive surprise is more investable when the firm has liquidity and debt-service capacity to exploit the dislocation, while a negative surprise is more damaging for financially fragile firms facing refinancing and cash-flow constraints. The interaction creates a credibility-and-survival sort within the same peer shock, separating firms that can absorb sector-level forced selling from those whose new earnings information accelerates a funding-driven withdrawal. Neither parent alone distinguishes whether a surprise can be financed through stress or whether a strong balance sheet changes the market's interpretation of that surprise.
factors.name: Buffered Earnings Peer-Cascade Sort

factors.trading_idea: A positive EPS surprise with weak top-line confirmation is not necessarily a deteriorating margin signal: when it is supported by positive cash earnings quality, it can reveal operational efficiency that is costly for analysts to model quickly. The effect should be strongest where the EPS consensus has been stale before the release and the same-day price reaction is muted, indicating information avoidance rather than a fully anticipated result. The child predicts positive six-bar drift because subsequent analyst model revisions and investor reassessment of durable cost structure arrive after the headline; it is falsifiable if this conditional group does not outperform other positive EPS-surprise reporters over the following six bars.
factors.name: Estimate-Stasis Cash-Validated Efficiency Drift

factors.trading_idea: A negative sector shock is more likely to propagate with delay into firms whose apparent EPS growth is driven by debt-financed buybacks rather than cash-supported operating improvement. Sparse contemporaneous trading leaves these fragile names temporarily underreacting to the sector decline, while their weak financing capacity makes subsequent benchmark hedging, risk reassessment, and deleveraging disproportionately negative. Parent A alone does not identify which underresponders have a fundamental reason for a persistent downside repricing, while Parent B alone is a slow-moving disclosure state without a market catalyst or transmission-timing signal.
factors.name: Buyback-Fragility Downside Relay

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-demand shocks can produce unusually large reported sales outcomes that investors initially extrapolate as persistent firm-specific growth. A positive sales surprise with worsening cash conversion is particularly likely to be a low-quality or transitory realization; when it also receives an unusually strong same-day price reaction, the market has rapidly embedded that optimistic interpretation and the reassessment should occur within the fixed six-bar horizon. The edge persists because investors react to the salient headline and price move before incorporating the less salient cash-collection evidence across financial statements. This is falsified if, conditional on a fresh sales beat and cash-conversion deterioration, stronger standardized announcement-day returns do not predict more negative subsequent industry-relative returns.
factors.name: Tail Sales Cash Overshoot Reversal

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s robust negative IC indicates that value-aligned relative-price moves are more often crowded, temporary flow episodes than gradual information incorporation at the six-bar horizon. When a cheap stock rises or an expensive stock falls on unusually high price impact per traded dollar, constrained liquidity providers are likely absorbing one-sided rebalancing demand; the subsequent partial unwind should reverse the aligned move. This edge can persist because delegated value and momentum rebalancing is gradual while balance-sheet-constrained liquidity suppliers cannot immediately arbitrage the transient dislocation; it is falsified if high-impact aligned moves continue more strongly than ordinary aligned moves over the next six bars.
factors.name: Liquidity-Gated Valuation Path Correction

factors.trading_idea: A positive revenue surprise with receivables and inventory growth outrunning sales identifies a disclosure whose headline optimism is economically fragile, but it does not by itself establish whether the ensuing price decline is still informative or already overdone. The realized positive direction of Parent B is consistent with abnormal volume-marked selling under market fear being a capitulation/liquidity-demand state rather than persistent informed selling: constrained sellers can push prices below the value implied even by poor cash conversion. The child therefore goes long the intersection of a fresh adverse cash-quality headline and fear-gated sell-pressure exhaustion; Parent A alone misses when the bad news is already over-discounted, while Parent B alone lacks a concrete accounting catalyst that identifies unusually vulnerable names for an overshoot-and-rebound.
factors.name: Cash-Quality Capitulation Rebound

factors.trading_idea: Broad, same-direction flow across economically close industry peers is more likely to represent a distributed institutional theme than a single-stock shock. Firms without a recent earnings disclosure have less firm-specific information to counteract that thematic demand, so they are more susceptible to delayed cross-excitation and should catch up in the peer-flow direction. The edge persists because portfolio-manager rebalancing, differentiated liquidity, and slow fundamental-information processing distribute thematic orders across constituents over several sessions; it is falsified if broad peer flow has no incremental six-bar predictive power among firms with stale earnings information after sector demeaning.
factors.name: Industry Breadth Stale-Information Relay (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: A volume-confirmed sector shock is a common-information impulse, but firms differ in their empirically estimated delayed admittance to such impulses because exposure mapping, investor attention, and liquidity provision are not updated simultaneously. The factor buys stocks with a positive historical delayed transfer response to an upward sector impulse (and shorts the converse), only when their current idiosyncratic response has not already acknowledged that impulse. This is falsifiable: conditional on large sector-return and sector-volume innovations, the high-minus-low admittance-gap portfolio should earn its return primarily over the next six sessions, while the effect should be absent after low-volume sector moves; it can persist because estimating a time-varying impulse-response profile requires event history and exposes arbitrageurs to sector-shock reversal risk.
factors.name: Volume-Confirmed Sector Admittance Gap

factors.trading_idea: Broad, contemporaneous downside-volume participation within an industry is more consistent with basket, ETF, or risk-budget liquidation than with a firm-specific information event. A focal stock that also trades under downside pressure but closes near the top of its range has revealed latent demand capable of absorbing that non-informational supply, so its price should repair over the next six sessions. The edge persists because investors cannot cheaply distinguish forced common flow from informed selling in real time, while liquidity providers need time and balance-sheet capacity to replenish inventory; it is falsified if high-close-location names fail to outperform weak absorbers during equally broad peer sell episodes.
factors.name: Broad Peer-Flow Absorption Repair

factors.trading_idea: A positive EPS surprise should continue to drift only when subsequent analyst revisions to both EPS and revenue estimates agree, indicating that investors are updating beliefs about broad operating strength rather than a transitory accounting or margin effect. The signal concentrates on confirmed beats whose initial two-day price response remains muted, where public analyst revisions have begun to validate the news but broad portfolio rebalancing and estimate dissemination are incomplete. This is falsifiable: conditional on a fresh positive EPS surprise, six-bar forward returns should rise monotonically with the minimum of EPS- and revenue-consensus revisions and should be strongest following below-median initial price reactions. The edge can persist because cross-channel estimate reconciliation is dispersed across analysts and slow-moving institutional processes, whereas headline earnings trading is immediate.
factors.name: Post-Earnings Revision Coherence

factors.trading_idea: Volatility-targeting and risk-control investors reduce exposures after a sustained rise in broad downside volatility, and the selling is concentrated in stocks with high trailing downside semibeta rather than high ordinary beta. The child therefore goes long sector-relative defensive names only when a five-day downside-volatility burst is both elevated versus its own trailing baseline and persistent across multiple down days; the delayed implementation of institutional de-risking is expected to fit the fixed six-bar horizon. This is falsified if high-downside-semibeta stocks do not underperform their defensive sector peers during activated fear regimes, or if the spread is equally strong outside those regimes. The edge can persist because dynamic-risk mandates must transact after realized volatility is observed and cannot instantly transfer risk to slower-moving discretionary capital.
factors.name: Fear-Regime Semibeta Rebalance

factors.trading_idea: Repeated high-volume closes at one end of the range are interpreted as a self-exciting execution cluster, but a falling directional excitation rate identifies the completion phase rather than continuing informed demand. At completion, dealers and liquidity providers who accumulated inventory while absorbing the cluster can unwind it, so exhausted buy-side clusters should underperform and exhausted sell-side clusters should outperform over the next six sessions. This is falsified if conditional six-day returns do not move opposite to the signed decelerating intensity, or if the same relation is equally strong during accelerating clusters; the edge can persist because daily-bar participants observe the pressure but cannot directly observe its latent execution-age or dealer inventory state.
factors.name: Decelerating Auction Excitation Release

factors.trading_idea: A downside cascade is a repair opportunity only when the volatility/range disturbance is already showing low conditional persistence: this identifies forced inventory clearing whose liquidity shock is extinguishing rather than a deleveraging process that remains active. The cascade, weak-participation, and close-at-low state from Parent A supplies evidence of unabsorbed selling, while Parent B's downside-conditioned range-persistence estimate separates transient dislocation from durable volatility pressure. Balance-sheet resilience further restricts the trade to issuers able to attract arbitrage capital, an interaction neither parent has alone because one lacks a shock-extinction test and the other lacks a forced-sale solvency context.
factors.name: Resilient Cascade Extinction Repair

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s negative realized sign suggests that abnormal range and participation are more often an exhaustion state than a continuation state at the six-day horizon. This child isolates the subset with low directional efficiency: unusually high volume and range, but only a modest open-to-close displacement relative to the full intraday range, indicating two-sided liquidation and dealer inventory absorption rather than information-rich repricing. The falsifiable prediction is that large positive (negative) intraday displacements in this inefficient-climax state reverse over the next six sessions, while efficient high-volume directional moves do not. The effect can persist because inventory replenishment and the unwinding of forced or urgency-driven flow occur over several daily bars, whereas arbitrageurs face adverse-selection risk in distinguishing informed moves from transient liquidity shocks in real time.
factors.name: Inefficient Climax Inventory Reversal

factors.trading_idea: A broad non-market spectral peer decline is an information shock, but a constituent can temporarily underreact when contemporaneous auction buying pressure masks the move. This masking is materially more dangerous when EPS growth is being supported by debt-financed share shrinkage and weak free-cash-flow backing: the peer shock makes the latent financing fragility salient, so the initially resilient price should relay downward over the next six bars. Neither peer lag alone distinguishes a transient idiosyncratic divergence from a vulnerable balance-sheet repricing, nor does buyback fragility alone provide the timing catalyst and directional anchor.
factors.name: Spectral Buyback-Masked Downside Relay

factors.trading_idea: A fresh earnings surprise is more likely to generate delayed price discovery when unusually large dollar-volume arrives without a commensurate intraday range expansion: this is consistent with institutional implementation being absorbed by latent liquidity rather than immediately clearing the market. The signal carries the signed surprise forward for several days, because liquidity providers and slower allocators adjust inventory and execution schedules gradually after an information event. The edge should persist because the relevant latent-demand and absorption state is not directly observable from daily bars and because immediate arbitrage is capacity constrained around event-driven volume. It is falsified if signed surprises with high volume-to-range absorption do not exhibit stronger six-day continuation than equally sized surprises with immediate range expansion.
factors.name: Surprise Absorption Implementation Drift

factors.trading_idea: Broad fear episodes force systematic de-risking, but stocks that recover from their intraday lows while market-wide negative breadth remains elevated reveal immediate absorption by patient buyers rather than merely low historical fear beta. This resilience should attract additional defensive and risk-managed capital over the following week as allocators distinguish names with real-time demand from names still subject to forced liquidation. The edge is falsified if, conditional on elevated market fear, high-resilience names do not outperform low-resilience names over six daily bars; it persists because absorbing stressed supply requires balance-sheet capacity and cannot be instantaneously arbitraged without bearing crash-state inventory risk.
factors.name: Fear-Breadth Intraday Resilience Rotation

factors.trading_idea: A negative sector-tail shock becomes a self-reinforcing selling cascade when financially fragile firms also have optimistic revenue revisions unsupported by collections and operating cash flow. The accounting signal identifies firms whose headline growth narrative is vulnerable, while the balance-sheet and downside-sector-exposure state identifies when that vulnerability is likely to be forcefully repriced rather than remain ignored. Neither parent alone distinguishes ordinary receivables-based revision fragility from the subset exposed to a contemporaneous, contagion-like sector deleveraging regime.
factors.name: Sector Shock Cash-Flow Fragility Cascade

factors.trading_idea: An EPS-consensus revision is most predictive when the sector-relative price has not yet acknowledged it, but the posterior reliability of that revision depends on the firm's capital-allocation state. Upward revisions should diffuse more persistently for cheap firms executing cash-funded repurchases, whereas downward revisions are more damaging for expensive firms whose per-share support relies on debt-funded buybacks. The interaction carries edge because the revision supplies new information, the funding state determines whether that information validates or breaks the capital-allocation narrative, and the muted relative-price response identifies the portion still unassimilated.
factors.name: Funding-State Revision Assimilation Gap

factors.trading_idea: A sustained excess share of volume on down bars, combined with unusually regular participation and muted contemporaneous price impact, is a daily-bar signature of a sliced institutional sell program being temporarily absorbed by liquidity providers. Unlike the parent’s single-day recovery event, this child measures a multi-session inventory-transfer state, so the expected price response can persist into the fixed six-day horizon as dealer inventory is redistributed and hidden supply continues. The edge should persist because the underlying parent order is concealed, completion timing is uncertain, and arbitraging the signal requires bearing adverse-selection and inventory risk. It is falsified if names with high down-volume concentration, regular volume cadence, and compressed impact subsequently outperform rather than underperform over six sessions.
factors.name: Cadenced Down-Volume Impact Deficit

factors.trading_idea: During unusually broad idiosyncratic fear, a stock that trades materially below its prior close but finishes near the top of its daily range is more likely experiencing completed forced selling and genuine risk transfer than latent adverse selection. Broad panic causes investors to reduce exposure mechanically, while the strongest intraday recoveries identify names for which institutional demand is willing to absorb supply; slower portfolio reallocation and short-covering can continue over the next week. This edge should persist because daily-bar investors cannot directly observe whether intraday selling was forced or whether absorption came from durable demand. It is falsified if, conditional on broad fear, high recovery-efficiency names do not outperform sector peers over the following six bars.
factors.name: Panic Recovery Reallocation

factors.trading_idea: A coherent, historically unusual joint EPS-and-revenue surprise establishes an idiosyncratic common-information shock, but its six-day pricing effect is strongest when the immediate high-participation order-flow cascade runs against the news. Such opposing flow is consistent with liquidity-constrained rebalancing, stale-position unwinds, or slow institutional model revision absorbing the shock rather than disproving it. The interaction has edge neither parent has alone: surprise novelty identifies when a flow imbalance is informative rather than generic, while persistent opposite-signed flow identifies delayed shock propagation rather than an already-completed earnings drift.
factors.name: Surprise-Rupture Opposing-Flow Release (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s negative realized sign suggests that a thin, upper-range close after selling is often not genuine absorption: in a self-exciting sell regime, a quiet red bar can be a temporary lull in a still-active liquidation sequence. This child explicitly distinguishes such lulls from true extinction by requiring a positive trailing propagation coefficient in standardized downside shocks; under near-critical excitation, inherited sell intensity remains likely to reignite, so the apparent intraday recovery should fail over the next six sessions. The hypothesis is falsifiable: conditional on low or negative downside-shock autocorrelation, the same thin upper-range red bars should not predict negative returns. The edge can persist because hidden execution schedules, dealer inventory constraints, and short-sale/friction costs make the latent branching state difficult to arbitrage from daily OHLCV alone.
factors.name: Near-Critical Sell Echo Failed Bounce

factors.trading_idea: A simultaneous EPS-and-revenue revision is more credible when the market is already exhibiting unusually clustered directional trading consistent with the revision, but that flow has not yet generated its normal price impact. The estimate change supplies the fundamental information direction, while muted-impact metaorder flow identifies an implementation and inventory-absorption state in which that information is still being accumulated rather than fully incorporated into price. Neither parent alone distinguishes informed revisions from weak consensus noise or directional flow from non-informational execution; their concordance isolates revisions being validated by unfinished institutional demand.
factors.name: Revision-Absorption Concordance Drift

factors.trading_idea: A positive EPS surprise generated alongside a revenue beat and improving operating profitability is more likely to reflect durable demand and operating leverage than one generated solely by temporary cost cutting. Market participants often trade the reported earnings headline before separating top-line strength from margin quality, leaving a short post-report repricing window. The hypothesis is falsified if revenue-plus-margin-confirmed surprises do not outperform equally sized EPS-only surprises over the following week.
factors.name: Top-Line and Margin Surprise Durability

factors.trading_idea: A simultaneous deterioration in receivables-to-sales and inventory-to-sales is a more credible indication of weakening customer payment capacity and demand than receivables alone. The signal is stronger when other firms in the same industry have recently disclosed receivables deterioration, indicating a common customer-credit shock, and when the focal firm has weak net short-term liquidity. This should predict negative six-day returns because sector-level credit stress is disclosed asynchronously while equity investors initially process each filing in isolation; the hypothesis is falsified if fragile firms with joint working-capital deterioration do not underperform industry peers following recent peer deterioration.
factors.name: Peer Cash-Conversion Contagion

factors.trading_idea: The apparently contradictory result in Parent A is consistent with a recovered intraday wick being temporary dealer inventory absorption rather than completed liquidation when the stock is a high conditional downside-beta vehicle. Parent B supplies the missing state variable: in broad fear, institutions continue de-risking precisely these conditional-beta exposures across subsequent sessions. Thus, a high-beta name that sells off idiosyncratically on abnormal volume but rebounds from its low is a hidden portfolio-liquidation continuation signal, whereas the same wick in a low-beta name is more likely genuine supply exhaustion.
factors.name: Conditional Beta Failed Absorption

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s negative realized IC suggests that muted-impact abnormal volume is more often the final stage of a liquidity-demand episode than evidence of an unfinished informed metaorder. When abnormal trading activity is decelerating but its recent price impact remains unusually compressed, passive liquidity providers have likely absorbed the residual inventory and the temporary signed dislocation should reverse over the next week. This is falsifiable: reversal should be concentrated in compressed-impact episodes with declining arrival intensity, while otherwise similar flow with sustained or accelerating intensity should not reverse. The edge can persist because institutional execution completion and dealer inventory rebalancing occur gradually, while daily-bar participants cannot directly observe the exhaustion state of the underlying order flow.
factors.name: Decaying-Arrival Compressed-Impact Reversal

factors.trading_idea: Persistent same-signed, high-participation intraday pressure is not necessarily evidence of unfinished informed demand: when its normalized price impact declines while participation remains high, liquidity replenishment is increasingly absorbing the execution schedule and the remaining move is predominantly temporary dealer inventory displacement. The child therefore trades against the direction of coherent pressure only in this terminal, declining-impact state, rather than flipping the parent universally. This is falsifiable: the reversal should occur after sustained participation with falling return-per-participation, but should disappear or become continuation when impact efficiency remains elevated; the edge can persist because latent execution completion and dealer inventory are not directly observable from daily bars and are costly to arbitrage under uncertain remaining order flow.
factors.name: Replenished Impact Terminal Reversal

factors.trading_idea: Analyst-consensus revisions provide a discrete public anchor for firm value, but prices need not immediately adjust in proportion to the revision when trading participation is unusually low. The signal buys stocks with a recent positive estimate revision whose industry-relative price response is weak, and shorts stocks with negative revisions whose relative price response remains too strong. This should persist because consensus changes are interpreted and implemented gradually by attention-constrained investors; it is falsified if, conditional on fresh revisions and low participation, six-day returns do not increase monotonically with the revision-minus-price-response gap.
factors.name: Estimate-Anchor Extrapolation Gap

factors.trading_idea: A correlation burst identifies an industry-contagion regime, but the parent incorrectly treated every synchronized shock as an early-stage relay. When the peer shock is accompanied by unusually high own-name participation, the contagion has already reached the stock and forced-flow, ETF hedging, and dealer inventory absorption are likely near completion; the next week should reverse the peer-shock direction. This can persist because sector-flow completion and inventory unwinds are constrained by execution risk and cannot be instantaneously arbitraged; it is falsified if the negative forward slope on peer shock is no stronger during own-volume bursts than during ordinary-volume correlation bursts.
factors.name: Saturated Industry Contagion Reversal

factors.trading_idea: The child uses Parent A's synchronized range-volume stress as an onset detector rather than a static drought level, isolating the first phase of a broad dealer-capacity withdrawal when temporary impact compression is most likely to resolve within six bars. It then applies Parent B's directional excitation and flow-implied impact deficit: clustered flow follows through when its signed return remains below the name's historical flow-to-return response, while already overpaid flow is faded. The interaction has edge because systemic onset identifies when apparent absorption is capacity-constrained rather than ordinary idiosyncratic liquidity provision, making the impact-deficit branch materially more informative.
factors.name: Systemic Onset Buffered Flow Resolution

factors.trading_idea: Sector shocks propagate through correlated names with heterogeneous execution timing: basket and index trading moves the sector first, while single-name investors and beta-targeting portfolios adjust more gradually. The signal identifies stocks whose recent return has lagged their own trailing beta-implied response to an ex-self sector shock, concentrating on statistically meaningful sector moves rather than on sparse quarterly estimate events. The edge should persist because completing a sector-level hedge in individual constituents is costly and constrained by liquidity, mandates, and delayed portfolio rebalancing; it is falsified if beta-adjusted laggards do not close their sector-response gap over the next six bars, especially following large sector shocks.
factors.name: Leave-One-Out Sector Beta Lag

factors.trading_idea: Negative-return volatility shocks are not symmetric with positive shocks: a large downside range innovation can trigger volatility-targeting deleveraging, margin pressure, and renewed risk reduction over subsequent days. The signal is long stocks whose downside range shocks decay quickly and short stocks whose downside range innovations remain elevated, conditional on a recent negative return. This mechanism would be falsified if downside range-shock persistence has no incremental relationship with forward returns after controlling for total volatility and recent return.
factors.name: Downside Range-Innovation Decay Spread (jitter) (jitter) (jitter) (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s reversed sign suggests that high-downside-semibeta stocks are not simply punished after broad fear shocks: the highest-semibeta names can outperform once mechanical volatility-targeting sales have already created an idiosyncratic overshoot. This child identifies completed rather than ongoing deleveraging by requiring a persistent market downside-volatility regime, a stock-specific return shortfall relative to its estimated downside-semibeta exposure, and abnormal trading volume. The edge should persist for roughly six days because constrained systematic sellers transact immediately after realized-risk triggers, while discretionary capital and short-covering repair the temporary residual-price dislocation more slowly; it is falsified if high-semibeta, high-volume idiosyncratic selloffs do not rebound relative to sector peers during activated fear states.
factors.name: Fear Semibeta Capitulation Repair

factors.trading_idea: Industry peers' newly released earnings surprises create a decaying fundamental-information impulse that cross-excites related stocks through analyst comparable-company revisions, supply-chain inference, and industry portfolio rebalancing. The child trades only names without a concurrent own earnings event whose idiosyncratic price response has not yet aligned with the signed peer impulse, distinguishing delayed information transmission from the parent's generic synchronized-flow reversal. This is falsified if, conditional on no own release, muted idiosyncratic responses to peer surprise impulses do not exhibit a stronger six-day return in the peer-surprise direction than already-aligned names. The edge can persist because mapping quarterly peer disclosures into firm-specific valuation implications and executing sector reallocations is costly and delayed, especially for less salient names.
factors.name: Peer Fundamental Underreaction Relay

factors.trading_idea: A latent institutional order program leaves a distinctive daily-bar footprint when signed close-location pressure is phase-aligned across short and medium scales, yet its contemporaneous price displacement remains unusually small per unit of inferred participation. This is interpreted as a liquidity reservoir absorbing an unfinished metaorder rather than a completed information shock; as the reservoir is depleted, the direction of the persistent pressure should be expressed over the following six sessions. The hypothesis is falsified if phase-aligned, under-impact buying pressure does not predict positive six-day returns, or analogous selling pressure does not predict negative returns. The effect can persist because daily OHLCV only provides a noisy proxy for hidden order flow, while trading directly against a persistent institutional program entails inventory and adverse-selection risk.
factors.name: Multiscale Participation Phase Reservoir

factors.trading_idea: Abnormal volume with little immediate price movement can represent latent institutional interest, information gathering, or early-stage order splitting rather than a completed repricing. The useful distinction is whether a name historically converts such attention-only bursts into same-signed directional moves over subsequent days; high conversion intensity should predict continuation, while low conversion intensity indicates noise or balanced liquidity provision. The edge should fail if abnormal low-range volume has no stable conditional relationship with subsequent signed returns after controlling for sector-wide activity.
factors.name: Attention-to-Price Conversion Intensity

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth risk makes clustered aggregate downside shocks more informative than isolated down days: they induce a temporary rise in demand for corporate claims that are less likely to co-crash and have stronger internally funded liquidity buffers. The child therefore goes long low conditional tail-dependence, cash-resilient firms only after a recent cluster of market-tail days, when institutional de-risking and hedge rebalancing should continue to rotate capital for roughly the next week. This edge can persist because tail dependence is estimated noisily from rare events and balance-sheet resilience is disclosed infrequently, making the conditional insurance demand difficult to arbitrage precisely. It is falsified if, after matched aggregate tail clusters, high-resilience/low-tail-dependence firms do not outperform their sector peers over the subsequent six trading days, or if the spread is equally large outside stress clusters.
factors.name: Clustered Tail Resilience Rotation

factors.trading_idea: The child treats an industry sell cascade as an endogenous, exponentially decaying sequence of peer downside arrivals rather than as a simple contemporaneous drawdown. Within that state, earnings news is sorted by the direction of a firm's financing-buffer trajectory: a positive surprise is more likely to propagate when liquidity, coverage, and cash-generation capacity are improving, while a negative surprise is more damaging when those buffers are deteriorating. The interaction carries edge because cascade intensity identifies attention-constrained contagion, while changing rather than static financial capacity identifies whether the earnings event changes the market's perceived ability to survive and finance through that contagion.
factors.name: Hawkes Buffer-Trajectory Surprise Relay

factors.trading_idea: Fresh earnings information is most valuable when an industry downside cascade has already reached a high-intensity state but its peer sell-event arrival rate is decaying: forced basket selling is then being exhausted and investors can reallocate toward the firms whose disclosure changes their relative fundamental ranking. The child requires the earnings-surprise direction to agree with name-level relative price resilience and intrabar closing pressure, distinguishing genuine information-led absorption or rejection from mechanically delayed peer-flow moves. Neither parent alone identifies this transition-specific selection: peer extinction lacks a fundamental direction, while earnings under peer stress does not distinguish an accelerating liquidation from the tradable release phase.
factors.name: Extinction-Gated Earnings Absorption

factors.trading_idea: A systemic downside-volatility burst creates forced selling most acutely in stocks with unusually high downside semibeta, but high semibeta alone cannot distinguish a completed liquidation from an unresolved risk transfer. The child requires an idiosyncratic panic-volume/range shock and then uses the close location to determine whether that selling was absorbed by buyers or accepted at lower prices. This interaction has edge because Parent A identifies where deleveraging pressure should be strongest, while Parent B supplies the intrabar execution evidence that the marginal seller has actually been met rather than that the stock remains in a continuing liquidation.
factors.name: Systemic Semibeta Absorption Validation

factors.trading_idea: Abnormal-volume closes near one end of the daily range proxy for a one-sided liquidity-demand event, but their implication depends on the stock's immediately preceding return state: the same apparent buy pressure can represent informed continuation after a decline or liquidity-provider inventory recycling after a rally. The child estimates this conditional directed transition map causally from prior pressure states to next-day return signs and trades only current pressure states with a historically reliable conditional response. The edge should persist because daily OHLCV makes the latent execution state noisy, while sparse-liquidity price formation and fragmented institutional execution can take several sessions to resolve; it is falsified if high predicted transition states do not outperform equally sized pressure events after conditioning on prior return sign.
factors.name: Conditional Flow Transition Information

factors.trading_idea: Clustered broad left-tail days proxy for rare high-marginal-utility consumption states in which investors reduce risk mechanically, while close-near-low abnormal-volume selling identifies the names receiving the immediate liquidity shock. The child goes long the strongest downside-pressure names only when they have resilient financing capacity, because selling of cash-rich, low-leverage firms in a systemic tail episode is more likely delegated risk-budget liquidation than new solvency information. Fragile firms are deliberately excluded because identical order-flow pressure is more likely to reveal genuine refinancing risk; this interaction distinguishes temporary forced-flow overshoots from fundamental deterioration, which neither parent can isolate alone.
factors.name: Tail-Cluster Resilient Liquidity Release

factors.trading_idea: A sector-wide shock is incorporated first in liquid, heavily traded constituents, while thinly traded names with similar sector exposure can temporarily underreact because arbitrage capital and order-book capacity are sparse. Long a low-liquidity name whose return falls short of its beta-implied sector move, and short a name that overshoots its implied move. This should fail if residual gaps do not subsequently close after controlling for sector beta, size, and idiosyncratic volatility.
factors.name: Sparse-Liquidity Sector Shock Diffusion

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth risk implies that losses occurring in aggregate downside states carry disproportionate marginal-utility cost. Firms with high estimated downside-market beta and weak financial buffers are especially costly to hold in such states, so they should offer a positive subsequent financing premium as investors and intermediaries slowly reprice tail-risk capacity. The hypothesis is falsified if conditional downside beta, particularly when interacted with low cash coverage and high leverage, does not positively predict six-bar returns after controlling for its unconditional cross-sectional rank; the edge can persist because tail exposure is episodic, capital intensive to hedge, and difficult for constrained arbitrageurs to warehouse.
factors.name: Conditional Tail Financing Beta Premium

factors.trading_idea: The parent's negative realized sign suggests that regular high participation with muted impact is more often a liquidity-provider inventory state than evidence of unfinished informed demand. When a previously regular, absorbed schedule abruptly subsides, dealers no longer need to maintain the temporary quote concession created while warehousing the flow, so the prior signed footprint reverses over the next several days. This is falsifiable: conditional on elevated, regular, low-impact participation followed by a participation drop, returns should move opposite the preceding footprint at six bars, while the same footprint without termination should not show the same prompt reversal. The effect can persist because daily bars conceal the identity and inventory constraints of liquidity suppliers, and arbitrageurs cannot directly observe whether the apparent schedule has actually ended.
factors.name: Terminated Absorbed Schedule Reversal

factors.trading_idea: The parents jointly indicate that an intraday recovery after a panic selloff is not reliably evidence of completed liquidation: for high downside-semibeta names, dealers and short-coverers can mechanically lift the close while systematic de-risking remains active. The child therefore conditions the rebound pattern on both broad cross-sectional fear and the stock's historical downside sensitivity, identifying temporary inventory absorption that is likely followed by renewed selling over the next week. This interaction carries edge because breadth distinguishes a market-wide risk-budget shock from isolated news, while semibeta identifies the names that remain the preferred vehicles for the next deleveraging leg.
factors.name: Systemic Rebound Inventory Overhang

factors.trading_idea: A downside range shock can reflect either temporary depletion of displayed liquidity or a persistent informed/forced sell program. The child distinguishes these states using a square-root-volume-normalized signed impact proxy: shocks that close well off the low indicate liquidity replenishment and should rebound, while shocks embedded in a persistent sequence of downside impact indicate scheduled execution and should continue lower. The edge can persist because inventory-constrained liquidity providers and execution algorithms unwind or complete orders over several daily bars, while outside arbitrageurs only observe noisy OHLCV proxies rather than the underlying queue depth and parent order. This is falsified if close-location recovery and trailing signed-impact imbalance do not jointly explain six-bar returns after conditioning on downside range and relative volume.
factors.name: Impact Replenishment versus Sell Schedule

factors.trading_idea: A downside range shock is most likely to continue when weak close location and persistent square-root-volume-normalized sell impact coincide with unusually persistent negative-day range innovations, indicating that both execution pressure and deleveraging demand remain active. Conversely, a close recovering from the low is a reliable rebound signal only when downside range innovations decay relative to upside innovations, because this identifies genuine liquidity replenishment rather than a temporary pause in an ongoing sell program.
