The final directional event is then a terminal-flow signal: persistent sell-side excitation with compressed impact should rebound, while analogous buy-side excitation should fade over the next six bars. This edge can persist because daily-bar participants observe volume and direction but cannot directly observe latent liquidity replenishment or the remaining inventory of the initiating trader; it is falsified if directional continuation remains stronger than reversal specifically after impact compression.
factors.name: Buffer Replenishment Terminal Flow Flip

factors.trading_idea: Clusters of same-signed, unusually high-participation daily bars can proxy for a persistent parent order or a sequence of informed arrivals. When this directional arrival intensity is high but the cumulative price response remains muted, latent demand has not yet fully traversed available liquidity and should continue in the same direction over the next six bars. This is falsifiable: positive (negative) Hawkes arrival imbalance should predict positive (negative) six-bar returns only when contemporaneous five-bar displacement is small relative to prior volatility; the effect should vanish when the same flow has already produced a large price displacement. The edge can persist because daily bars obscure order splitting, latent depth, and the residual inventory still to be transferred.
factors.name: Muted-Impact Hawkes Completion Drift

factors.trading_idea: Peer return and estimate-revision leadership identifies an industry information wave, but a lagging stock should only close that gap when its recently disclosed cash quality supports survival through the heavy-tailed downside states that investors fear. Quiet realized paths can conceal this state contingency: balance-sheet-resilient firms with compressed downside risk are underpriced as safe recipients of peer-good-news diffusion, whereas fragile names receive little catch-up credit despite an apparent peer lag. The interaction carries edge because peer leadership supplies short-horizon direction while tail-resilience and cash-versus-headline confirmation distinguish credible delayed assimilation from a rational discount for hidden financing risk.
factors.name: Tail-Resilient Peer Diffusion

factors.trading_idea: Positive concordant EPS and revenue revisions usually create public buying interest, but a lower-wick recovery occurring inside an already intense, volume-supported sell schedule reveals that better public consensus is being met by persistent private supply. The recovery is therefore not interpreted as absorption or revision underreaction: it is a temporary replenishment bounce while informed sellers continue to execute. This conflict has edge neither parent has alone because revisions identify the public-information catalyst while the pre-existing sell-flow state distinguishes privately informed distribution from ordinary post-revision demand.
factors.name: Revision-Sell Schedule Conflict

factors.trading_idea: A valuation-momentum breakdown is most informative when industry peer filings indicate that customer-credit stress is accelerating: expensive firms already losing relative price leadership become especially vulnerable as the market updates from idiosyncratic weakness to a common cash-collection shock. The valuation and momentum components identify firms with limited fundamental support, while the lagged leave-one-out peer state distinguishes a broadening credit problem from an isolated disappointing disclosure. This interaction carries edge neither parent has alone because valuation-trend weakness is not uniformly bearish, and peer receivables deterioration is only economically actionable when concentrated in already-expensive price laggards.
factors.name: Peer Credit-State Valuation Breakdown

factors.trading_idea: The parent result suggests that declining downside-shock intensity is not generally seller exhaustion: on daily data it can instead be the low-activity interval of an execution program whose participation is scheduled in volume time. This child identifies cooling downside pressure only when negative returns remain concentrated on above-normal-volume sessions, closes remain near the day’s low, and square-root volume-normalized impact is stable across recent sell days—signatures of a persistent supply program rather than a one-off liquidity vacuum. The expected edge is negative because dealers cannot safely front-run an uncertain latent seller until repeated, volume-conditioned impact reveals the program; it is falsified if these confirmed cooling states do not underperform similarly elevated downside episodes with unstable impact or intraday recovery.
factors.name: Volume-Time Sell Program Continuation

factors.trading_idea: A newly accelerating burst of directional abnormal volume is more likely to represent the early stage of an institutional execution wave than the mature persistent flow used by the parent. When that arrival-rate acceleration coincides with a deterioration in realized liquidity resiliency (unusually large intraday range per dollar traded), marginal orders should move prices quickly over the next several sessions as liquidity providers widen risk tolerance and other traders infer informed flow. The edge should persist because daily bars do not reveal the parent order, hidden liquidity, or remaining execution schedule; it is falsified if fresh buy-side flow accelerations in fragile-liquidity names subsequently underperform, or analogous sell episodes subsequently outperform, over six bars.
factors.name: Accelerating Flow Resiliency Break

factors.trading_idea: A persistent signed close-location flow becomes more informative when its price impact is accelerating relative to the stock's own recent range-per-participation relationship. This transition is interpreted as limit-order replenishment weakening or cancellations increasing: a previously absorbable execution schedule is beginning to consume available displayed and hidden depth, so residual parent-order demand should generate same-direction drift over the next six sessions. The edge persists because daily-bar traders cannot directly observe queue cancellations, hidden liquidity, or the remaining institutional parent-order inventory; it is falsified if directional flow accompanied by rising normalized impact does not outperform similarly signed flow with stable or falling impact.
factors.name: Queue-Cancellation Impact Convexity

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s negative realized IC suggests that a buy burst after decelerating sell intensity is often not replenishment demand, but short-covering or dealer-facilitated relief while a residual sell program remains undisclosed. This child preserves the sell-cluster extinction state but only scores upward, high-volume relief events that fail to reclaim the pre-cascade price anchor; these events indicate inventory overhang and predict renewed selling over the next six bars. The edge persists because daily-bar participants cannot directly observe the remaining parent-order inventory, while temporary liquidity provision can make a relief bar look informative before the scheduled supply reappears. It is falsified if unreclaimed high-volume relief events after decelerating sell clusters do not underperform comparable relief events that reclaim their prior price anchor.
factors.name: Hawkes Relief-Failure Overhang

factors.trading_idea: During broad de-risking, an intraday rebound in a valuation-stretched stock can reflect short covering, dealer liquidity provision, or holders using the rebound to exit rather than informed demand absorption. This interpretation is most credible when the rebound occurs on unusually high turnover, because active liquidity makes a temporary relief rally executable for sellers; these names should subsequently underperform over the next six bars as the fundamental overvaluation again dominates. The edge persists because arbitraging it requires shorting crowded, high-beta names precisely during a volatile risk-off state, exposing the arbitrageur to squeeze and gap risk.
factors.name: Fear-Relief Overvaluation Unwind

factors.trading_idea: The opening price embeds overnight inventory imbalances, news interpretation, and auction liquidity conditions, whereas the close reflects whether continuous trading accepted that repricing. A large gap that is rejected intraday, particularly on below-normal volume, is more likely to represent a temporary auction-price dislocation than durable information and should revert over the subsequent week. The other side of the trade is liquidity-demanding investors forced to transact at the open and short-horizon traders extrapolating the headline gap despite weak daytime confirmation.
factors.name: Opening Gap Acceptance Failure

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth risk implies that stocks whose returns co-move most strongly with aggregate downside states have especially state-dependent cash flows and discount rates. A fresh earnings surprise should therefore be incorporated more gradually for high downside-beta firms: positive surprises reduce perceived bad-state fragility and attract delayed risk-bearing demand, while negative surprises trigger continued de-risking. The edge can persist because the relevant downside exposure is noisy, time-varying, and costly to hedge around sparse earnings events; it is falsified if, conditional on the same surprise, post-release six-day returns do not increase with sector-relative downside beta.
factors.name: Consumption-Tail Earnings Repricing

factors.trading_idea: Clustered same-direction, abnormal-volume return events are a daily-bar proxy for self-exciting informed order flow: an initial information shock induces follow-on trading as investors process the signal and execution programs are split across sessions. The factor goes long when positive marked-event intensity is accelerating faster than negative intensity, but only when the contemporaneous price impact is muted relative to the name's own normal impact, indicating latent demand has not yet fully moved the price. This should be falsifiable because the conditional forward return should be positive only after high branching-style event intensity with muted impact, while equally large isolated shocks or high-impact exhausted shocks should not continue; the edge persists because fragmented attention and gradual institutional execution cannot be instantaneously arbitraged without bearing event and inventory risk.
factors.name: Marked Hawkes Diffusion Efficiency

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s sector-relative framing is retained, but its price-trend confirmation is replaced with a more direct measure of gradual belief updating: persistent analyst EPS revisions that the stock price has not yet absorbed. Positive persistent revisions in cheap firms and negative persistent revisions in expensive firms should have the largest subsequent drift because analysts, discretionary investors, and benchmarked institutional flows incorporate multi-update fundamental information gradually rather than instantaneously. The hypothesis is falsified if, conditional on persistent estimate revisions, stocks whose sector-relative price response lags the revision do not outperform those whose prices have already incorporated it over the next six bars.
factors.name: Persistent Estimate Belief Lag

factors.trading_idea: A downside range shock that is much larger than a stock's own conditional range forecast is more consequential when refinancing capacity is weak: lenders, risk managers, and leveraged holders reduce exposure into a volatility spike, creating asymmetric follow-through rather than symmetric variance mean reversion. The signal shorts financially fragile firms with an unusually large negative volatility innovation and buys robust firms experiencing a comparable positive or benign innovation. This mechanism should fail if downside conditional-range innovations have the same subsequent return distribution for high- and low-financing-risk firms after matching on market beta, size, and total volatility.
factors.name: Financing-Amplified Downside Innovation

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth beliefs should matter most when market downside moves arrive in clusters, because investors then place a larger price on firms' resilience to aggregate tail states. The child trades fresh quality disclosures only during such tail-cluster regimes and gives greater weight to firms with high trailing conditional downside beta, where a change in operating resilience is economically most consequential. This is falsifiable: the signal should lose its conditional advantage in calm regimes and should be strongest among names whose returns historically load on market-tail days. The edge can persist because mapping sparse, point-in-time accounting updates into state-dependent tail-risk repricing is information-intensive and difficult for constrained arbitrageurs to warehouse during stressed markets.
factors.name: Tail-Clustered Quality Disclosure Assimilation

factors.trading_idea: A quality firm's fear-day, high-volume selloff is most likely to rebound when its price-volume path does not resemble a predictable liquidation program. The child uses Parent A's quality-conditioned panic pressure only when Parent B's negative high-volume state has high transition entropy and a high probability of escaping the same downside state, indicating fragmented or exhausted liquidity demand rather than serial forced-sale continuation. This interaction adds edge because fundamentals alone cannot identify whether selling is finished, while path disorder alone cannot distinguish a transitory flow shock from economically justified deterioration.
factors.name: Quality Panic Entropy-Escape Rebound

factors.trading_idea: Bad-news price moves should be more persistent when modest operating weakness can tighten a firm's financing or liquidity constraint. Firms with weak cash coverage, high leverage, and deteriorating operating cash-flow or working-capital quality have greater downside convexity: a negative return shock is more likely to trigger risk reassessment rather than mean reversion. Slow-moving fundamental disclosures and constrained arbitrage against distressed names permit this conditional underreaction to persist; it is falsified if comparable negative shocks reverse equally for fragile and financially resilient firms.
factors.name: Balance-Sheet Bad-News Convexity

factors.trading_idea: A margin-led EPS beat is only likely to correct over the next week when investors have visibly treated the headline as important: an unusually positive close-to-close response accompanied by abnormal turnover reveals concentrated headline attention before revenue and margin durability are fully processed. The parents' ambiguity wedge identifies the information conflict, while their delayed-event construction motivates carrying the signal beyond the announcement bar; conditioning it on the initial attention state avoids fading quiet or already-disbelieved reports. Revenue-confirmed beats that attract the same attention are instead relatively stronger, because attention reinforces a fundamentally corroborated surprise rather than an over-extrapolated margin outcome.
factors.name: Attention-Gated Margin Ambiguity Correction

factors.trading_idea: Order-flow cascades become more likely when directional pressure persists while the market's ability to absorb shocks deteriorates: small impulses increasingly have permanent-looking effects, a daily-bar analogue of critical slowing down before a phase transition. Long persistent positive imbalance states and short persistent negative states, but only when return response is still incomplete relative to accumulated flow. This should be rejected if elevated persistence merely identifies high-volatility names and does not improve the conditional sign accuracy of the six-day return forecast.
factors.name: Critical Imbalance Persistence

factors.trading_idea: A large range-per-dollar-volume shock is most likely an idiosyncratic liquidity vacuum rather than broadly impounded news when the stock's absolute-return volatility is weakly synchronized with the rest of the market. In that state, the signed close-to-close move is expected to continue over roughly six days because liquidity suppliers replenish depth gradually and institutional flow is executed across sessions, rather than being fully cleared in the shock bar. This is falsified if isolated impact shocks reverse as often as synchronized shocks after controlling for their initial return; the edge can persist because traders observing daily bars cannot directly distinguish temporary shallow depth from informed flow or observe the latent order schedule.
factors.name: Desynchronized Liquidity Vacuum Follow-Through

factors.trading_idea: Persistent downside-volatility bursts create two distinct six-bar paths: names with visibly high downside semibeta that have already underperformed are often mechanically sold and become candidates for a rapid risk-rebalance rebound, while apparent defensive shelters with newly elevated tail dependence have not yet been fully repriced and face delayed de-risking. The interaction separates exhausted visible-risk selling from latent nonlinear-risk discovery, resolving Parent B's reversed empirical direction rather than simply flipping its sign. Parent A identifies the delayed-unwind leg but not the oversold high-semibeta rebound, while Parent B's semibeta sort alone cannot distinguish completed liquidation from hidden-tail shelters.
factors.name: Fear Tail-Visibility Rotation

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth shocks make investors especially averse to equities whose returns load on broad market left tails, particularly when weak funding capacity makes cash flows and refinancing needs convex in a downturn. The child measures this lower-tail beta directly rather than inferring tail exposure from a quiet realized path, and activates the cross-section only after a broad negative market shock, when the required compensation for bearing crash-sensitive balance sheets should be most visible over the next six bars. The edge should persist because tail exposure is difficult to hedge cheaply, while quarterly funding information and rare-event dependence are costly for arbitrageurs to continuously model. It is falsified if high tail-beta/funding-fragility names do not outperform low-exposure names following broad downside shocks, or if tail beta adds nothing beyond ordinary market beta and sector membership.
factors.name: Tail-Beta Funding Convexity Premium

factors.trading_idea: The child targets names that appeared historically safe in downside-beta space relative to their ordinary beta, but whose recent downside co-crash probability has abruptly risen during a broad fear shock. These are hidden systemic-risk proxies: conventional beta models and prior risk budgets still treat them as defensive, while nonlinear tail linkage reveals that their protection is unreliable. A muted same-day decline creates a transmission gap, so subsequent de-risking should penalize these names more than either high-beta names already recognized by Parent A or generic tail-dependent names in Parent B.
factors.name: Hidden Tail-Safe Deleveraging Gap

factors.trading_idea: Newly disclosed net equity issuance or buybacks alter the effective public float and force gradual portfolio rebalancing by benchmarked, capacity-constrained investors. The price effect should be negative after issuance and positive after repurchases, especially where the implied float adjustment is large relative to the stock's normal dollar-turnover capacity; the signal decays because the demand imbalance is gradually absorbed. This is falsifiable: conditional on a fresh share-count or net-issuance disclosure, subsequent 6-bar returns should be more negative for issuance and more positive for repurchase in names with longer turnover-implied absorption times. The edge can persist because disclosure-driven ownership rebalancing is costly and staggered, while arbitrageurs face the same liquidity and borrow constraints that slow the adjustment.
factors.name: Disclosed Float Overhang Capacity

factors.trading_idea: Forced selling in financially vulnerable firms is most likely to continue when it occurs near an expected reporting date, because uncertainty about the imminent information release reduces contrarian liquidity provision. A recent negative consensus revision supplies the directional state variable: dealers and fundamental buyers are less willing to absorb a downside volume shock when the pending report is increasingly expected to validate bad news. Neither parent alone distinguishes ordinary balance-sheet-driven liquidation from the particularly fragile pre-announcement state in which negative information, refinancing risk, and sparse liquidity reinforce one another.
factors.name: Pre-Announcement Rollover Cascade (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: Mechanically sliced institutional execution can create a quasi-periodic sequence of similarly signed, volume-weighted price pressures, unlike information-driven trading whose timing is less clock-like. When this periodic pressure remains detectable but its most recent amplitude collapses, the execution program is likely ending and liquidity providers can unwind inventory, producing a reversal over the next six bars. The hypothesis is falsified if names with high periodicity, fading pressure, and positive recent pressure continue to outperform rather than underperform, or if the analogous sell-pressure cases do not rebound. The effect can persist because identifying the terminal stage requires estimating a noisy trailing spectral pattern across many names, while market makers face inventory and adverse-selection risk before the program's completion is confirmed.
factors.name: Spectral Execution Clock Terminal Fade

factors.trading_idea: During broad fear episodes, a stock decline that is not shared by its usual downside-correlation neighborhood is more likely to reflect temporary liquidation, stale liquidity, or an idiosyncratic order imbalance than a durable repricing. In contrast, declines confirmed by a tightly connected peer group are more plausibly information-bearing and should not be mechanically faded. The inefficiency persists because broad de-risking and execution constraints force investors to sell liquid or mandate-constrained names before fundamental arbitrage capital can distinguish isolated shocks from cluster-wide information.
factors.name: Panic Graph Isolation Repair

factors.trading_idea: A coherent earnings and revenue surprise is more likely to generate a durable six-day analyst-revision drift when it validates an already credible capital-allocation policy: cheap firms retiring shares from free cash flow have both financial capacity and a stronger signal of management discipline. Conversely, coherent negative surprises are especially damaging when they expose expensive firms using debt-supported repurchases, because the report forces investors to reassess both earnings power and the sustainability of per-share support. The interaction carries edge beyond either parent alone because surprise direction identifies the new information while buyback funding and valuation identify whether that information confirms a credible compounding narrative or breaks a fragile one.
factors.name: Capital-Allocation Conditioned Surprise Drift

factors.trading_idea: A clustered set of industry peers simultaneously reporting earnings and revenue surprises is a high-precision information burst: it cross-excites comparable-company valuation updates more credibly than an isolated EPS surprise. The child targets firms without their own concurrent release whose two-day idiosyncratic response remains muted relative to the signed, recent peer burst, so the information should be incorporated within the fixed six-day horizon rather than over a long post-event drift. The hypothesis is falsified if, among no-own-event firms, response gaps following broad joint peer-surprise bursts do not predict stronger six-day returns in the burst direction than already aligned firms. The edge can persist because analysts and discretionary industry portfolios must translate multiple releases into firm-specific read-throughs, while systematic strategies may react to the peer basket before resolving which individual names have not yet repriced.
factors.name: Joint Surprise Burst Response Relay

factors.trading_idea: Pinned close-location pressure alone is often generated by uninformed execution that liquidity providers can absorb and subsequently reverse, consistent with Parent B's failed unconditional drift direction. The child treats that pressure as informative only when its sign agrees with a recent point-in-time cash-realization revision: persistent buying aligned with improving cash quality is more likely informed accumulation, while persistent selling aligned with deteriorating cash realization is more likely informed distribution. This interaction distinguishes fundamental-information-motivated metaorders from mechanically trapped flow, an identification neither price-volume absorption nor cash revisions can make alone.
factors.name: Cash-Confirmed Pinned Flow

factors.trading_idea: Persistent absorbed range pressure is not intrinsically directional: Parent B's realized negative IC suggests that, absent information, it is often temporary execution flow that subsequently reverses. Parent A indicates that when pressure coincides with a fresh, concordant EPS-and-revenue consensus update, the pressure is more likely informed assimilation and should continue rather than fade. The child therefore uses consensus-revision state to switch the sign of absorbed pressure: follow aligned pressure during fresh coherent information arrival, but fade the same pressure when no such information state exists.
factors.name: Revision-State Pressure Polarity Switch

factors.trading_idea: Volume-leading-range hysteresis normally identifies delayed liquidity adjustment and directional continuation, but that continuation is less credible when the apparent earnings narrative is supported by debt-financed buybacks rather than operating cash generation. The child treats accounting-engineering intensity as a regime variable: it preserves flow continuation for fundamentally credible firms while inverting the same signed flow pressure for firms with a large EPS-versus-income wedge, shrinking shares, weak free cash flow, and rising debt. The interaction carries edge because it distinguishes genuine demand-information flow from headline-driven demand that is more likely to exhaust once balance-sheet fragility is recognized.
factors.name: EPS Engineering Flow-Regime Inversion

factors.trading_idea: Cooling downside-range clusters alone can continue lower when they reflect informed repricing, while regular high-participation selling alone can rebound because the apparent program is being absorbed rather than extended. This child goes long only when the two coincide with a collapse in downside impact per square-root volume and improving close location: the seller is still trading on its volume clock, but each unit of scheduled flow moves price less as displayed and latent liquidity replenishes. That interaction identifies absorption of mechanical supply, a state neither parent can isolate because one treats stable impact as continuation and the other cannot distinguish informational cooling from volume-scheduled liquidation.
factors.name: Scheduled-Flow Impact Compression Repair

factors.trading_idea: The parents jointly suggest that isolated high-participation range shocks are not persistent information events on this daily horizon, but temporary dealer-inventory and liquidity-demand dislocations. The child conditions that reversal on the valuation state: a cheap stock closing near the low of an idiosyncratic high-volume range is likely to attract value-sensitive absorption, while an expensive stock closing near the high is more vulnerable to profit-taking and withdrawal of marginal buyers. Neither parent alone distinguishes an idiosyncratic shock that has a credible valuation-based absorber from one whose directional move is unsupported by fundamentals.
factors.name: Valuation-Conditioned Idiosyncratic Inventory Reversal

factors.trading_idea: Institutional execution commonly follows recurring weekly participation schedules, allowing liquidity providers to anticipate and warehouse routine flow; its price impact should therefore be relatively temporary. A volume realization that is unusually large versus the stock's own same-weekday execution clock, and that closes decisively in one direction, is more consistent with an unanticipated information-motivated imbalance whose impact is not yet fully incorporated. The edge persists because the predictable component is name-specific and must be estimated from historical execution timing, while the surprise is only observable after the daily auction closes.
factors.name: Weekday Clock Surprise Impact

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s positive realized IC suggests that, at a six-bar horizon, abrupt idiosyncratic downside volatility in financially fragile firms more often identifies forced-selling exhaustion than a still-unpriced deterioration in solvency. The child therefore only treats the shock as bullish when unusually high turnover accompanies a strong close-location recovery from the intrabar low, evidence that liquidity providers and value buyers absorbed the sell program rather than withdrew. The edge can persist because identifying temporary liquidation from daily price-volume geometry requires bearing crash and inventory risk; it is falsified if fragility-weighted downside shocks with both abnormal volume and high close-location do not outperform comparable shocks lacking those absorption signatures over the next six bars.
factors.name: Fragile Tail Absorption Rebound

factors.trading_idea: Daily return and volume innovations trace a signed loop rather than merely a contemporaneous price-impact relationship. A positive loop occurs when abnormal trading activity arrives before a negative return and then fades as price stabilises: this is consistent with temporary liquidity-demand inventory being absorbed rather than persistent adverse information, so it should precede relatively positive six-bar returns; the opposite loop should precede weaker returns. This is falsifiable by testing whether forward-return spreads are monotonic in trailing signed loop area after controlling for current return and volume shocks. The edge can persist because investors commonly react to endpoints such as return, volume, or volatility, while the causal phase ordering between activity and price is a lower-salience state variable and inventory transfer takes several sessions to unwind.
factors.name: Return-Volume Hysteresis Relaxation

factors.trading_idea: A consensus revision is most likely to generate delayed repricing when it is both economically credible and in conflict with the price anchor formed before the update. High cash-realization quality filters revisions that are likely to survive investor scrutiny, while a price move in the opposite direction identifies names for which the revised earnings information has not yet been incorporated. Neither condition alone distinguishes credible-but-already-priced news from surprising-but-unreliable news; their interaction isolates the residual information gap expected to close over the fixed six-bar horizon.
factors.name: Quality Anchor-Conflict Resolution Drift

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s negative realized IC indicates that a high-volume buy response during decelerating sell intensity is more often temporary replenishment than confirmed sell-program extinction. Dealers and short-covering buyers can create a sharp positive bar while latent institutional supply remains, especially when price fails to reclaim the pre-cascade reference level; the residual sell inventory is then re-executed over the following week. This should persist because daily-bar observers cannot directly see hidden parent orders, dealer inventory, or off-book liquidity, and it is falsified if failed replenishment rallies after an elevated sell cascade do not underperform comparable positive-volume bars without residual sell intensity over six days.
factors.name: Hawkes Replenishment Failure Continuation

factors.trading_idea: Rare, coherent EPS-and-revenue surprise ruptures create a difficult-to-process earnings narrative, but the delayed repricing should be most durable when analysts confirm the report through an aligned consensus revision and the firm can fund its outlook internally rather than through debt issuance. The signal specifically targets ruptures whose sector-relative price response remains small relative to their statistical novelty, then weights the catch-up by free-cash-flow-backed credibility. Neither parent alone distinguishes a merely unusual report from an unusual report that has both analyst confirmation and a credible financing channel while still being under-assimilated by the market.
factors.name: Cash-Backed Rupture Revision Gap

factors.trading_idea: A persistent institutional execution program can raise a name's participation rate for several days while producing unusually little price impact per dollar traded, because liquidity providers and opposite-side flow initially absorb the order. A coherent signed intraday footprint under this muted-impact, regular-participation state indicates that the program remains unfinished rather than that a one-day liquidity shock has exhausted; its direction should therefore continue over the next six bars. The edge can persist because daily bars do not reveal trader identity, remaining parent-order size, or hidden liquidity, and arbitrageurs face substantial noise and inventory risk when attempting to front-run low-impact flow. It is falsified if elevated, serially regular participation with below-normal impact does not distinguish subsequent directional drift from ordinary high-volume price moves.
factors.name: Regular Participation Muted-Impact Drift

factors.trading_idea: A negative earnings surprise with unusually high volume but little range expansion identifies supply that is being absorbed rather than immediately clearing the market. Parent B's inverted realized sign suggests that absorbed surprise flow is not uniformly continuation: for fundamentally strong firms, bad-news-induced selling can be an inventory-transfer episode, especially once Parent A's idiosyncratic downside excitation is elevated but demonstrably decelerating. The interaction has edge because the surprise identifies a concrete catalyst and latent liquidity state, while cascade extinction distinguishes completed forced selling from still-accelerating adverse-information repricing.
factors.name: Quality Bad-News Absorption Release

factors.trading_idea: Large post-earnings moves are heavy-tailed belief shocks: investors overweight a salient earnings anchor, creating disposition-driven selling above the anchor and reluctant-holder supply below it. The child only trades this reference-point reversal when the stock's displacement agrees with a peer-supported industry lead-lag gap and the firm is financially resilient, separating temporary disagreement and implementation delay from rational distress or firm-specific information. This interaction has edge because the anchor identifies who is likely inventory-constrained, while peer fundamentals and solvency identify whether the price divergence is likely to repair within the fixed six-bar horizon.
factors.name: Tail Event Peer-Concordance Reversal

factors.trading_idea: Marked sell intensity alone can often identify capitulation, which explains Parent B's empirically positive forward-return direction: intense selling may exhaust supply and rebound. The child isolates the opposite case by requiring that clustered marked selling occurs in a high conditional-downside-beta stock that has also recovered from an idiosyncratic intrabar selloff during broad fear. The recovered wick then represents temporary dealer absorption rather than seller exhaustion, while the elevated downside beta identifies names institutions still need to reduce, creating a six-session continuation short signal neither flow intensity nor a single wick can distinguish alone.
factors.name: Downside-Beta Absorption Aftershock

factors.trading_idea: An analyst-consensus revision is most actionable when it has not yet been absorbed into the stock price, especially when it is idiosyncratic rather than a broad sector-wide revision that attracts immediate attention. This is a conditional factor-timing implementation: the estimated-revision signal is scaled down in high-breadth revision regimes and amplified for isolated revisions with weak sector-relative price confirmation. The mechanism is falsified if recent sector-relative returns already fully incorporate subsequent analyst-estimate changes, or if revision breadth does not condition the signal's realized spread.
factors.name: Idiosyncratic Revision Pass-Through Deficit

factors.trading_idea: Daily signed return-volume shocks can act as coarse observations of latent buy and sell order-flow events. Repeated same-sign, unusually high-participation events over a decaying window indicate a self-exciting metaorder or information-diffusion process whose impact is not fully completed, whereas alternating signs imply that excitation is being absorbed by opposing liquidity. The effect should fail when elevated volume is not directionally clustered, which distinguishes persistent order-flow pressure from generic high-volume noise.
factors.name: Volume-Marked Directional Excitation Pressure

factors.trading_idea: The market frequently rewards reported sales growth before fully distinguishing internally funded expansion from growth purchased with dilution, leverage, or aggressive balance-sheet investment. Revenue acceleration supported by operating cash flow and stable-to-falling share count is a more credible growth regime, while growth accompanied by issuance, debt expansion, and rapid asset accumulation is vulnerable to repricing. The mechanism should fail if financing composition has no incremental explanatory power beyond revenue growth and sector membership.
factors.name: Self-Financed Growth Confirmation

factors.trading_idea: A self-exciting, directionally coherent sequence of abnormal return-volume events is evidence that a latent metaorder remains active, which is Parent A's useful state variable. Parent B contributes the crucial discriminator: continuation is selected only when persistent signed participation has produced less price movement than its own historically estimated impact, indicating that liquidity replenishment has temporarily absorbed rather than completed the execution program. This interaction avoids treating every cascade as continuation or every impact deficit as a catch-up trade: the deficit is informative specifically when an endogenous directional cascade supplies evidence of an unfinished order-flow source.
factors.name: Endogenous Reignition Underimpact

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed aggregate consumption-growth risk is proxied by the Hill tail thickness of recent market downside returns: when this state rises, marginal utility in bad aggregate states becomes especially convex and investors rotate toward firms that are both fundamentally resilient and empirically less exposed to market downside shocks. The signal therefore combines cash-flow and balance-sheet resilience with a trailing downside beta, increasing the penalty for downside-beta exposure only in a fat-left-tail regime. The edge should persist because firm-specific crash exposure cannot be cheaply eliminated with an index hedge and institutional de-risking of fragile balance sheets is gradual; it is falsified if the resilience-minus-downside-beta spread does not strengthen specifically following elevated Hill tail states.
factors.name: Hill Tail Resilience Rotation

factors.trading_idea: A broad industry selloff is more likely to represent a persistent funding and de-risking event when it occurs inside an unusually synchronized market-wide downside regime, rather than an isolated sector repricing. In that hierarchical shock state, investors first reduce basket exposure and only subsequently discriminate between firms with different liquidity, leverage, profitability, and cash-flow buffers. The interaction carries edge because market synchrony identifies when cross-sectional fundamentals matter for forced allocation, while the leave-one-out peer shock identifies which industries are actually transmitting that common stress.
factors.name: Hierarchical Shock-Absorption Rotation

factors.trading_idea: Revenue-consensus revisions are usually processed faster than the full earnings implication, especially for firms with high fixed operating-cost intensity where a sales revision has convex consequences for margins and EPS. Go long firms with favorable revenue-estimate acceleration whose EPS consensus has not yet caught up, and short the opposite configuration. The mechanism is falsified if subsequent EPS-estimate changes do not close the revenue-to-EPS revision gap; slow analyst-model updates and investors' focus on top-line headlines are the expected source of delay.
factors.name: Operating-Leverage Revision Transmission

factors.trading_idea: Investors and automated news systems often extrapolate a positive revenue surprise before fully incorporating whether the reported sales are being converted into cash-like working-capital outcomes. A positive surprise accompanied by receivables and inventory growth materially exceeding revenue growth is more likely to reflect channel stuffing, loose credit terms, or demand pulled forward, so its initial valuation uplift should reverse over the following week. This is falsifiable if the interaction between surprise and the working-capital mismatch has no incremental negative 6-bar return after controlling for the surprise, sector, and each growth component separately; the edge can persist because headline data are immediately salient while joint interpretation of sales quality requires slower accounting analysis.
factors.name: Headline Cash-Conversion Mismatch

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s EPS-versus-revenue wedge likely captured a feature that the market correctly interpreted quickly, rather than a delayed margin-quality correction. This child instead isolates analyst EPS-consensus revisions arriving after an earnings report, when analysts have processed guidance and model implications but some investors have not yet incorporated the revised cash-flow outlook. Positive delayed revisions accompanied by a muted two-day price response should drift upward over the next six bars as slower-moving portfolios and peer analysts update; the edge persists because revision dissemination and institutional implementation are staggered. This is falsifiable: conditional on a report within the prior 15 bars, future six-bar returns should increase monotonically in post-report EPS-estimate revisions after controlling for the contemporaneous price response.
factors.name: Delayed Revision Muted-Response Drift

factors.trading_idea: The child buys a downside opening gap that is rejected intraday during a sector-synchronous sell-liquidity shock, but only after the stock's previously elevated idiosyncratic downside semivariance has begun to decay. This combines Parent A's identification of a mechanically forced auction overshoot with Parent B's volatility state variable: declining semivariance distinguishes an extinguishing liquidation cascade from unresolved adverse information. The interaction has edge because gap rejection alone can be a temporary bounce, while downside-volatility cooling alone does not locate the discrete inventory-transfer event where short-horizon price repair is most likely.
factors.name: Synchronous Gap Semivariance Release

factors.trading_idea: An adverse dual earnings-and-revenue surprise at a financially fragile issuer creates a plausible forced-sale program, but that event alone cannot distinguish permanent repricing from temporary inventory pressure. The child activates only when Hawkes-style abnormal sell intensity remains elevated yet its fast intensity drops below its slow intensity, while the cumulative predicted sell impact has not been paid and ranges remain compressed. This interaction identifies the specific transition from absorbed, scheduled liquidation to seller exhaustion: Parent A supplies the economically constrained supply shock, while Parent B supplies the endogenous flow-decay and deferred-impact state that makes a six-day rebound more likely.
factors.name: Rupture Extinction Impact Release

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth states are better represented by a firm's empirical probability of jointly entering its own left tail when the aggregate market is in a severe left tail than by a linear downside beta. A newly disclosed improvement in cash liquidity or cash-flow quality is most valuable for firms with high conditional tail dependence because it directly lowers their probability of distress in disaster states, yet investors tend to process the balance-sheet update and nonlinear disaster exposure separately. The hypothesis is falsifiable: positive resilience updates should have stronger 6-bar IC among high conditional-tail-dependence names, while the interaction should be weak for low-tail-dependence names; the edge persists because rare-event dependence is noisy to estimate and quarterly balance-sheet assimilation is operationally slow.
factors.name: Tail-Dependence Cash Resilience Update

factors.trading_idea: A negative range innovation is more likely to continue over the next week when it arrives inside an already self-exciting sequence of downside shocks rather than as an isolated volatility event. The balance-sheet weakness mechanism from Parent A supplies the susceptibility state: fragile firms face tighter financing constraints and less dip-buying capacity, while Parent B supplies the conditional range-surprise measure that identifies genuinely abnormal downside information. Their interaction carries edge because a fragile firm with a single large move may simply mean-revert, whereas a fragile firm experiencing a renewed downside range shock after recent downside excitation is more likely undergoing a forced-deleveraging cascade.
factors.name: Fragility-Gated Downside Excitation

factors.trading_idea: Directional abnormal-volume excitation is valuable only when the associated flow is both under-reflected in price and persistent across adjacent bars: this identifies a still-active metaorder whose buffered impact should be released over the next several days. Conversely, compressed impact with weak flow persistence is more consistent with liquidity replenishment after a fresh terminal impulse, so the directional event is faded. The interaction carries edge because Parent A's impact deficit distinguishes unpaid from paid flow, while Parent B's persistence state distinguishes a temporary buffer from genuine completion.
factors.name: Persistent Impact-Deficit Router

factors.trading_idea: Parent A's contrary sign is consistent with inherited downside excitation often representing a broad, still-risky deleveraging regime rather than a tradable local exhaustion. This child only acts when the sell cascade is demonstrably idiosyncratic relative to the stock's industry range-volatility innovation, so the pressure is more likely a temporary depth failure than common information or systemic inventory withdrawal. A low-participation downside range shock that has stopped receiving fresh downside marks and closes high in its range indicates that local forced supply has been absorbed; this interaction should repair within six bars because neither isolated-shock identification nor excitation deceleration alone distinguishes local absorption from a continuing market-wide liquidation.
factors.name: Idiosyncratic Excitation Extinction Repair

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s inverted result is consistent with investors correctly rewarding, rather than fading, margin-led EPS beats when they reflect durable operating leverage instead of accounting noise. This child isolates positive EPS surprises with non-negative revenue confirmation, a contemporaneous improvement in operating margin, and strong cash conversion; these are the reports most likely to trigger delayed upward analyst revisions and six-day post-earnings drift. The edge should persist because validating whether margin expansion is cash-backed and operationally repeatable requires processing the filing and updating forecasts, while the initial market reaction is dominated by the earnings headline. It is falsifiable: among positive EPS reporters with non-negative revenue surprises, subsequent six-bar returns should increase monotonically in the joint rank of EPS surprise, margin improvement, and income quality.
factors.name: Cash-Confirmed Margin Revision Lag

factors.trading_idea: This child isolates earnings disclosures whose fundamental direction is corroborated by cash-flow versus accrual growth, but whose translation into valuation is difficult because of working-capital ambiguity or intangible intensity. It then requires the immediate price response to under-implement that credible news and carries the gap forward only while consensus remains unrevised after a stale-forecast spell. The interaction creates edge because cash confirmation rejects low-quality surprises, opacity explains why analysts need time to process them, and the revision-cleared clock targets the specific period in which the price and consensus bridges remain incomplete.
factors.name: Cash-Confirmed Opaque Implementation Clock

factors.trading_idea: A positive EPS surprise caused by unexpectedly strong revenue is more likely to represent persistent demand information than one caused solely by temporary cost control, tax effects, or accounting noise. Investors often initially anchor on the headline EPS beat, but revise medium-term sales and margin expectations more gradually when both revenue and EPS surprises confirm each other. The hypothesis is falsified if joint revenue-and-EPS surprises do not outperform EPS-only surprises after controlling for sector and announcement-period volatility.
factors.name: Demand-Led Earnings Surprise Drift

factors.trading_idea: Parent A identifies whether persistent sell pressure is being absorbed through concave price impact, but concavity is more credible when the selling resembles a regular execution schedule rather than a one-off information shock. This child conditions impact curvature on a renewal-clock proxy: sustained downside bars with stable pressure increments and regular participation are consistent with a mechanical metaorder being passively absorbed. The interaction has edge because orderly flow alone does not reveal whether liquidity is replenishing, while concave impact without a scheduling state can confuse transient news reactions with forced-flow exhaustion.
factors.name: Scheduled Sell Curvature Release

factors.trading_idea: A large downside-range variance innovation that closes near the session high is evidence that aggressive selling was absorbed, but by itself it cannot distinguish a temporary liquidity overshoot from a rational repricing of a financially fragile issuer. The child activates this recovery-shaped volatility signal primarily when broad market fear is elevated and the issuer has a strong liquidity and debt-service buffer, where mandate-constrained deleveraging is more likely to have pushed price below fundamental survival value. The interaction creates edge because the volatility path identifies seller exhaustion while the balance-sheet state filters out names whose downside shock is more likely to reflect genuine solvency risk.
factors.name: Solvency-Gated Variance Absorption Release

factors.trading_idea: The child treats nonlinear co-crash exposure not as a standalone premium, but as a state-dependent constraint on whether fundamental-price disagreement can close quickly. When aggregate left-tail events are clustering, capital is preferentially reallocated toward firms with improving estimates and cash-flow yield that have historically avoided disproportionate co-crashes; unsupported smooth trends in tail-vulnerable firms become especially fragile. This interaction carries edge neither parent has alone: Parent A identifies delayed fundamental validation, while Parent B supplies the marginal-utility regime and resilience screen that determines which validation gaps are financeable during stressed risk allocation.
factors.name: Tail-Resilient Fundamental Validation Gap

factors.trading_idea: Confirmed earnings news has its strongest six-day effect when it arrives against the direction of a cooling, one-sided price-volume execution burst: the prior move is more likely temporary inventory pressure than informed repricing. A muted announcement-day reaction leaves the fundamental information incompletely assimilated, while metaorder completion removes the mechanical flow that had been suppressing or inflating the price. Neither parent alone distinguishes a delayed fundamental repricing from a generic flow reversal; their interaction identifies disclosures that both invalidate the mechanical-price anchor and retain unpriced information.
factors.name: Disclosure Opposed Flow Completion Drift

factors.trading_idea: Parent A's realized sign suggests that an intense bad-news sell cascade often marks local inventory exhaustion rather than continued fundamental drift: the marginal seller has already acted and subsequent returns rebound. Parent B's realized sign indicates that the same apparent dislocation is dangerous when it occurs inside synchronized sector-wide liquidity stress, because broad deleveraging is persistent rather than a name-specific overshoot. The child therefore buys bad-news cascades only when the stock's downside excitation is unusually localized relative to its sector and suppresses cases where sector-wide impact-and-downside synchrony remains elevated; this separates exhausted idiosyncratic supply from continuing systemic forced flow.
factors.name: Localized Bad-News Cascade Exhaustion

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s negative realized sign suggests that regular high participation and closes near a bar extreme more often identify mechanical benchmark or closing-auction demand than an informed metaorder with permanent price impact. This child isolates the subset where repeated terminal directional pressure fails to produce a commensurate multi-day close-to-close displacement relative to intraday range: this is evidence that liquidity providers and the broader market are not accepting the price move, leaving temporary dealer inventory to unwind over the next several sessions. The hypothesis is falsified if, conditional on similarly elevated and regular participation, low-acceptance buy pressure does not underperform low-acceptance sell pressure over six days; the edge can persist because the distinction between temporary execution pressure and information is only revealed gradually through subsequent price acceptance, while inventory risk is unwound over multiple daily sessions.
factors.name: Nonaccepted Terminal Flow Inventory Fade

factors.trading_idea: An accelerating stock-industry correlation identifies a transient contagion regime in which peer returns are more likely to represent a common innovation than unrelated noise. Within that regime, the relevant opportunity is not simply high industry beta: it is a low-but-active-capacity stock whose own excess return has failed to complete the beta-implied response to a volume-weighted peer shock. The interaction carries edge because correlation synchronization validates the peer shock's information content, while liquidity stress identifies the names for which that information is still incompletely incorporated over the next six bars.
factors.name: Synchrony-Gated Liquidity Backlog Relay

factors.trading_idea: Large-volume closes near one end of the daily range can reveal a latent directional auction imbalance, but only when recent high-activity imbalances have repeatedly been followed by same-signed next-day close locations. This phase-locking pattern is consistent with a metaorder being partially absorbed by liquidity providers and then reappearing as the order is worked across multiple sessions; the child buys positive current imbalances in names with a positive estimated propagation coefficient and shorts the symmetric negative cases. The hypothesis is falsified if the conditional six-day return is not increasing in the signed volume-location impulse after conditioning on its trailing one-bar auction-response coefficient. The edge can persist because the latent parent order and dealer inventory trajectory are not directly observable from daily bars, while traders reacting only to closing returns cannot distinguish persistent informed flow from a one-day liquidity shock.
factors.name: Phase-Locked Auction Inertia

factors.trading_idea: Abnormal-volume idiosyncratic returns are observable slices of latent institutional parent orders, but only names whose earlier slices have reliably transferred into same-signed returns over the next several days should exhibit continuation. The child estimates this stock-specific lagged transfer response and applies it to current signed abnormal-volume pressure, rather than treating every high-volume move as momentum. It is falsified if the estimated 1-5 day transfer coefficient does not condition future relative returns after sector neutralisation. The edge can persist because parent-order size and execution schedules are hidden, while arbitrageurs face impact and inventory risk when attempting to front-run a partially revealed institutional program.
factors.name: Delayed Execution Transfer

factors.trading_idea: The CAPE-style mechanism in value_matters_predictability_of_stock_index_returns implies that valuation is a slow-moving return anchor while momentum captures the short-run path by which prices move toward or away from that anchor. Stocks that are cheap relative to sector peers and already beginning to outperform are more likely experiencing gradual belief updating toward fundamentals; richly valued names that are starting to underperform face the symmetric unwind. The signal should fail if the conditional continuation of value-aligned trends is no stronger than either standalone value or standalone momentum, indicating that the apparent anchor is not economically relevant at the six-bar horizon.
factors.name: Valuation Anchor Phase Alignment

factors.trading_idea: A large downside volatility innovation normally reflects either informed repricing or temporary liquidity withdrawal. When the same bar closes near its high after an abnormally large downside move and elevated participation, liquidity replenishment has already absorbed the sell imbalance; high-ROIC, cash-generative firms are less likely to be undergoing permanent adverse-information repricing. The hypothesis is falsifiable: this interaction should predict positive six-bar returns only after downside-volatility innovations with strong close-location recovery, and should fail for weak-quality firms or bars closing near their lows. The edge persists because confirmation of replenishment requires the completed bar, while constrained liquidity providers and slow-moving discretionary capital need subsequent days to normalize inventory and prices.
factors.name: Downside Innovation Close-Location Resilience

factors.trading_idea: Sector-wide price moves are rapidly processed through index, ETF, and common-factor trading, whereas a volume-confirmed return that diverges from same-sector peers is more likely to contain issuer-specific information. Such moves should continue over the next week because specialized investors must verify and disseminate firm-specific information, while institutional execution is often spread over multiple sessions. The hypothesis is falsified if peer-relative returns have equal or greater continuation when volume is unusually low, or if volume-confirmed sector-common moves are as predictive as volume-confirmed idiosyncratic moves. The edge should persist because identifying whether a move is genuinely firm-specific requires noisy peer decomposition and costly fundamental attention rather than a mechanically observable market-wide signal.
factors.name: Peer Divergence Participation Diffusion

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s negative realized IC suggests that a quiet-consensus EPS beat that exceeds the revenue beat is more often treated by investors as a durable operating-margin improvement when it is actually a low-quality earnings event. This child isolates the economically specific failure mode: earnings growth exceeds operating-cash-flow growth while receivables and inventories are building, indicating that reported margin strength has not converted into cash and may reflect aggressive revenue recognition, inventory accumulation, or deferred operating costs. The expected negative return arises as analysts and investors parse cash-flow and working-capital disclosures after initially extrapolating the headline EPS beat; this persists because those accounting details are more costly to process than the headline surprise.
factors.name: Silent Margin Cash-Conversion Fragility

factors.trading_idea: Routine liquidity-motivated trading produces a relatively stable conditional relationship between daily volume surprise and absolute return. A return that is unusually large even after conditioning on contemporaneous activity is a break in that price-volume coupling: it is more likely to reflect information arriving through dispersed investors than a mechanically completed liquidity trade, so its signed direction should continue over the next six sessions. This is falsified if signed conditional-impact residuals reverse after controlling for volume surprise; the edge can persist because daily volume cannot reveal the private-information content, investor heterogeneity, or gradual institutional response behind an abnormal displacement.
factors.name: Conditional Impact Copula Information Residual

factors.trading_idea: A sector-level, high-participation directional cascade identifies a shared information shock, but it does not reveal which constituent is still being executed or merely experiencing a completed impulse. The child goes long lagging names only when their own abnormal directional flow remains serially persistent and its predicted impact exceeds the price move already realized, indicating an active execution backlog rather than the terminal replenishment state that weakened Parent B at six days. The interaction has edge because the sector cascade validates that local flow is information-linked, while the persistent impact deficit selects the specific constituent where sector information has not yet been fully transmitted into price.
factors.name: Sector Cascade Persistent Deficit Relay

factors.trading_idea: A recovered high-volume downside wick has opposite implications depending on whether the stock's downside exposure is already visible and fully sold, or whether tail dependence has only recently become apparent. The child goes long visibly high-semibeta names that have already capitulated into an absorbed wick, but shorts temporarily recovered high-conditional-beta names whose newly elevated tail dependence remains hidden and whose prior relative performance indicates liquidation is incomplete. This interaction carries edge because Parent A identifies dealer-mediated temporary recovery while Parent B identifies whether the risk has been visibly exhausted versus still being discovered by de-risking portfolios.
factors.name: Tail-Visibility Absorption Router

factors.trading_idea: Analysts often update revenue and EPS forecasts asynchronously because sales, pricing, cost, and margin assumptions are maintained in separate model sections. A same-direction update in one channel shortly after an update in the other is therefore a confirmation event: it signals a broad fundamental-model reset rather than a transitory headline revision, and prices should continue to adjust over the following week. The edge should persist because portfolio-manager model refreshes and analyst-note dissemination are staggered, while arbitrageurs cannot safely trade every isolated revision without distinguishing coherent business improvement from offsetting margin or accounting changes.
factors.name: Sequential Dual-Consensus Confirmation Drift

factors.trading_idea: Analysts and narrative-driven investors can extrapolate margin expansion more aggressively than revenue growth, particularly for expensive firms whose valuation embeds a long duration of future profitability. A positive EPS-consensus revision that substantially exceeds the concurrent revenue-consensus revision is therefore more likely to be an overvalued margin-expectation shock when forward earnings yield is low. The edge should persist because assessing whether a revision is supported by durable operating leverage requires slower fundamental interpretation than reacting to the headline revision, and the child is falsified if expensive margin-only revision names do not underperform over the following six sessions.
factors.name: Valuation-Weighted Margin Revision Extrapolation

factors.trading_idea: A downside volatility burst caused by deleveraging or liquidity-demand shocks should create a temporarily elevated sell-intensity state, but the economically relevant turning point is when that intensity decelerates while price impact per unit participation falls. This indicates that liquidity supply has replenished before the prior downside displacement has been fully repaired, so the residual rebound should occur over the next six trading days. The hypothesis is falsifiable: conditional on large recent downside displacement, names with high slow sell intensity, falling fast-versus-slow intensity, and declining impact should outperform equivalent displaced names without impact relaxation. The edge can persist because forced sellers, volatility-targeting flows, and dealer inventory rebuilding operate with multi-day execution and balance-sheet constraints rather than being instantaneously arbitraged away.
factors.name: Downside Variance Relaxation Rebound

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s positive realized IC suggests that a negative earnings surprise combined with intense downside activity is more often a forced-selling and inventory-transfer state than an unresolved information cascade. This child therefore goes long only when selling participation remains elevated but marginal downside price impact is falling relative to the immediately preceding phase: this is observable evidence that liquidity demand is being absorbed by patient buyers. The edge should persist because institutional de-risking and liquidity-provider inventory transfer occur over several days, while arbitrageurs cannot safely infer absorption from the earnings surprise alone. It is falsified if negative-surprise names with falling impact-per-participation do not outperform comparable negative-surprise names whose impact remains elevated.
factors.name: Bad-News Absorption Efficiency Reversal

factors.trading_idea: A sector shock creates a catch-up opportunity only when it is part of a self-exciting, high-participation information cascade rather than an isolated price move. The parent-style beta-adjusted underreaction signal is therefore conditioned on a Hawkes-like directional sector-shock intensity, constructed from prior same-sign sector shocks marked by abnormal sector turnover. This interaction identifies resilient, low-turnover names that have failed to absorb a propagating sector repricing; neither residual underreaction alone nor cascade intensity alone distinguishes delayed assimilation from a one-off idiosyncratic move.
factors.name: Sector Cascade Resilience Lag Assimilation

factors.trading_idea: An earnings and revenue surprise is more informative when it arrives from a pre-existing regime of internally funded growth: strong cash conversion and operating-cash-flow growth with limited dilution or debt dependence make a positive report more likely to represent durable demand rather than financially engineered expansion. Conversely, a jointly negative report is especially damaging when the firm already relies on external financing, because the disclosure raises both operating and funding-risk concerns. Neither parent alone distinguishes whether the immediate report shock is being transmitted through a credible financing state, creating an asymmetric six-day repricing channel.
factors.name: Financing-Credible Dual Surprise

factors.trading_idea: A cash-quality filing update supplies a directional information anchor, but the parent’s persistent low-entropy structure is mostly a mature execution state whose payoff arrives beyond six days. This child instead detects the initiation of a likely institutional execution schedule: a fresh acceleration in close-location-weighted participation immediately following a cash-quality revision, only when flow and the revision agree in sign. The edge should persist because liquidity providers and arbitrageurs cannot costlessly front-run a large, gradually executed order when its direction is inferred only probabilistically from a sparse filing update and noisy daily-bar flow; it is falsified if fresh aligned flow does not outperform equally signed but mature or unanchored flow over the next six bars.
factors.name: Cash Event Flow Initiation

factors.trading_idea: A market-wide fear episode is identified by broad negative returns, elevated cross-sectional downside dispersion, and unusually high aggregate volume. Stocks with historically high loading to these fear episodes are sold mechanically by risk-parity deleveraging, ETF flows, and discretionary de-risking, but financially defensive firms with strong cash buffers and low leverage have less fundamental reason to remain impaired. The factor buys defensive firms experiencing an unusually negative fear-beta residual and shorts fragile firms with a positive or weakly negative residual. It fails if balance-sheet strength does not distinguish the post-fear return of stocks with similar realized downside sensitivity.
factors.name: Downside Fear Beta with Balance-Sheet Defense

factors.trading_idea: Broad fear makes signed high-participation return events ambiguous: they can be forced liquidation in cash-generative firms or information-driven repricing in firms with weak refinancing capacity. The child only trades a fear-beta residual once same-direction marked flow has clustered and then cooled, treating a resilient firm's completed sell program as a temporary displacement while treating a fragile firm's completed buy impulse as an unsustainable defensive bid. Neither parent alone distinguishes a residual shock from a completed directional liquidity episode whose likely reversal is determined by the issuer's ability to self-fund through stress.
factors.name: Fear-Flow Completion Funding Asymmetry

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s realized sign indicates that apparent downside cascades were more often liquidity-vacuum dislocations than persistent informed selling at the six-day horizon. This child measures whether a large intrabar sell excursion is actively absorbed: price must recover materially from its low while trading participation is elevated, and repeated absorption builds a short-lived inventory reservoir that predicts subsequent recovery. The edge can persist because liquidity providers and value-sensitive buyers cannot instantaneously rebalance inventory and capital after several absorption episodes; it is falsified if high absorption states do not precede positive six-day returns, or if the relationship is equally strong when the bar closes near its low.
factors.name: Intrabar Absorption Reservoir

factors.trading_idea: Within an industry, a broad peer-price advance accompanied by improving peer revenue or EPS expectations is often assimilated unevenly over several days. A lagging stock with a strong liquidity buffer and modest leverage is more likely to be a temporary attention or implementation lag than a distressed-value trap, whereas an equally lagging highly levered firm may rationally fail to catch up. The factor buys financially resilient laggards behind an industry move and shorts resilient names that have overshot their peer move without superior fundamental revisions. This mechanism is falsified if solvency conditioning does not improve the catch-up rate relative to an unconditioned industry-relative-return signal.
factors.name: Solvency-Screened Industry Leader-Lag Catch-up

factors.trading_idea: Industry-relative price momentum is most credible when analyst EPS revisions point in the same direction, but consensus confirmation alone can still reflect extrapolative belief disagreement in names with fragile cash conversion. The child amplifies confirmed trends only when a recent cash-cycle and liquidity update validates the trend direction, while reducing exposure to names whose recent returns are dominated by downside-tail realizations. This interaction separates gradual fundamental information diffusion from momentum that is merely compensation for heavy-tailed distress risk or a price response unsupported by cash realization.
factors.name: Tail-Robust Cash-Validated Revision Trend

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s positive realized IC suggests that a negative-surprise sell cascade is typically observed late in the liquidation process rather than at its onset: after an initial forced selloff, downside intensity decays while price impact falls despite still-elevated participation. This is a critical-cascade extinction state in which liquidity providers have absorbed much of the constrained supply and marginal sellers become scarce, creating a six-day rebound even though the fundamental news was adverse. The edge can persist because institutional de-risking, inventory transfer, and liquidity replenishment are slower than an arbitrageur’s ability to recognize an already-exhausted price-impact regime. It is falsified if names with negative earnings news, decelerating downside excitation, and falling impact per unit volume do not subsequently outperform after controlling for the earnings-surprise magnitude.
factors.name: Post-Shock Impact Resilience Release

factors.trading_idea: Analyst revenue and EPS revisions often arrive sequentially because demand assumptions are updated before margin, tax, and share-count assumptions are reconciled. A second same-direction revision in the other channel resolves this ambiguity and should diffuse into portfolio valuations over the following week, whereas simultaneous or isolated changes are more likely to be immediately incorporated or mechanically driven. This is falsifiable: six-day IC should be concentrated after temporally ordered, concordant cross-channel updates and should disappear for conflicting second updates. The edge can persist because analyst-model revision workflows and institutional earnings-model updates are asynchronous, making the confirmation event slower to aggregate than a single headline revision.
factors.name: Sequential Estimate Confirmation Diffusion

factors.trading_idea: An abrupt increase in idiosyncratic downside semivariance is more informative when a firm has both high leverage and a thin cash liquidity buffer: negative shocks then raise collateral, refinancing, and risk-capacity concerns rather than merely reflecting a transitory market move. Constrained holders and lenders reduce exposure gradually, so high fragility-weighted downside-volatility innovation should predict negative six-bar returns. The edge can persist because balance-sheet constraints and the distinction between systematic versus name-specific bad-news volatility are not directly tradable, while short-sale risk and crash exposure limit immediate arbitrage. This is falsified if downside-volatility innovations have no more negative subsequent return among cash-poor, levered firms than among well-funded firms.
factors.name: Funding-Fragility Downside Variance Innovation

factors.trading_idea: A severe downside range shock that closes near the day's low is more likely to continue over the fixed six-day horizon when the issuer has both high debt dependence and little liquid-asset coverage. This separates genuine bad-news/deleveraging cascades from the parent's isolated thin-book shocks, which should repair rather than persist. The edge persists because public balance-sheet data is slow-moving but its interaction with a sudden price-impact state is costly for arbitrageurs to warehouse: constrained investors and dealers tend to reduce exposure gradually after the shock. The hypothesis is falsified if, after matching on drawdown and range magnitude, highly indebted low-cash firms do not underperform financially resilient firms over the next six bars.
factors.name: Fragile Balance-Sheet Downside Cascade

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s positive realized IC implies that a recurrent downside-shock cluster is more often a late-stage liquidation state than an active continuation state: once the marked sell intensity begins to decay, marginal sellers have been depleted. A close in the upper part of a high-volume daily range indicates that residual supply is being absorbed rather than that the price is simply bouncing on thin liquidity, creating a tradable release over the next six bars. The edge should persist because inventory transfer, risk-limit liquidation, and dealer replenishment occur gradually; it is falsified if mature declining sell clusters with high-close absorption do not outperform equivalent clusters lacking absorption after controlling for recent returns and volatility.
factors.name: Endogenous Sell Decay Absorption

factors.trading_idea: Earnings announcements reveal information not only about the reporting firm but also about demand, costs, and competitive conditions for its sector peers. A sector-level surprise should diffuse most strongly into peers whose recent sector-relative price reaction is in the wrong direction or absent, because analysts and benchmarked investors must map issuer-specific news into peer-level earnings implications over several sessions. The edge should persist because this inference is noisy and heterogeneous across firms, making immediate arbitrage difficult; it is falsified if peers that initially underreact to signed sector earnings news do not subsequently move in the direction of that news over the next six sessions.
factors.name: Peer Earnings Underreaction Relay

factors.trading_idea: Fundamental news with high turnover but incomplete price conversion is usually interpreted as delayed incorporation, but this inference changes when the stock is already in a downside-excitation state. In that state, high volume without range expansion is more plausibly liquidity-provider absorption of informed distribution and temporary price support than benign institutional accumulation; positive unconverted news subsequently unwinds, while negative news that fails to fall can rebound after hidden selling pressure exhausts.
