The interaction has edge because a conversion gap alone cannot distinguish attention-driven drift from adverse-selection absorption, while absorption alone lacks the fundamental-news anchor needed to identify which suppressed price response is likely to reverse over the next six days.
factors.name: Asymmetric Absorption Conversion Unwind

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth risk makes investor risk aversion rise nonlinearly after aggregate downside-tail days, causing constrained investors to sell equities broadly before differentiating firms by their ability to survive weak demand and tight financing. The child goes long high-free-cash-flow-yield, low-debt firms with low estimated downside market beta, and short their fragile tail-sensitive counterparts, but only during an acute market-tail state. The edge should persist because rare-state risk reallocation, mandate-driven deleveraging, and delayed balance-sheet discrimination cannot be costlessly arbitraged in the first trading week. It is falsified if, conditional on market downside-tail shocks, cash-rich low-tail-beta firms do not outperform cash-poor high-tail-beta firms over the subsequent six bars within industries.
factors.name: Tail-State Cash Resilience Rotation

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s negative IC suggests that apparent intraday absorption after panic selling is more often temporary relief inside an unresolved deleveraging episode than a completed reversal. This child models fear as a self-exciting downside-jump process: repeated abnormal negative returns with abnormal participation raise the hazard of further forced selling, especially when the latest bar closes near its low and therefore shows acceptance rather than rejection of the lower price. The edge should persist because investors cannot reliably distinguish a transient liquidity shock from a continuing redemption, margin, or risk-limit cascade in real time, while short-sale and inventory constraints slow arbitrage. It is falsified if names with the highest accelerating downside-excitation hazard do not have more-negative sector-relative returns over the following six bars.
factors.name: Downside Jump Excitation Hazard

factors.trading_idea: Aggregate heavy-left-tail states make investors especially sensitive to hidden cash-flow fragility, but Parent A's broad resilience signal can be crowded and ambiguously priced. This child trades fresh quality disclosures only when they contradict recent industry-relative price action and when the firm-specific quiet-path/financial-fragility state identifies whether the disclosure resolves latent tail exposure: bad news in fragile, compressed-risk firms should continue down, while good news in resilient firms that have underperformed should catch up. The interaction carries edge because the tail regime supplies the discount-rate urgency, while the contradiction and balance-sheet state identify the particular names for which the market has not yet incorporated the disclosure.
factors.name: Tail-Regime Quality Dissonance Resolution

factors.trading_idea: The child buys stocks whose selling is unusually negative relative to their trailing market-fear beta, but only when the residual sell cascade has begun to decay rather than accelerate. Parent B supplies the idiosyncratic overshoot test, while Parent A supplies the temporal confirmation that marginal forced sellers are exhausted; sector-relative balance-sheet resilience separates a reversible flow dislocation from a valid funding-risk repricing. This interaction has edge because a negative residual alone can still be informed bad news, whereas decaying residual excitation in a financially resilient issuer is more consistent with temporary de-risking pressure.
factors.name: Fear Residual Decay Repair

factors.trading_idea: A concentrated-volume transaction anchor identifies the latent cost basis at which disposition-driven supply and demand should pull price back toward equilibrium. The child trades that anchor reversion only when compressed, high-participation close-location pressure points toward the anchor but has not yet produced net displacement, indicating that the relevant flow is currently being absorbed rather than already incorporated into price. The interaction resolves Parent B's ambiguous standalone pressure direction: pressure is not treated as a universal continuation signal, but as confirmation that the specific anchor-restoring flow implied by Parent A is active and temporarily constrained.
factors.name: Anchor-Confirmed Absorption Reversion

factors.trading_idea: Prices respond viscoelastically to unusually large trading-volume impulses: when prior high-participation price shocks have repeatedly retained their sign over subsequent days, current volume-confirmed shocks are more likely to represent slowly propagated information rather than temporary inventory pressure. The factor estimates this stock-specific relaxation kernel from only past impulse-response pairs and takes the direction of the current abnormal-volume return only when persistence is positive. This is falsifiable because future returns conditional on a positive estimated relaxation kernel should exceed those following otherwise identical shocks with zero or negative kernel estimates; the effect can persist because institutional execution and gradual common-shock incorporation are intermittent and costly to infer in real time.
factors.name: Volume-Impulse Relaxation Memory

factors.trading_idea: A high-turnover rebound during market fear is not uniformly a short-covering trap: it is more likely to persist when it follows a coherent, low-impact sell program, because repeated selling without proportional price displacement indicates that patient buyers have absorbed forced supply. Valuation stretch makes the rebound controversial and slows fundamental arbitrage, while the absorbed liquidation identifies the state in which the relief move reflects completed de-risking rather than a transient liquidity bounce. Parent B alone cannot distinguish genuine supply exhaustion from short-covering, and Parent A alone does not isolate the crisis-state rebound at which absorbed sell pressure converts into positive continuation.
factors.name: Fear Relief Sell-Absorption Confirmation

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s negative result is consistent with high-volume close-location pressure being largely closing-auction inventory transfer, which can reverse rather than continue. This child instead identifies a different mechanism: an intraday directional move whose price impact per unit of float turnover is rising relative to the name’s own square-root-impact baseline, indicating progressive depletion or cancellation of available liquidity rather than merely high participation. If displayed and latent depth are being exhausted by a continuing informed execution program, marginal impact should rise over consecutive sessions and returns should continue in that direction; the hypothesis is falsified if rising float-normalized impact convexity has no directional six-day continuation once ordinary volume shocks are excluded. The edge can persist because estimating latent depth depletion from daily turnover and impact requires inventory-risk-bearing arbitrage, while liquidity providers cannot instantly restore depth under adverse-selection risk.
factors.name: Float-Normalized Impact Convexity

factors.trading_idea: During a broad synchronized downside shock, basket and index-linked selling is transmitted first to industry constituents with high historical sensitivity to peer returns. A stock whose recent trading capacity is unusually low relative to its own normal volume cannot absorb this cross-impact efficiently, so peer-driven selling should continue to transmit into its price over the next week. The edge should persist because passive basket flows and liquidity-provider inventory constraints act mechanically, while arbitrageurs face execution risk precisely when available trading capacity is scarce; falsifiably, the negative continuation should be concentrated in high peer-beta, low-capacity names after broad downside shocks and disappear outside that state.
factors.name: Common-Mode Cross-Impact Capacity Lag

factors.trading_idea: A broad industry shock is often incorporated first through liquid basket constituents, while names trading below their normal participation rate can initially underreact because sparse liquidity raises the cost of immediate arbitrage and inventory transfer. The child measures a stock's beta-adjusted shortfall versus its industry's common return shock and emphasizes underresponses occurring with subdued relative dollar-volume participation. This is falsifiable: conditional on a material industry shock, a positive signed response gap should predict positive six-bar catch-up returns only among low-participation names; the effect should disappear or weaken for names trading at elevated participation.
factors.name: Common-Shock Sparse Response Gap

factors.trading_idea: A persistent directional institutional order program should generate elevated but regular participation, while passive limit-order supply gradually replenishes and reduces price impact per unit of traded activity. Falling impact elasticity during a still-directional, stable-volume program indicates that the program is not yet complete rather than that a one-off liquidity shock is reversing. The edge persists because outside arbitrageurs observe only aggregate daily bars, cannot directly observe the parent order's remaining size, and face adverse-selection risk when supplying liquidity; it is falsified if impact-compressing directional programs do not continue more than equally directional programs with unstable participation or rising impact.
factors.name: Elasticity-Decay Execution Drift

factors.trading_idea: Revenue surprises within an industry reveal a common demand shock, but its implications diffuse gradually as peer firms report on different dates. Firms with high SG&A intensity have greater operating leverage to the same revenue shock, so a positive peer-surprise state should be especially underpriced when their own return has lagged the peer basket; the reverse holds for negative shocks. The edge can persist because investors initially process each earnings release as issuer-specific and need subsequent peer disclosures to distinguish an industry demand shock from idiosyncratic noise. This is falsified if peer revenue-surprise states do not predict six-bar catch-up returns most strongly among high-SG&A firms with weak contemporaneous relative-price responses.
factors.name: Peer Revenue Shock Operating-Leverage Lag

factors.trading_idea: Sparse-liquidity price formation can create a measurable hysteresis loop between signed abnormal trading activity and subsequent price changes: when signed volume repeatedly leads returns, latent execution pressure is being transmitted into prices with delay rather than immediately cleared. The child goes long positive current flow when the trailing price-flow loop shows flow leading price, and short negative flow under the same condition; opposite loop orientation implies that volume is predominantly a reaction to past price moves and reverses the signal. This is falsified if the sign of current signed abnormal volume does not predict six-day returns more strongly when its trailing phase-space orientation indicates a flow-leading regime. The edge can persist because identifying the direction of the response loop requires aggregating noisy daily range, close-location, volume-surprise, and lagged-path information, while liquidity suppliers and benchmarked execution traders react to the imbalance incrementally.
factors.name: Phase-Space Flow Lead Hysteresis

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s adverse sign is consistent with isolated price-opposed consensus changes being stale analyst reactions to a price move rather than newly discovered information. This child instead selects revisions that are reinforced across both EPS and revenue estimates and have persisted through two successive estimate-update intervals, while the stock’s idiosyncratic price response remains muted. Such coherent, repeated fundamental-model updates should diffuse into institutional portfolios over the following week because reconciling revenue and earnings revisions across analysts is slower than reacting to a single consensus change; the hypothesis is falsified if coherent revisions with muted initial price response do not outperform incoherent or already-price-reflected revisions at six days.
factors.name: Dual-Channel Revision Inertia

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s negative IC indicates that high-volume idiosyncratic downside shocks were more often information-bearing or parts of persistent institutional sell programs than exhausted forced-liquidation events. This child treats repeated residual downside shocks, abnormal participation, and closes near the daily low as marked self-exciting sell events: a recent cluster implies that the latent seller or information diffusion process remains active, so subsequent returns should remain weak. The edge can persist because short sellers and liquidity providers face adverse-selection risk, borrow constraints, and execution costs while a metaorder or gradual repricing unfolds; it is falsified if high marked-event intensity does not predict more-negative six-day sector-neutral returns after controlling for the current residual return and volume shock.
factors.name: Idiosyncratic Sell-Excitation Continuation

factors.trading_idea: A dilution-funded, expensive rally is most vulnerable immediately after a newly available filing makes the dilution information salient, rather than throughout the entire quarter. The child gates Parent B's persistent valuation-and-dilution fragility by Parent A's fresh-disclosure and attention state, and further requires a downside-tail-heavy return history: under heavy-tailed cash-flow-risk beliefs, investors demand a sharper repricing once attention shifts from headline growth to per-share claims. Neither parent alone distinguishes stale fragility from an imminent disclosure-processing event occurring in a state where downside-risk beliefs make the unwind more discontinuous.
factors.name: Tail-State Fresh Dilution Unwind

factors.trading_idea: Both parents’ negative realized signs suggest that an apparently absorbed sell program and subsequent volume cooling are often not completed forced-sale inventory transfer, but a temporary dealer-supported recovery while systematic downside risk is still being repriced. The child isolates this adverse case: a decayed idiosyncratic sell-arrival cluster must have muted impact and apparent liquidity release, but only receives a high score when downside beta has recently risen relative to ordinary beta, indicating newly discovered rather than already-visible tail exposure. This interaction has edge because sell-flow release alone confuses completion with distribution, while tail-beta discovery alone does not identify the mechanically supported recovery that gives portfolios time to de-risk over the next six bars.
factors.name: Hidden-Tail Release Distribution Trap

factors.trading_idea: Momentum and benchmark-constrained investors often reward headline earnings growth and high-volume rallies while treating adjusted EPS as more salient than the economic cost of stock compensation and persistent share issuance. A rally is more fragile when it coincides with rising sharesOutstanding, high sbcToRevenue, weak freeCashFlowYield, and an expensive enterprise-value multiple: the apparent growth is being partly financed by outside equity holders. The signal shorts the most expensive dilution-backed rallies and buys fundamentally cash-generative, non-dilutive names that have lagged; it is falsified if the dilution interaction adds no negative forward return beyond valuation or momentum alone.
factors.name: Dilution-Funded Rally Unwind

factors.trading_idea: The paper's entropy result implies that persistent flow is informative about the arrival of information but does not itself reveal direction. Quarterly improvements in cash realization relative to accounting earnings provide a slow-moving directional anchor: institutions can accumulate firms whose earnings have become more cash-backed, while analysts and benchmarked investors update only gradually after the filing. Buy low-entropy upward price-volume structures following an improvement in income quality or operating-cash-flow growth, and short the mirror image of orderly distribution following deteriorating cash quality; the effect is falsified if the interaction adds no six-day drift beyond the fundamental update and price-volume structure separately.
factors.name: Cash-Quality Confirmed Accumulation

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s negative realized sign suggests that repeated high-participation intraday pressure in daily data is more often a temporary liquidity-demand footprint than an unfinished metaorder. This child isolates terminal episodes in which signed intraday impact was coherent and unusually large, but the price movement delivered per unit of relative participation is now falling: passive liquidity has begun replenishing while the aggressive schedule loses marginal ability to move the price. The expected six-bar return is opposite the earlier pressure because dealers gradually unwind inventory and the residual temporary impact decays; this is falsifiable because reversal should occur only after impact elasticity decelerates, not for equally directional high-volume episodes whose impact remains stable or accelerates.
factors.name: Participation-Elasticity Decay Reversal

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth shocks should appear as clustered, unusually large revenue and earnings surprises among economically related firms rather than as isolated idiosyncratic events. A fresh firm-level tail surprise that agrees with a recently accumulating industry-peer surprise state is more likely to represent slowly incorporated common-demand information, so its sign should persist over the next six trading days. The edge can persist because quarterly disclosures arrive asynchronously, investors face costly interpretation of whether an extreme result is firm-specific or demand-wide, and peer confirmation resolves that disagreement only gradually.
factors.name: Clustered Tail Surprise Diffusion

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s positive realized IC implies that cash-confirmed surprises accompanied by unchanged consensus are not temporary overreactions: they are disclosures whose information is incorporated gradually. This child explicitly isolates the underreaction case, where the signed fundamental surprise is large but the contemporaneous price response is small relative to comparable stocks, while cash-flow innovation validates that the news is economically meaningful. The prediction is falsifiable: conditional on a new disclosure and analyst silence, high positive reaction-shortfall scores should earn positive six-bar returns, high negative scores should earn negative returns, and the effect should weaken when the initial price response already matches the surprise. The edge can persist because interpreting cash-flow versus accrual information and revising models is slower and more institutionally costly than reacting to an earnings headline.
factors.name: Cash-Confirmed Reaction Shortfall Drift

factors.trading_idea: Investors and analysts initially anchor on the headline EPS surprise, but a report whose revenue surprise and operating-cash-flow growth contradict the EPS result requires slower interpretation of margins, costs, and accruals. Long firms with stronger sales and cash conversion than their EPS surprise implies, and short firms with EPS strength unsupported by sales or cash conversion. The edge should persist because quarterly disclosure reconciliation is attention-intensive and revisions occur after the initial headline reaction; it is falsified if the conditional return spread vanishes once sales and cash-flow information are included alongside EPS surprise.
factors.name: Cash-Sales Earnings Wedge Reappraisal

factors.trading_idea: An opening gap that is strongly rejected during the day is most informative when it moves against an already self-exciting, high-participation peer-sector repricing cascade. In that state, the sector move supplies a credible directional information prior while the opposite-signed, low-validation opening gap identifies a temporary auction or inventory dislocation in the individual name. Parent A alone cannot distinguish a false gap from a reversal of genuine news, while Parent B alone cannot identify the specific name-level auction mispricing that creates an unusually clean catch-up entry.
factors.name: Peer Cascade-Conditioned Gap Rejection

factors.trading_idea: A favourable industry-peer earnings impulse is most underpriced when a stock has been temporarily held down by a now-clearing, high-volume downside cascade rather than by a concurrent firm-specific disclosure. The fading cascade supplies the forced-flow state from Parent A, while the peer impulse supplies the directional fundamental anchor from Parent B; together they identify names where selling prevented incorporation of relevant peer information and whose rebound has an externally validated direction. Unlike a standalone panic-reversal trade, the signal does not buy exhausted selling without positive fundamental read-through, and unlike a generic peer relay, it concentrates on the subset with a mechanically delayed price response.
factors.name: Peer Disclosure Cascade Clearance Relay

factors.trading_idea: Downside order-flow excitation should continue rather than mean-revert when a stock is both expensive relative to sector peers and already in a sector-relative weak price phase: the valuation anchor gives fundamental investors little reason to absorb forced selling, while negative momentum confirms beliefs are being revised downward. Conversely, the same liquidity-driven sell shock in cheap or improving names is more likely to find value-sensitive buyers and become a transient dislocation. The interaction therefore isolates cascades whose microstructural selling pressure is reinforced by the cross-sectional valuation-and-belief state, rather than treating every thin-volume decline as equally persistent.
factors.name: Valuation-Gated Downside Cascade

factors.trading_idea: A change in analyst EPS consensus is a discrete public-information arrival, and its scale relative to price approximates the contemporaneous change in expected earnings yield. Revisions arriving on abnormally low dollar volume receive less immediate investor attention and should therefore exhibit stronger six-day continuation, with positive innovations outperforming and negative innovations underperforming. The edge can persist because sparse estimate updates and costly event monitoring leave low-salience revisions incompletely incorporated; it is falsified if revision-yield innovations have no stronger forward-return relation when contemporaneous trading attention is low.
factors.name: Attention-Discounted Forecast Innovation

factors.trading_idea: A revenue- and margin-confirmed earnings surprise is most informative when a coherent industry move independently points in the same direction, establishing that the disclosure is part of a broader common-information shock rather than an idiosyncratic headline. The child only retains this verified news when the reporting stock has both underreacted relative to peers and traded below normal participation, indicating that its quote has not yet joined the industry-wide repricing. Neither parent alone distinguishes a merely muted earnings reaction from a delayed cross-name transmission channel in which peer action validates the news while low participation prevents immediate arbitrage.
factors.name: Verified Event Peer Relay Gap

factors.trading_idea: Quiet, concordant analyst revisions should drift most reliably when they confirm a pre-existing valuation anchor and the price phase has already begun moving in the same direction. A positive low-attention revision in a cheap, sector-outperforming stock represents gradual fundamental re-rating, while a negative revision in an expensive, sector-underperforming stock identifies an unwind with limited immediate attention. Neither parent alone distinguishes revisions that reinforce an economically credible valuation-path transition from revisions that merely arrive in already-dislocated or contradictory price states.
factors.name: Valuation-Phase Gated Quiet Revision

factors.trading_idea: Large opening dislocations that continue in the same direction through the close on unusually high participation are more likely to reflect an institutional execution schedule or information-bearing auction imbalance than a transient opening liquidity shock. The close-to-open continuation indicates that opposite-side liquidity did not absorb the auction imbalance, so the residual parent order and slow-moving liquidity-provider inventory adjustment should extend the move over the next week. This edge persists because institutional orders are split across days and auction information is costly to infer in real time; it is falsified if high-volume, directionally confirmed opening gaps do not have more signed 6-bar drift than equally large gaps that are absorbed intraday.
factors.name: Opening Auction Unabsorbed Metaorder Drift

factors.trading_idea: Analyst estimate changes are most actionable when price has not yet acknowledged them, but the persistence of that information depends on the firm's capital-allocation credibility. Positive unassimilated revisions should transmit more reliably for cheap firms funding repurchases from free cash flow, whereas negative unassimilated revisions should be more damaging for expensive firms relying on debt-supported repurchases. The interaction creates edge because the revision identifies the information shock while the allocation state distinguishes durable per-share compounding from fragile financial engineering.
factors.name: Revision Allocation Transmission Lag

factors.trading_idea: A broad range-volume shock signals a temporary withdrawal of liquidity provision, but the parent report suggests its impact-deficit branch resolves too slowly for a six-day target. This child instead identifies the transition out of that state: systemic stress breadth has peaked and is falling, while a stock still trades unusually high volume in a compressed range, indicating that replenished liquidity is absorbing rather than extending its earlier idiosyncratic displacement. The prediction is a six-bar reversal of the pre-release idiosyncratic move; it is falsified if compressed high-participation trading after a breadth release continues in the prior direction. The edge can persist because dealer inventory rebalancing and restoration of displayed liquidity occur gradually after a common shock, while immediate arbitrageurs cannot directly observe the latent inventory that produced the displacement.
factors.name: Systemic Release Absorption Displacement

factors.trading_idea: A positive revenue surprise with deteriorating cash conversion creates a plausible but low-quality headline that investors may initially extrapolate. The child factor only fades an upside price acceleration when that disclosure-quality warning is fresh and the move occurs on weak relative participation, identifying a particularly fragile repricing rather than treating every low-volume acceleration as noise. The interaction carries edge because poor conversion makes the headline fundamentally suspect, while low participation indicates that the market has not received broad informed confirmation of the price response.
factors.name: Disclosure-Quality Gated Attention Exhaustion

factors.trading_idea: A sustained collapse in the entropy of volume allocated to up versus down days identifies directional trading pressure that is unlikely to be generated by diffuse, symmetric noise. When this directional volume imbalance has produced unusually little cumulative price displacement, liquidity suppliers appear to be temporarily warehousing the flow; the eventual reduction of that inventory buffer should produce a same-direction catch-up over the next several days. This is falsifiable: conditional on high directional-volume concentration and low impact efficiency, future returns should follow the volume-implied direction, while the effect should disappear when the same flow already has a large cumulative price displacement. The edge can persist because daily-bar participants observe only an aggregated proxy for latent order-flow persistence, while liquidity provision, capital constraints, and execution scheduling delay full price discovery.
factors.name: Directional Volume Entropy Impact Deficit

factors.trading_idea: When volatility is unusually synchronized across a stock's sector, market-maker risk limits and investor attention are consumed by common-sector repricing, reducing capacity to process idiosyncratic earnings information. A coherent EPS-and-revenue surprise with an initially muted signed price response should therefore drift in the surprise direction over the following six days, especially when the sector's common volatility is elevated. This is falsifiable: conditional on coherent report events, subsequent returns should be increasing in surprise sign times the synchrony-and-muted-response score, while the same surprise should have materially less drift during low-synchrony sector states. The edge can persist because the conditioning variable is an episodic inventory and attention-capacity constraint, rather than publicly arbitrageable directional momentum.
factors.name: Sector-Synchrony Congested Surprise Drift

factors.trading_idea: Fresh operational-quality disclosures are most informative when they contradict a smooth, visually persuasive industry-relative price trend: investors extrapolate the clean trend before fully processing the harder-to-interpret change in ROIC, cash-flow quality, or margins. The disagreement is amplified in names with an unusually downside-heavy recent return distribution, a market-based proxy for heavy-tailed consumption-risk concerns and heterogeneous beliefs, because tail-sensitive investors reprioritize fundamental resilience after the disclosure. Unlike Parent A, the child preserves the directional sign of the quality update rather than multiplying it by any opposite price move; unlike Parent B, it only trades disagreement when a newly available quality event resolves the trend narrative.
factors.name: Tail-Gated Quality Trend Disagreement

factors.trading_idea: Common-shock regimes induce broad de-risking, but the quality premium is strongest when idiosyncratic abnormal trading is demonstrably converting into directional price impulses rather than being balanced liquidity provision. The child therefore conditions the defensive quality spread on a signed attention-to-price conversion state: it emphasizes high-quality firms receiving buy-side conversion and fragile firms receiving sell-side conversion during market synchrony. Parent A identifies when flight-to-quality is economically relevant, while Parent B distinguishes whether contemporaneous volume reflects executable, propagating order-flow pressure; their alignment identifies the subset of systemic reallocations likely to continue over the fixed six-bar horizon.
factors.name: Synchrony-Confirmed Quality Flow

factors.trading_idea: Fresh dilution disclosures are most likely to be mispriced when investors are extrapolating a currently rewarded quality/value mode and the stock has captured an unusually large share of its industry's recent upside tail. Attention-heavy positive reactions then reflect disagreement concentrated in a small set of narrative winners, a cross-sectional analogue of heavy-tailed consumption-belief shocks, while dilution and SBC information remain underweighted. Parent B identifies the disclosure-processing error, whereas Parent A supplies the crowded peer-relative state: the interaction isolates cases where a favorable fundamental narrative has made the initial reaction especially vulnerable to a six-bar unwind.
factors.name: Disclosure Tail-Mode Overcapture Unwind

factors.trading_idea: A rejected downward opening gap is most informative when it occurs after persistent, high-volume sector-wide sell arrivals: the prior flow identifies a common deleveraging or redemption regime, while the auction rejection identifies the moment that forced supply fails to obtain further price acceptance. Parent A alone cannot distinguish a routine idiosyncratic gap fade from a liquidation episode, and Parent B alone cannot time when a persistent sell program has become exhausted. Their interaction targets names where systemic selling pressure remains elevated but the opening auction has begun to clear at an anomalously poor, weakly validated price.
factors.name: Common-Flow Auction Rejection Repair

factors.trading_idea: A positive EPS surprise accompanied by a large, high-volume idiosyncratic sell-off on a calm market day is not delayed good-news absorption: it is an informed veto of a stale accounting headline. Sophisticated investors may be reacting to forward guidance, order trends, or balance-sheet information that is not captured by the consensus surprise, while slower investors initially anchor on the headline beat. The signal should predict lower six-day returns because the valuation reconciliation takes several sessions, and it persists because the relevant qualitative or forward-looking information is costly to extract and difficult to arbitrage immediately.
factors.name: Calm-Market Informed Earnings Veto

factors.trading_idea: Large informed or institutional orders are commonly split across days to limit footprint. A persistent directional sequence of close-location-weighted participation, when each unit of participation is moving price unusually little, indicates demand that has not exhausted displayed liquidity and is therefore likely to continue over the next week; high-impact bursts instead resemble forced or exhausted flow and are down-weighted. The edge should persist because the parent order, its urgency, and hidden liquidity are not directly observable from daily bars, while fully arbitraging the signal requires accepting inventory and adverse-selection risk; it is falsified if the score has no forward-return relation after controlling for recent return, realized volatility, and volume surprise.
factors.name: Sliced Flow Impact Reserve

factors.trading_idea: A recurrent downside-innovation cluster identifies the same endogenous selling state as Parent A, but cluster intensity alone mixes an actively accelerating liquidation with a mature, overshot cascade. The child goes long only when recurrence has established that the selloff was a genuine cluster and the volume-marked sell intensity is now decelerating while participation cools, indicating that forced supply is being exhausted and dealer inventory can be replenished. This phase interaction has edge because deceleration is informative only after verified self-excitation: an isolated quiet down day is not a liquidation completion, while an active high-intensity cluster remains vulnerable to further forced selling.
factors.name: Recurrent Downside Cluster Deceleration Repair

factors.trading_idea: Earnings information is incorporated less completely when the market receives an unusually dense cluster of reports, because analyst and investor attention is rationed across simultaneous disclosures. A confirmed surprise should therefore drift in its economically credible direction when the initial idiosyncratic reaction is muted, while debt-financed buyback engineering reverses the interpretation of otherwise positive headline news. The hypothesis is falsifiable: the six-day signal should be concentrated on report dates with an elevated standardized market-wide report count and should disappear on isolated report dates; the edge can persist because episodic attention capacity and costly fundamental verification cannot be instantaneously arbitraged.
factors.name: Report-Cluster Credibility Bottleneck

factors.trading_idea: A positive EPS beat that materially exceeds the revenue surprise is most vulnerable when it arrives after stale analyst expectations and an already deteriorating operating-margin trend. The child additionally requires an unusually strong immediate price response relative to the stock's pre-event volatility, identifying cases where investors have embraced the salient EPS headline before processing the weak demand and margin context. Neither parent alone distinguishes a merely ambiguous result from one that has already been over-capitalized into price while consensus remains anchored to obsolete profitability assumptions; that interaction should create a sharper six-bar reversal.
factors.name: Stale Headline Euphoria Margin Unwind

factors.trading_idea: The parent treated repeated revisions as confirmation, but repeated same-direction estimate maintenance can instead mark a mature and already-priced analyst consensus. This child isolates a fresh forecast innovation: an EPS and/or revenue estimate change that is large relative to that issuer's own prior estimate-update scale, with extra weight when both forecast channels agree. The edge should persist for roughly a week because model revisions are published discretely while portfolio managers and slower fundamental investors must assess whether a large cross-channel change alters their valuation case; it is falsified if the top-ranked fresh innovations do not outperform the bottom-ranked innovations over the next six bars after controlling for event-day returns.
factors.name: Cross-Channel Forecast Innovation Diffusion

factors.trading_idea: Daily close locations encode which side of each day's auction retained control after intraday bargaining. A persistent directional sequence of close locations combined with compressed realized ranges indicates that liquidity suppliers are repeatedly accommodating one-sided demand without fully repricing the stock; once their inventory tolerance is depleted, prices should drift in the direction of the latent imbalance over the following week. This is falsifiable: conditional forward returns should be positive for persistent high-close-location sequences and negative for persistent low-close-location sequences, with the effect concentrated when range compression is high; the edge can persist because dealer inventory accommodation and fragmented investor execution are costly and issuer-specific rather than instantly arbitraged.
factors.name: Ordinal Auction Imbalance Release

factors.trading_idea: Newly reported net buybacks financed by free cash flow rather than debt are a credible signal that management has private confidence in durable earnings capacity, and they mechanically increase per-share claim growth that analysts often incorporate only gradually. Conversely, equity issuance or debt-financed payout signals financing pressure and should precede weaker returns. This is falsifiable: among new quarterly filings, a portfolio sorted on cash-funded net-payout capacity should have positive six-day residual IC even after controlling for earnings-surprise and short-run price-response factors; the edge persists because financing-source reconciliation is less salient than headline earnings and requires combining separate cash-flow and financing statements.
factors.name: Cash-Funded Net Payout Capacity

factors.trading_idea: Information avoidance should be strongest when a new fundamental disclosure is difficult to translate into an earnings forecast: intangible-heavy firms, high-SBC firms, and businesses with volatile working-capital requirements require more analyst effort than a headline earnings number. When operational fundamentals update materially but consensus forecasts remain unchanged, the market is likely to incorporate the information only gradually as coverage catches up. The trade is falsified if unchanged estimates after such disclosures do not predict later revisions or if the conditional return effect is no stronger in high-complexity firms.
factors.name: Complexity-Gated Forecast Silence Drift

factors.trading_idea: Forced selling during broad fear is self-exciting: a large negative, high-volume return raises near-term sell intensity, but the intensity decays quickly once marginal sellers are exhausted. The child goes long firms where a still-elevated slow panic intensity exceeds its fast intensity, indicating recent capitulation is fading, and where cash, liquidity, operating cash flow, and conservative leverage make a forced-sale rebound credible. The edge should persist because constrained de-risking and redemption-driven sales respond to recent price and flow pressure rather than issuer-specific solvency, while fundamental investors require time to recognize that the surviving issuer is mispriced. It is falsified if financially resilient names with decaying downside-excitation intensity do not outperform fragile names or names with continuing excitation over the following six sessions.
factors.name: Exhausted Panic Buffer Repair (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: Broad, coherent industry returns often reflect a shared demand or cost shock rather than firm-specific news. Firms with high fixed operating commitments and slow inventory turnover have greater operating leverage, so their earnings sensitivity to that shock is initially underappreciated and their relative returns should continue to amplify over the following week. The edge persists because correctly mapping quarterly operating structure into short-horizon shock elasticities is capital-intensive and exposure changes only when financial reports update; it is falsified if high-rigidity firms do not exhibit larger same-direction post-shock relative returns than flexible peers.
factors.name: Operating Rigidity Shock Amplification

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s fading-sell-intensity signal likely mixed genuine adverse information with forced selling, explaining its incorrect out-of-sample direction. This child instead targets a slower and observable information-processing mechanism: newly reported earnings surprises should drift for several sessions when the initial industry-relative price response is small relative to the stock’s normal volatility. The edge can persist because investors and analyst models update heterogeneous earnings implications gradually, while sector-relative reaction filtering removes market-wide report-day moves; it is falsified if muted-response positive (negative) surprises do not subsequently outperform (underperform) over six sessions.
factors.name: Report Underreaction Elasticity Gap

factors.trading_idea: This child treats an earnings-anchor displacement as a heavy-tailed information state rather than automatically fading it: the realized negative sign in Parent B implies that salient post-event moves tend to continue when they are corroborated by industry information. It trades Parent A's peer lead-lag catch-up only when the lagging name has already moved in the same direction as its peers since the earnings anchor, indicating partial but incomplete assimilation rather than a contrarian overshoot. Balance-sheet resilience and improving cash conversion distinguish credible continuation-and-catch-up from a peer move that rationally excludes a financially fragile issuer.
factors.name: Tail Anchor Concordant Diffusion

factors.trading_idea: When several peers release earnings on the same day, limited investor attention, dealer balance sheet, and liquidity-provider capacity make immediate price discovery less complete for the harder-to-trade names. The child therefore trades the signed dual-surprise only when it occurs in an unusually concentrated sector reporting cluster, and emphasizes names whose initial signed response is muted despite elevated price impact. The mechanism is falsifiable: its return should concentrate in high peer-release-breadth days and high-impact names, while disappearing for isolated reports or liquid names; it persists because synchronized disclosure demand temporarily exceeds the capacity to process and hedge idiosyncratic information.
factors.name: Common-Shock Earnings Capacity Lag

factors.trading_idea: Liquidity shocks become more damaging when many names in the same sector simultaneously exhibit abnormal range and turnover, because sector ETFs, risk-parity deleveraging, and correlated liquidity provision transmit a common forced-flow shock. Within such episodes, stocks with the largest idiosyncratic downside displacement relative to their sector peers are likely oversold rather than uniquely informed, creating a short-horizon repair trade. The hypothesis is falsified if high-loading names continue to underperform after controlling for sector returns and contemporaneous fundamental-news proxies, which would imply that the synchronization reflects genuine common information rather than liquidity evaporation.
factors.name: Sector Liquidity Synchrony Overshoot

factors.trading_idea: Institutional liquidation is commonly split into relatively regular daily participation slices to reduce footprint. A sustained, regular sell-pressure sequence that abruptly fades while closes recover toward the top of their daily ranges indicates that the predictable supply schedule has likely completed and liquidity providers no longer need inventory compensation, creating a rebound over the next week. The effect should persist because the completion of a constrained execution program is not directly observable from daily bars and because passive liquidity suppliers unwind inventory gradually; it is falsified if regular sell-pressure fade with resilient closes does not outperform irregular or still-active selling.
factors.name: Regular Sell Program Completion Resilience

factors.trading_idea: Clusters of broad negative market-tail days proxy for periods when the marginal utility of consumption becomes highly nonlinear and investors reprice assets by their downside co-crash exposure. During these states, firms with both high conditional market-tail beta and weak cash-flow-funded balance-sheet buffers should underperform over the next week, while cash-buffered, low-tail-beta firms should attract defensive capital. The edge persists because tail dependence is estimated from infrequent joint-loss observations and balance-sheet resilience is disclosed only quarterly, making rapid arbitrage and precise hedging difficult; it is falsified if the conditional safety spread is no stronger after clustered market-tail events than during ordinary market states.
factors.name: Consumption-Tail Buffered Co-Crash Sort

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth shocks should price nonlinear co-crash exposure rather than ordinary market beta: investors require compensation for equities whose own extreme losses become materially more likely on aggregate crash days than on routine negative market days. The cash-flow yield and income-quality composite restricts this exposure to firms capable of surviving a systemic contraction, separating priced joint-tail risk from likely permanent distress or weak accounting. This edge should persist because portfolios cannot cheaply diversify losses that arrive jointly in marginal-utility states; falsifiably, high-score names should earn higher average forward returns and suffer disproportionately negative returns specifically on subsequent aggregate left-tail days, while the effect should be weaker on ordinary down-market days.
factors.name: Systemic Tail Coincidence Premium

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s useful component is the synchronized liquidity-drought state, but its cumulative impact-resolution branch is naturally slow because it mixes mature and newly initiated flow. This child conditions specifically on a fresh acceleration of signed abnormal-volume arrivals and trades only the under-reacted side of the flow-implied move; when dealers are simultaneously capacity constrained, a new directional cluster is less readily absorbed and should continue over the next several sessions. The hypothesis is falsifiable: conditional on systemic range-volume breadth, high fresh-arrival underreaction should have positive six-bar returns, while equally large but mature or already-paid flow should not. The edge can persist because public daily volume and range are only coarse proxies for latent execution demand and dealer inventory, whose gradual hedging and order-slicing are not instantaneously arbitraged away.
factors.name: Systemic Fresh Arrival Underreaction

factors.trading_idea: A downside gap rejected into a high-participation close is bullish only when sector-wide negative-volume arrivals indicate that the initial selling was a correlated liquidity shock rather than firm-specific information. The auction-inertia mechanism is used as a state variable: a previously positive response of close locations to lagged recovery impulses identifies names where replenishing demand has persisted across sessions. This interaction creates a six-day edge because synchronised forced selling supplies the overshoot, while phase-locked recovery flow distinguishes a durable inventory-transfer relay from an isolated dead-cat bounce.
factors.name: Forced-Sale Recovery Phase Relay

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s useful feature is conditional downside continuation, but this child replaces balance-sheet fragility with an endogenous-order-flow mechanism. A fresh idiosyncratic negative return is more likely to continue when it arrives after a short sequence of prior downside innovations, because forced selling, stop-loss execution, and dealer inventory reduction create self-exciting sell pressure rather than an isolated information shock. The edge should persist because arbitrageurs face uncertain cascade duration and adverse selection during the selling episode; it is falsified if equally large idiosyncratic losses have the same six-day forward return regardless of their pre-shock downside-excitation intensity.
factors.name: Idiosyncratic Downside Branching Pressure

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth risk implies that broad downside shocks are not linearly priced: stocks with high conditional beta specifically during market-tail days are disproportionately exposed to consumption-disaster states. After a fresh broad drawdown, constrained intermediaries and risk-controlled investors reduce those exposures over several days, so low tail-beta stocks should outperform high tail-beta stocks at the fixed six-bar horizon. This is falsified if, conditional on a negative market-stress episode, historical downside-tail beta does not negatively predict subsequent six-day cross-sectional returns; the effect can persist because state-contingent tail exposure is difficult to hedge cheaply and deleveraging is gradual rather than instantaneous.
factors.name: Consumption-Tail Beta De-Risking

factors.trading_idea: Analyst EPS revisions are more credible when management is simultaneously retiring shares rather than issuing equity: repurchases reveal that insiders are willing to deploy corporate capital at the prevailing valuation, while issuance weakens the informational content of optimistic consensus changes. The child therefore targets upward estimate revisions in net repurchasers and downward revisions in net issuers, a cross-channel credibility mechanism distinct from price-volume pressure. This is falsifiable: within revision quintiles, six-bar forward returns should rise monotonically with net repurchase intensity, and the revision-return relation should be materially weaker or reversed among net issuers. The edge can persist because analyst-revision processing and interpretation of reported financing decisions occur through separate investor channels, while issuance data is infrequent and costly for management to manipulate.
factors.name: Issuance-Validated Estimate Revision Drift

factors.trading_idea: Institutional metaorders are commonly executed in relatively regular daily participation slices to control footprint and benchmark slippage. When participation is persistently elevated yet unusually regular, and bars repeatedly close near their directional extreme, this identifies a likely uncompleted buyer or seller rather than a one-off liquidity shock; buy programs should continue to create positive six-day drift and sell programs negative drift. The edge persists because competing liquidity providers cannot observe the parent order's remaining quantity and face adverse-selection risk when front-running apparent informed flow; it is falsified if regular elevated participation has no additional forward-return association after conditioning on the direction of close-location imbalance.
factors.name: Clocklike Participation Terminal Imbalance

factors.trading_idea: Market-wide synchrony identifies common-risk episodes in which investors reassess balance-sheet susceptibility rather than firm-specific narratives. Within those episodes, an abnormal sector return-volume cascade marks where deleveraging and benchmark-driven reallocation are still propagating; resilient, cash-generative firms should attract relative demand while leveraged, weak-profitability firms remain the natural sources of liquidity. Neither parent alone distinguishes a broad quality rotation from a localized cascade nor identifies whether a cascade occurs during a systemic common-shock state, whereas their interaction isolates the cross-sectional flight-to-resilience during unfinished sector transmission.
factors.name: Systemic Cascade Quality Susceptibility

factors.trading_idea: Sector shocks often arrive in clustered directional bursts rather than as isolated events; repeated shocks create a persistent cross-excitation state in which liquid or attentive names incorporate the information first. The child measures each stock's cumulative response deficit relative to a leave-one-out sector benchmark and trades that deficit only while sector shock intensity remains elevated and the stock's own trading activity is subdued, indicating an attention/backlog mechanism rather than firm-specific news. The edge should persist because arbitrage capital and passive-flow transmission have finite capacity during clustered shocks; it is falsified if high-intensity, quiet underresponders do not subsequently converge toward their beta-implied sector path over six bars.
factors.name: Leave-One-Out Hawkes Backlog Assimilation

factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth risk implies that a sequence of unusually large common losses raises marginal utility and risk-manager demand for disaster protection disproportionately. When the trailing Hill tail-index estimate indicates a fatter-than-usual market left tail and recent market losses remain elevated, stocks with high conditional downside-market beta should continue to face deleveraging and hedging-related selling over the next six sessions; the factor therefore favors low-tail-loading stocks. The edge should persist because joint-tail exposure is difficult to hedge precisely, while institutional risk limits and volatility-targeting adjustments are implemented gradually rather than instantaneously. This is falsifiable: the defensive spread should be concentrated in fat-tail stress states and should be weak or absent during calm, thin-tailed market regimes.
factors.name: Hill Tail-State Downside Defense

factors.trading_idea: Institutional liquidation programs commonly divide trades into regularly spaced participation slices, whereas information-driven selling is less temporally regular and tends to retain price impact. This child identifies names with unusually regular volume-marked sell arrivals, then requires both a recent collapse in sell intensity and declining price damage per unit of normalized volume, consistent with completion of an absorbed mechanical program. The edge should persist because liquidity suppliers and arbitrageurs bear inventory and adverse-selection risk while the program is active, so they cannot reliably front-run the terminal rebound; it is falsified if cadence-conditioned completion has no incremental six-day return after controlling for recent return, turnover, and volatility.
factors.name: Cadenced Sell-Program Completion

factors.trading_idea: When many firms in a sector disclose results in the same few sessions, limited analyst and investor attention delays the assessment of which positive EPS surprises are supported by genuine cash realization. The child goes long firms with fresh positive, cash-credible surprises released during these sector disclosure clusters, where the fundamental confirmation should be incorporated over the following week rather than immediately. The effect can persist because processing statements and cash-flow quality is costly relative to reacting to the headline beat, while simultaneous peer releases compete for research capacity. It is falsified if, within sectors and clustered reporting periods, cash-credible positive surprises do not outperform cash-weaker positive surprises over the next six sessions.
factors.name: Congested Disclosure Cash Drift

factors.trading_idea: Repurchases are not uniformly good news: a buyback funded from operating cash flow by a cheaply valued firm can return surplus capital, while a debt-funded buyback at an expensive valuation can be a fragile attempt to support per-share metrics. Investors often react to the gross repurchase announcement or reported share-count reduction before disentangling funding source and valuation discipline. The trade should be rejected if debt-financed and cash-financed repurchases have indistinguishable subsequent cross-sectional returns after controlling for valuation and sector.
factors.name: Cash-Financed Buyback Value Release

factors.trading_idea: A forced-selling cascade should create a marked, self-exciting sequence of downside shocks, but the six-day opportunity is concentrated at the transition from high excitation to extinction rather than during the cascade itself. The child identifies names whose previously elevated volume-marked downside intensity is falling while the current bar shows high-volume intrabar absorption, indicating that latent demand is taking over from constrained sellers. The edge should persist because inventory transfer, margin-driven selling, and liquidity-provider replenishment resolve over several sessions and are difficult to arbitrage during stressed conditions; it is falsified if post-cascade extinction plus absorption does not outperform equally stressed names whose downside intensity remains elevated.
factors.name: Marked Cascade Extinction Absorption

factors.trading_idea: The hidden-order mechanism implies that low entropy in the joint price-volume path identifies structured trading activity and predicts a larger forthcoming move, but not its sign. A fresh earnings or revenue surprise supplies the missing directional information: buy positive-surprise names and sell negative-surprise names only when their recent daily return-volume transitions are unusually predictable. The hypothesis is falsified if post-report signed drift is no stronger in low-entropy names than in matched high-entropy surprise names.
factors.name: Entropy-Conditioned Earnings Impulse

factors.trading_idea: A large downside excursion that closes in the upper portion of its daily range can look like absorption, but if it still fails to regain the prior close, the recovery is more consistent with passive liquidity temporarily accommodating an informed sell program than with completed capitulation. Unusually high participation combined with low range-per-participation identifies sessions in which that inventory transfer can occur without immediate price impact, leaving residual supply to pressure prices over the following six days. This hypothesis is falsified if these high-volume, low-impact failed recoveries do not underperform comparable downside-recovery sessions; the effect can persist because daily bars reveal neither the identity nor the remaining size of the seller, while shorting immediately entails borrow, timing, and adverse-selection risk.
factors.name: Failed Recovery Inventory Transfer

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s useful component is the reversal of isolated, high-participation dislocations, but its phase-area construction is complex and appears insufficiently distinct from the existing book. This child instead identifies an asymmetric downside order-flow cascade whose exponentially decayed intensity is still elevated but has begun to extinguish relative to sector peers; in fundamentally stronger firms, such selling is more likely temporary inventory transfer or forced liquidation than adverse private information. The hypothesis is falsifiable: high-quality names with idiosyncratic, decelerating downside excitation should outperform over the next six bars, while the effect should weaken or reverse for low-quality names and for cascades whose intensity continues accelerating. The edge can persist because liquidity providers and arbitrageurs face capital, inventory, and event-risk constraints during a sell cascade and only replenish risk after its extinction becomes observable.
factors.name: Quality-Gated Idiosyncratic Sell-Cascade Release

factors.trading_idea: A favorable revenue headline can be over-extrapolated when it arrives in a financially fragile firm whose unusually quiet price path has concealed left-tail refinancing and working-capital risk. The child fades headline news only when the cash-conversion update contradicts it and the equity has low sector-relative downside/range volatility despite weak coverage, leverage, and short-term funding exposure. This interaction carries edge neither parent has alone because cash-cycle disagreement is most consequential when investors are simultaneously underpricing the firm's latent tail state, especially following broad downside demand for balance-sheet safety.
factors.name: Quiet-Tail Cash-Cycle Repricing

factors.trading_idea: A stale-consensus earnings surprise becomes more informative when a broad industry drawdown forces investors to discriminate rapidly between firms that can absorb funding and demand shocks and firms that cannot. During peer stress, positive surprises from liquid, cash-generative firms signal resilient earnings capacity and attract defensive rotation, while negative surprises from fragile firms reveal that the industry shock is likely to propagate through financing constraints. Neither parent alone identifies this news-by-stress transmission channel: the surprise lacks a systemic allocation state, while balance-sheet quality lacks a fresh catalyst that reveals which firms are actually diverging.
factors.name: Stressed Stale-Surprise Balance-Sheet Relay

factors.trading_idea: A clustered analyst revision is most likely to generate near-term drift when it occurs inside an accelerating industry contagion regime but has not yet induced abnormal own-name participation. The revision cluster supplies fundamental directional information, while low own volume distinguishes an unfilled relay from Parent B's completed, inventory-heavy contagion state; muted relative price response further identifies names where the information has not been assimilated. Neither parent alone separates fundamental peer confirmation from the phase of market-flow transmission, whereas their interaction targets the early, under-participated leg before forced-flow completion creates reversal risk.
factors.name: Unsaturated Revision Contagion Relay

factors.trading_idea: When several industry peers release directionally similar earnings surprises in close succession, investor attention and analyst-processing capacity are congested; a firm's own surprise can therefore be only partially incorporated even if trading activity is elevated. The child buys positive and shorts negative earnings surprises whose immediate price response is unusually muted, but only when prior peer reports establish a concordant information-arrival cluster. This is falsifiable: conditional on surprise sign, muted-response firms with concordant recent industry-report intensity should have larger 6-bar abnormal returns than equally muted isolated reports; the edge can persist because clustered disclosure processing is costly and asynchronous across investors rather than a mechanically arbitrageable price pattern.
factors.name: Industry Report-Congestion Surprise Drift

factors.trading_idea: An EPS beat accompanied by a revenue miss is a disagreement between short-run reported profitability and the sales trajectory analysts use to forecast durable earnings. The parent’s negative realized sign suggests that cash validation and stale-consensus filters did not identify underreaction; instead, the market initially gives too much weight to the EPS headline and subsequently incorporates lower revenue and margin assumptions through analyst revisions. This effect can persist for roughly six bars because rebuilding forward estimates after a mixed release is slower than trading the immediately salient EPS surprise, while the conditional revenue shortfall is less easily arbitraged than a plain earnings-surprise signal. It is falsified if large positive EPS surprises with contemporaneous revenue misses do not underperform other earnings reporters over the next six daily bars.
factors.name: Margin-Only Beat Revision Correction

factors.trading_idea: Fear episodes are characterized by nonlinear co-crashes rather than ordinary correlation: stocks that have recently become much more dependent on broad-universe downside-tail days are likely being repriced as systemic-risk proxies. If a current market-wide downside shock occurs, names with elevated conditional tail dependence but relatively muted same-day declines should subsequently underperform as hedgers and risk-parity allocators complete de-risking. The effect should disappear if tail-dependence innovations do not predict subsequent relative returns after controlling for ordinary volatility and beta; the opposite side of the trade is supplied by investors who infer risk from conventional covariance estimates that understate crash-state linkage.
factors.name: Tail-Dependence Fear Transmission Gap

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s positive realized IC suggests that clustered downside range shocks are more often a temporary liquidity-vacuum and forced-sale state than a continuing default-risk cascade. This child therefore identifies the transition from elevated downside excitation to cooling excitation: recent selling pressure remains unusually high, but fast event intensity has fallen below its slower state, consistent with marginal sellers being exhausted and liquidity providers beginning to replenish depth. The edge should persist because forced liquidations and dealer inventory rebalancing unwind over several daily bars; it is falsified if positive forward returns do not concentrate in cooling states, or if equally excited but still-accelerating clusters rebound just as strongly.
factors.name: Downside Cluster Cooling Liquidity Repair (jitter)

factors.trading_idea: Quarterly fundamental news is most informative when an opening-auction dislocation initially moves against that news but continuous trading rejects the gap in the news-consistent direction. High abnormal turnover indicates that investors are paying attention, while a still-muted net close-to-prior-close move indicates that the fundamental repricing is not yet complete. Unlike Parent A, the child does not fade every failed gap; unlike Parent B, it requires a microstructural correction that identifies which attention events are resolving a wrong-way auction price rather than merely generating noisy event turnover.
factors.name: Surprise-Aligned Auction Recovery Lag

factors.trading_idea: Analyst estimate changes arriving simultaneously across many firms in a sector create an attention-capacity bottleneck: investors can recognize the sector-level information but underprocess the issuer-specific component of each revision. The signal isolates a firm's revision from its leave-one-out sector revision, and emphasizes it when peer revision breadth is high and the stock has not yet moved in the residual revision's direction. The edge should persist because allocating analyst and portfolio-manager attention across a clustered disclosure/revision cycle is costly, while arbitrageurs must distinguish common sector information from slower-to-verify firm-specific information. Falsifiably, positive residual revisions during high sector revision breadth should outperform negative residual revisions over the next six sessions, particularly when their initial two-day price response is muted.
factors.name: Sector Revision Congestion Residual Drift

factors.trading_idea: A fresh earnings surprise at one firm conveys information about demand, costs, and competitive conditions for close industry peers, but peer prices incorporate this read-through with a short delay. The child goes long firms that have under-reacted to a positive, price-confirmed peer surprise and short firms that have under-reacted to a negative one, with stronger exposure when the candidate's trading activity indicates lower attention. The edge should persist because mapping issuer-specific earnings news into heterogeneous peer exposures requires costly fundamental interpretation, while the hypothesis is falsified if the industry-relative catch-up spread is absent over the next six bars after conditioning on fresh peer surprises.
factors.name: Peer Earnings Read-Through Lag

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s negative realized IC implies that high downside-semibeta stocks do not continue to suffer after a fear burst; instead, they rebound once broad downside volatility begins to cool, because the initial volatility-targeting liquidation has already occurred. This child identifies that transition from elevated fear to stabilization and buys high-semibeta firms with credible balance-sheet capacity, which are more likely to survive the shock and receive returning risk appetite rather than face genuine solvency-driven selling. The effect should persist because systematic de-risking is mechanical and immediate while risk re-allocation, discretionary dip-buying, and short covering occur more gradually over the following week. It is falsified if high-semibeta, financially resilient names fail to outperform sector peers specifically after downside-volatility bursts begin cooling, or if the same spread is equally strong without a preceding fear shock.
factors.name: Cooling-Fear Quality Semibeta Rebound

factors.trading_idea: The parent’s negative out-of-sample sign suggests that daily signed abnormal-volume marks with muted impact are more often temporary liquidity-demand shocks than informed unfinished metaorders. This child explicitly restricts the signal to bars closing near the middle of their intrabar range, where two-sided liquidity replenishment has absorbed directional pressure rather than validating a news-driven close at an extreme; concentrated sell pressure should subsequently rebound and concentrated buy pressure should fade. The edge can persist because daily-bar investors cannot directly observe latent dealer inventory and liquidity-provider replenishment, while arbitrageurs face inventory and execution risk in trading short-lived dislocations. Falsifiably, reversal should be strongest after high abnormal-volume pressure with low realized impact and midrange closes, and should disappear or reverse for equally high-volume bars closing near their directional extremes.
factors.name: Midrange Absorption Pressure Reversal

factors.trading_idea: The parent's negative realized IC implies that peer-concordant tail moves are more often persistent common bad-state reallocations than temporary earnings-anchor overshoots. Heavy-tailed consumption-growth risk makes downside co-crashes especially costly for constrained investors; stocks with historically high conditional downside dependence on the market and fragile balance sheets face continuing deleveraging after a fresh common-tail loss. This is falsifiable: conditional on a joint stock-market left-tail day, high tail-dependence/high-fragility names should underperform over the next six sessions, while this ordering should disappear outside common-tail days. The edge can persist because balance-sheet-constrained holders and risk-budgeted intermediaries cannot instantly restore exposure during aggregate tail states.
factors.name: Common-Tail Fragility Deleveraging Drift

factors.trading_idea: Downside-tail beta is most economically meaningful when a firm's ability to fund itself through a consumption or market-tail shock depends on the credibility of reported growth. Cash-backed estimate revisions validate the ability of high-tail-exposure firms to service financing needs and allow their disaster-risk premium to be earned, whereas receivable-funded revisions identify firms whose apparent growth and tail-risk compensation are both likely overstated. The interaction therefore distinguishes priced disaster exposure from an impending working-capital repricing, a separation neither tail beta nor collection quality makes alone.
factors.name: Calm Tail Collection Convexity

factors.trading_idea: Sequential, concordant revisions to both revenue and EPS estimates reveal an analyst-information cascade rather than a mechanical one-line forecast adjustment. This should be most slowly incorporated for R&D-intensive firms, where the mapping from current operating news to long-run cash flows is difficult to value and costly for arbitrageurs to verify. The hypothesis is falsified if aligned estimate-revision trends do not predict returns more strongly among high-R&D-intensity firms, or if disagreement between revenue and EPS revision directions has equal predictive power.
factors.name: R&D Cross-Channel Revision Persistence

factors.trading_idea: Persistent institutional accumulation or distribution produces a low-frequency return component rather than a sequence dominated by idiosyncratic daily reversals. The child isolates that component with a trailing Fourier energy ratio and only expresses its signed direction when signed volume participation agrees, targeting gradual information diffusion that should persist through the fixed six-bar horizon. The edge should survive simple momentum arbitrage because the conditioning distinguishes durable, flow-backed trends from noisy trends whose apparent momentum is primarily high-frequency variance; this is falsifiable if spectral concentration and flow alignment do not materially improve six-day IC versus the same trailing trend alone.
factors.name: Spectral Flow-Coherence Continuation

factors.trading_idea: A directional, high-participation range shock should transmit into subsequent returns when it is unusually severe for one stock but not synchronized with its sector. Such localized shocks indicate name-specific liquidity depletion and inventory imbalances that cannot be cheaply hedged through sector baskets, so liquidity providers pass the residual pressure into prices over subsequent days. This is falsifiable: conditional on persistent signed participation, forward returns should be strongest after positive idiosyncratic liquidity shocks with low stock-sector volatility correlation, and should disappear or weaken during synchronized sector-wide shocks. The edge can persist because daily-bar execution pressure and dealer inventory transfer are resolved more slowly than the initial price move.
factors.name: Localized Liquidity Shock Transmission

factors.trading_idea: Negative idiosyncratic return innovations are not symmetric with positive innovations: they raise risk limits, margin demand, and hedging activity, causing volatility and sell pressure to persist beyond the initial shock. The signal identifies names whose recent downside semivariance is unusually concentrated relative to their own trailing baseline, and takes the opposite side because these names should underperform over the next six sessions while the selling cascade remains active. The edge should persist because forced deleveraging and volatility-targeting adjustment occur gradually across institutional portfolios rather than being instantly arbitraged away. It is falsified if high downside-cluster intensity does not predict relatively weaker six-bar returns after normalizing each stock by its own volatility history.
factors.name: Downside Innovation Persistence Spread

factors.trading_idea: Analysts often revise revenue and EPS forecasts through different information channels: a positive EPS revision that is large relative to the accompanying revenue revision implies an improving expected margin, pricing, or cost outlook rather than merely stronger nominal demand. Margin-information is harder for investors to verify immediately and is incorporated gradually as subsequent disclosures validate the operational improvement, while portfolio managers commonly react first to headline sales revisions. The edge should therefore persist because the signal isolates a forecast-composition shock rather than generic estimate momentum; it is falsified if high-wedge firms do not subsequently exhibit stronger realized profitability or do not outperform over the next six bars.
factors.name: Consensus Margin Revision Wedge

factors.trading_idea: Broad sector selling is more likely mechanical when abnormal negative-volume-event breadth first rises and then decelerates, consistent with redemption or deleveraging demand being completed rather than fresh information continuing to arrive. A stock that remains a large residual laggard through that completion phase but closes high in its daily range on elevated volume is showing latent demand absorbing the remaining supply, so it should repair over the next six bars. The edge should persist because passive-flow completion and liquidity-provider inventory replenishment are gradual, whereas arbitrageurs cannot directly observe the underlying redemption schedule. Falsifiably, the signal should lose or reverse its predictive power when sector sell breadth is still accelerating or when the candidate closes near its intraday low, conditions associated with continuing information-driven selling.
factors.name: Sector Flow Deceleration Absorption

factors.trading_idea: Industry earnings surprises are noisy but timely observations of an underlying demand shock whose distribution is heavy-tailed: a large negative consumption-demand realization is disproportionately damaging to firms with more leveraged equity claims, while a positive realization has the opposite effect. The child retains the parent’s peer-information channel but removes the fragile price-confirmation, attention, and catch-up branches; it instead expresses the economically motivated cross-sectional heterogeneity in balance-sheet convexity. The edge should persist because mapping an infrequent peer report into firm-specific tail exposure requires fundamental interpretation of capital structure, and is falsified if the return spread between highly and weakly levered firms is absent over the next six bars following signed peer-surprise impulses.
factors.name: Levered Tail-Demand Read-Through
